sync_enum_types(
    context: Any, revision: str | tuple[str, ...], directives: list[MigrationScript]
) -> None

Append :class:ReplaceEnumOp for every enum whose members changed.

An alembic revision --autogenerate hook. Reads the enum members the database currently enforces, compares them with the metadata, and emits a replacement for each difference — the gap that makes adding a member to a Python enum a silent no-op today.

Detection is best-effort by design: an enum the backend cannot report on is skipped rather than diffed against a guess, because emitting a wrong replace_enum would drop values from live rows. PostgreSQL is read from pg_enum; SQLite from the generated CHECK constraint, and only when it still has the generated shape.

A renamed type is detected too, and emitted as :class:RenameEnumTypeOp ahead of any replacement — the case :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.enums.enum_type_name creates for a class ending in Enum, whose type used to be <name>_enum_enum. On PostgreSQL the declared type is missing and every column it types is still typed by one other existing enum that the metadata no longer declares; on SQLite the column's enum CHECK carries a name that differs from the declared one only where the enum name sits.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default context Any

Alembic's MigrationContext.

required revision str | tuple[str, ...]

The revision being generated.

required directives list[MigrationScript]

The scripts to amend.

required Source code in tempest_fastapi_sdk/db/enum_migrations.py 
def sync_enum_types(
    context: Any,
    revision: str | tuple[str, ...],
    directives: list[MigrationScript],
) -> None:
    """Append :class:`ReplaceEnumOp` for every enum whose members changed.

    An ``alembic revision --autogenerate`` hook. Reads the enum members
    the database currently enforces, compares them with the metadata,
    and emits a replacement for each difference — the gap that makes
    adding a member to a Python enum a silent no-op today.

    Detection is best-effort **by design**: an enum the backend cannot
    report on is skipped rather than diffed against a guess, because
    emitting a wrong ``replace_enum`` would drop values from live rows.
    PostgreSQL is read from ``pg_enum``; SQLite from the generated
    ``CHECK`` constraint, and only when it still has the generated shape.

    A **renamed** type is detected too, and emitted as
    :class:`RenameEnumTypeOp` ahead of any replacement — the case
    :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.enums.enum_type_name` creates for a
    class ending in ``Enum``, whose type used to be
    ``<name>_enum_enum``. On PostgreSQL the declared type is missing and
    every column it types is still typed by one other existing enum that
    the metadata no longer declares; on SQLite the column's enum
    ``CHECK`` carries a name that differs from the declared one only
    where the enum name sits.

    Args:
        context (Any): Alembic's ``MigrationContext``.
        revision (str | tuple[str, ...]): The revision being generated.
        directives (list[MigrationScript]): The scripts to amend.
    """
    if not directives:
        return
    script = directives[0]
    if script.upgrade_ops is None:
        return
    connection = context.connection
    if connection is None:
        return

    metadata = context.opts.get("target_metadata")
    if metadata is None:
        return

    declared = _declared_enum_types(metadata)
    existing = _existing_enum_types(connection, declared)
    renamed = _renamed_enum_types(
        connection, declared, existing, _declared_check_names(metadata)
    )

    for name, wanted in declared.items():
        old_name = renamed.get(name)
        current = existing.get(name)
        if old_name is not None:
            _drop_enum_type_swaps(script.upgrade_ops.ops, {old_name, name})
            if script.downgrade_ops is not None:
                _drop_enum_type_swaps(script.downgrade_ops.ops, {old_name, name})
            _append_with_reverse(
                script,
                RenameEnumTypeOp(old_name, name, columns=wanted.columns),
            )
            current = current or existing.get(old_name)
        if current is None or current.values == wanted.values:
            continue
        _append_with_reverse(
            script,
            ReplaceEnumOp(
                wanted.name,
                new_values=wanted.values,
                old_values=current.values,
                columns=wanted.columns,
            ),
        )

Build the include_object filter that hides enum CHECK drift.

Alembic's CHECK comparison reads the constraint from the database but drops it from the metadata side: it collects metadata CHECKs through all_table_check_constraints, which skips the ones a column's type attaches (SQLAlchemy marks them _type_bound). On SQLite — where an Enum column is a VARCHAR plus a CHECK — the database therefore always shows one constraint the metadata does not, and alembic check fails on a clean upgrade head proposing remove_constraint for ck_<table>_<enum>.

A reflected CHECK whose name matches a type-bound CHECK declared in metadata on the same table is not drift: the column type recreates it. Returning False skips it; every other object is left to Alembic. The table is part of the key because two tables may carry a check of the same name under a project's own naming convention, and a match on the name alone would hide one table's drift behind the other's.

A reflected enum-shaped CHECK (<column> IN (...)) on a column the metadata types with a check-carrying enum is hidden too, whatever its name. Its name can legitimately differ from the declared one — after :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.enums.enum_type_name stopped doubling the _enum suffix, or in a table an older SDK rebuilt — and the name-only match then proposed remove_constraint for the check that enforces the column. Renames and member changes are :func:sync_enum_types' job, which reads the same check.

Pass it as include_object in context.configure; :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.alembic_env.run_alembic_env does.

def type_bound_check_include_object(
    metadata: sa.MetaData | Sequence[sa.MetaData] | None,
) -> Callable[[Any, str | None, str, bool, Any], bool]:
    """Build the ``include_object`` filter that hides enum ``CHECK`` drift.

    Alembic's CHECK comparison reads the constraint from the database but
    drops it from the metadata side: it collects metadata CHECKs through
    ``all_table_check_constraints``, which skips the ones a column's type
    attaches (SQLAlchemy marks them ``_type_bound``). On SQLite — where an
    ``Enum`` column is a ``VARCHAR`` plus a ``CHECK`` — the database
    therefore always shows one constraint the metadata does not, and
    ``alembic check`` fails on a clean ``upgrade head`` proposing
    ``remove_constraint`` for ``ck_<table>_<enum>``.

    A reflected ``CHECK`` whose name matches a type-bound CHECK declared in
    ``metadata`` **on the same table** is not drift: the column type
    recreates it. Returning ``False`` skips it; every other object is left
    to Alembic. The table is part of the key because two tables may carry a
    check of the same name under a project's own naming convention, and a
    match on the name alone would hide one table's drift behind the
    other's.

    A reflected enum-shaped ``CHECK`` (``<column> IN (...)``) on a column
    the metadata types with a check-carrying enum is hidden too, whatever
    its name. Its name can legitimately differ from the declared one —
    after :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.enums.enum_type_name` stopped
    doubling the ``_enum`` suffix, or in a table an older SDK rebuilt —
    and the name-only match then proposed ``remove_constraint`` for the
    check that enforces the column. Renames and member changes are
    :func:`sync_enum_types`' job, which reads the same check.

    Pass it as ``include_object`` in ``context.configure``;
    :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.alembic_env.run_alembic_env` does.

    Args:
        metadata (sa.MetaData | Sequence[sa.MetaData] | None): The
            autogenerate target metadata, or a sequence of metadatas.

    Returns:
        Callable[[Any, str | None, str, bool, Any], bool]: The
        ``include_object`` callback Alembic expects.
    """
    names = _type_bound_check_names(metadata)
    columns = (
        {(ref.table, ref.column) for ref in _declared_check_names(metadata)}
        if metadata is not None
        else set()
    )

    def include_object(
        object_: Any,
        name: str | None,
        type_: str,
        reflected: bool,
        compare_to: Any,
    ) -> bool:
        """Keep every object except a table's own type-bound enum check.

        Args:
            object_ (Any): The object Alembic is considering — for a
                ``check_constraint`` it is the ``CheckConstraint``, whose
                ``table`` names the scope.
            name (str | None): The object's name, as Alembic reports it.
            type_ (str): The object kind (``"check_constraint"``, ...).
            reflected (bool): Whether the object came from the database.
            compare_to (Any): The metadata counterpart, when there is one.

        Returns:
            bool: ``False`` to hide a reflected check that belongs to the
            same table and name as a declared type-bound check, or that
            is the enum check of a declared enum column; ``True``
            otherwise.
        """
        if type_ != "check_constraint" or not reflected:
            return True
        table = getattr(object_, "table", None)
        table_name = getattr(table, "name", None)
        if (table_name, name) in names:
            return False
        sqltext = getattr(object_, "sqltext", None)
        column = _check_column(str(sqltext)) if sqltext is not None else None
        return (table_name, column) not in columns

    return include_object

def parse_accept_language(header: str | None) -> list[str]:
    """Parse an ``Accept-Language`` header into locales by descending ``q``.

    Args:
        header (str | None): The raw header value (e.g.
            ``"pt-BR,pt;q=0.9,en;q=0.8"``). ``None`` yields an empty list.

    Returns:
        list[str]: Locale tags ordered from most to least preferred,
        with the quality values stripped (e.g.
        ``["pt-BR", "pt", "en"]``).

    Notes:
        The header index is the sort tiebreaker, so tags sharing a quality
        value keep the order the client sent them in.
    """
    if not header:
        return []
    parsed: list[tuple[float, int, str]] = []
    for index, part in enumerate(header.split(",")):
        token = part.strip()
        if not token:
            continue
        tag, _, params = token.partition(";")
        tag = tag.strip()
        if not tag or tag == "*":
            continue
        quality = 1.0
        params = params.strip()
        if params.startswith("q="):
            try:
                quality = float(params[2:])
            except ValueError:
                quality = 1.0
        parsed.append((quality, index, tag))
    parsed.sort(key=lambda item: (-item[0], item[1]))
    return [tag for _, _, tag in parsed]

def make_flag_dependency(
    flags: FeatureFlags,
    name: str,
    *,
    enabled: bool = True,
    status_code: int = 404,
    detail: str = "Feature not available",
    code: str = "FEATURE_DISABLED",
) -> Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]:
    """Build a dependency that allows a route only when a flag matches.

    Mount it via ``Depends`` (or in a router's ``dependencies=[...]``)
    to gate an endpoint behind a flag. When the flag's state differs
    from ``enabled``, the dependency raises an :class:`AppException`
    rendered through the SDK envelope — ``404`` by default so a disabled
    feature simply looks absent.

    Args:
        flags (FeatureFlags): The feature-flag service to query.
        name (str): The flag name to check.
        enabled (bool): The flag state the route requires. ``True``
            (default) allows the route when the flag is on; ``False``
            allows it only when the flag is off (e.g. a deprecation
            kill-switch).
        status_code (int): Status code raised when the gate fails.
            Defaults to ``404`` (hide the feature); use ``403`` to
            signal it exists but is forbidden.
        detail (str): Message for the error envelope.
        code (str): Machine-readable error code for the envelope.

    Returns:
        Callable[[], Awaitable[None]]: An async FastAPI dependency.
    """

    async def _dependency() -> None:
        if await flags.is_enabled(name) != enabled:
            raise AppException(detail, code=code, status_code=status_code)

    return _dependency

def make_push_router(
    *,
    service_factory: Callable[[AsyncSession], DeviceService[Any]],
    session_factory: Callable[..., AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]],
    current_user_id: Callable[..., Any],
    prefix: str = "/api/push",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    vapid_public_key: str | Callable[[], str] | None = None,
    transfer_ownership: bool = False,
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter:
    """Build a router with ``POST /register`` and ``POST /unregister``.

    * ``POST {prefix}/register`` -> ``service.register`` (idempotent by
      token). A browser posts ``platform="web"`` with the endpoint and the
      two key fields; a mobile app posts ``platform="ios"`` / ``"android"``
      with its FCM registration token.
    * ``POST {prefix}/unregister`` -> ``service.unregister`` (delete by
      token, scoped to the authenticated user; no-op when absent or owned
      by another account).
    * ``GET {prefix}/vapid-public-key`` -> the key the browser subscribes
      with, mounted only when ``vapid_public_key`` is given.

    Both write endpoints require authentication via ``current_user_id``.

    Args:
        service_factory (Callable[[AsyncSession], DeviceService]): Builds a
            request-scoped service from the yielded session.
        session_factory (Callable[..., AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]]): Yields
            a request-scoped DB session (the project's ``get_session``).
        current_user_id (Callable[..., Any]): FastAPI dependency resolving
            the authenticated user's :class:`~uuid.UUID`.
        prefix (str): URL prefix. Defaults to ``"/api/push"``.
        tags (list[str] | None): OpenAPI tags. Defaults to ``["push"]``.
        vapid_public_key (str | Callable[[], str] | None): When set, mount
            the public ``GET {prefix}/vapid-public-key`` returning
            ``{"public_key": ...}``, so the key is not baked into the
            frontend build. Accepts a string or a zero-arg callable
            (resolved per request). ``None`` omits the route — the right
            choice for a mobile-only service.
        transfer_ownership (bool): Let ``POST {prefix}/register`` move
            a token registered to another account to the caller. Off by
            default (#632): the stored row is left untouched and the
            caller gets the same answer as a new registration. Turn on only
            where moving devices between accounts is a real case; the
            service override must then accept ``transfer_ownership=``.
        docs_locale (str | None): Language of the OpenAPI ``summary``
            and ``description`` text — ``"en-US"`` or ``"pt-BR"``.
            ``None`` (default) reads ``API_DOCS_LOCALE`` through
            :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings`,
            whose default is ``"en-US"``.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: Ready to mount with ``app.include_router``.
    """
    route_docs: RouteDocs = RouteDocs(docs_locale)
    router = APIRouter(prefix=prefix, tags=list(tags or ["push"]))

    if vapid_public_key is not None:

        @router.get(
            "/vapid-public-key",
            summary=route_docs.summary("push.get_vapid_public_key"),
            description=route_docs.description("push.get_vapid_public_key"),
            status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
        )
        async def get_vapid_public_key() -> dict[str, str]:
            """Return the VAPID public key the browser subscribes with.

            Public and unauthenticated. Answers ``""`` when the key is
            unset, which lets the frontend hide the opt-in instead of
            failing.

            Returns:
                dict[str, str]: ``{"public_key": <url-safe base64 or "">}``.
            """
            key = vapid_public_key() if callable(vapid_public_key) else vapid_public_key
            return {"public_key": key or ""}

    _session = session_provider_for(session_factory)

    def _service(session: AsyncSession = Depends(_session)) -> DeviceService[Any]:
        return service_factory(session)

    @router.post(
        "/register",
        summary=route_docs.summary("push.register"),
        description=route_docs.description("push.register"),
        status_code=status.HTTP_201_CREATED,
    )
    async def register(
        registration: DeviceRegistrationSchema,
        user_id: UUID = Depends(current_user_id),
        service: DeviceService[Any] = Depends(_service),
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Persist the device that will receive notifications.

        Args:
            registration (DeviceRegistrationSchema): Token, platform and
                the web encryption material when applicable.
            user_id (UUID): The authenticated user (FK owner).
            service (DeviceService): Request-scoped service.

        Returns:
            dict[str, str]: ``{"status": "registered"}``.
        """
        if transfer_ownership:
            await service.register(user_id, registration, transfer_ownership=True)
        else:
            await service.register(user_id, registration)
        return {"status": "registered"}

    @router.post(
        "/unregister",
        summary=route_docs.summary("push.unregister"),
        description=route_docs.description("push.unregister"),
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
    )
    async def unregister(
        registration: DeviceRegistrationSchema,
        user_id: UUID = Depends(current_user_id),
        service: DeviceService[Any] = Depends(_service),
    ) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Remove the caller's own device (idempotent).

        The delete is scoped to ``user_id``: a token registered to another
        account is left in place and the answer is the same ``200`` as for
        an unknown token, so the route never reveals who owns a token. A
        ``DeviceService`` subclass whose ``unregister`` override predates
        the ``user_id`` keyword still gets the scoping — the router checks
        ownership through ``list_for_user`` and calls the override only for
        the caller's own device, instead of failing with ``TypeError``.

        Args:
            registration (DeviceRegistrationSchema): The device to drop;
                only its ``token`` is used.
            user_id (UUID): The authenticated user; only their devices can
                be removed.
            service (DeviceService): Request-scoped service.

        Returns:
            dict[str, str]: ``{"status": "unregistered"}``.
        """
        token = registration.token
        if accepts_keyword(service.unregister, "user_id"):
            await service.unregister(token, user_id=user_id)
        elif any(row.token == token for row in await service.list_for_user(user_id)):
            await service.unregister(token)
        return {"status": "unregistered"}

    return router

def build_pagination_link_header(
    base_url: str,
    *,
    page: int,
    page_size: int,
    pages: int,
    extra_params: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    page_param: str = "page",
    size_param: str = "page_size",
) -> str:
    """Build a ``Link`` header for offset-based pagination.

    Includes the ``first`` / ``prev`` / ``next`` / ``last`` rel values
    expected by GitHub-style clients. ``prev`` / ``next`` are omitted
    when they don't exist (first / last page).

    Args:
        base_url (str): Absolute or relative URL of the collection
            endpoint (e.g. ``"https://api.example.com/api/users"`` or
            ``"/api/users"``). Existing query parameters are preserved.
        page (int): Current page number (1-based).
        page_size (int): Page size. Field name matches
            :class:`BasePaginationFilterSchema.page_size` and the
            ``BaseRepository.paginate`` keyword argument.
        pages (int): Total number of pages.
        extra_params (dict[str, str] | None): Extra query parameters
            that must be preserved on every link (filters, sort,
            etc.). Existing values on ``base_url`` win.
        page_param (str): Query parameter name for the page index.
            Defaults to ``"page"``.
        size_param (str): Query parameter name for the page size.
            Defaults to ``"page_size"``.

    Returns:
        str: A ``Link`` header value ready to assign to
        ``response.headers["Link"]``. Empty string when there's
        nothing to link to (single page, ``pages <= 0``).
    """
    if pages <= 0:
        return ""

    parsed = urlparse(base_url)
    existing_params: dict[str, str] = {}
    if parsed.query:
        for pair in parsed.query.split("&"):
            if "=" in pair:
                key, value = pair.split("=", 1)
                existing_params[key] = value
            else:
                existing_params[pair] = ""

    base_params: dict[str, str] = {**(extra_params or {}), **existing_params}

    def _url_for(target_page: int) -> str:
        params = {
            **base_params,
            page_param: str(target_page),
            size_param: str(page_size),
        }
        query = urlencode(params, doseq=True)
        return urlunparse(
            (
                parsed.scheme,
                parsed.netloc,
                parsed.path,
                parsed.params,
                query,
                parsed.fragment,
            ),
        )

    parts: list[str] = []
    if page > 1:
        parts.append(f'<{_url_for(1)}>; rel="first"')
        parts.append(f'<{_url_for(page - 1)}>; rel="prev"')
    if page < pages:
        parts.append(f'<{_url_for(page + 1)}>; rel="next"')
        parts.append(f'<{_url_for(pages)}>; rel="last"')

    return ", ".join(parts)

def decode_cursor(cursor: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Decode a cursor previously produced by :func:`encode_cursor`.

    Args:
        cursor (str): The opaque cursor string.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Any]: The decoded payload.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``cursor`` is not valid base64 or doesn't
            decode to a JSON object.
    """
    padding = "=" * (-len(cursor) % 4)
    try:
        raw = base64.urlsafe_b64decode(cursor + padding)
        payload = json.loads(raw)
    except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
        raise ValueError("Invalid cursor") from exc
    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        raise ValueError("Invalid cursor payload")
    return payload

def encode_cursor(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """Serialize a cursor payload to an opaque base64-url-safe string.

    Args:
        payload (dict[str, Any]): The cursor state to encode.
            Typically ``{"id": <uuid>, "value": <sort-key-value>}``.

    Returns:
        str: A URL-safe base64 string without padding.
    """
    raw = json.dumps(payload, default=str, separators=(",", ":")).encode()
    return base64.urlsafe_b64encode(raw).rstrip(b"=").decode("ascii")

def make_session_dependency(
    *,
    required: bool = True,
    session_auth: SessionAuth | SessionAuthFactory | None = None,
    on_missing: MissingSessionHandler | None = None,
) -> Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Session | None]]:
    """Build a FastAPI dependency that returns the resolved session.

    Two ways to find the session:

    * **Without** ``session_auth`` the dependency reads
      ``request.state.session``, which :class:`SessionMiddleware`
      populates. Mount the middleware BEFORE you use the dependency, or
      it always sees no session.
    * **With** ``session_auth`` the dependency reads the cookie and
      resolves it itself (sliding the TTL like the middleware does), so
      no middleware is needed. Only the routes that declare the
      dependency pay for the lookup, and a streaming route elsewhere in
      the app is not wrapped by a ``BaseHTTPMiddleware``. When the
      middleware did run for the request, its result is reused instead
      of resolving twice.

    ``session_auth`` may also be a :data:`SessionAuthFactory` — a callable
    taking the request — for a service whose ``SessionAuth`` only exists
    once settings are read. The dependency is then declarable at module
    level (``AdminDep = Annotated[Session, Depends(...)]``) before any
    ``SessionAuth`` is built, and the factory runs per request, only when
    the middleware left no session. Two apps in one process — the shape
    of tests that clear a settings cache — each resolve against their own.

    With ``required=True`` (the default) the dependency is typed as
    returning ``Session``, not ``Session | None``: it raises instead of
    returning ``None``, so a consumer needs no ``if`` to narrow the type.

    Args:
        required (bool): When ``True`` (default), a missing session
            raises — :class:`UnauthorizedException` (``401``) unless
            ``on_missing`` says otherwise. When ``False``, the
            dependency returns ``None`` and the handler decides what to
            do (typical for endpoints that work both anonymously and
            authenticated).
        session_auth (SessionAuth | SessionAuthFactory | None): Resolve
            the cookie directly with this service, or with the one the
            factory returns for the request, instead of relying on the
            middleware.
        on_missing (MissingSessionHandler | None): Builds the exception
            to raise when no session resolves — :func:`redirect_to` for
            HTML routes. ``None`` raises :class:`UnauthorizedException`.

    Returns:
        Callable[[Request], Awaitable[Session | None]]: An async FastAPI
        dependency, typed ``Awaitable[Session]`` when ``required=True``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``on_missing`` is given with ``required=False``
            — an optional dependency never raises, so the handler would
            never run.
    """
    if on_missing is not None and not required:
        raise ValueError("on_missing only applies when required=True")

    async def _resolver(request: Request) -> Session | None:
        """Return the request's session, or raise when it is required.

        Args:
            request (Request): The inbound request.

        Returns:
            Session | None: The live session, or ``None`` when optional
            and absent.

        Raises:
            Exception: ``on_missing(request)``, or
                :class:`UnauthorizedException`, when required and absent.
        """
        session: Session | None = getattr(request.state, "session", None)
        if session is None and session_auth is not None:
            auth = session_auth(request) if callable(session_auth) else session_auth
            cookie = request.cookies.get(auth.settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)
            request.state.session_id_plaintext = cookie
            if cookie:
                session = await auth.resolve(cookie)
            request.state.session = session
        if session is None and required:
            if on_missing is not None:
                raise on_missing(request)
            raise UnauthorizedException(message="session required")
        return session

    return _resolver

def make_session_router(
    service: SessionAuth,
    *,
    session_factory: Callable[..., AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]],
    prefix: str = "/auth/session",
    tags: list[str] | None = None,
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter:
    """Build the bundled session router.

    Args:
        service (SessionAuth): Configured auth service that talks
            to the store + verifies passwords against the user
            model.
        session_factory (Callable[..., AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]]):
            FastAPI dependency yielding an async SQLAlchemy session
            — typically ``db.session_dependency``.
        prefix (str): URL prefix. Defaults to ``"/auth/session"``.
        tags (list[str] | None): OpenAPI tags. Defaults to
            ``["session"]``.
        docs_locale (str | None): Language of the OpenAPI ``summary``
            and ``description`` text — ``"en-US"`` or ``"pt-BR"``.
            ``None`` (default) reads ``API_DOCS_LOCALE`` through
            :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings`,
            whose default is ``"en-US"``.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: Ready to mount with ``app.include_router``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``service`` was built with ``authenticator=``
            (for example by :meth:`SessionAuth.from_credentials`).
    """
    if service.user_model is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "make_session_router needs a SessionAuth built with user_model=; "
            "a SessionAuth from authenticator= / from_credentials() has no "
            "user table for the bundled JSON login. Write the login route "
            "with SessionAuth.login_with_credentials() instead."
        )
    settings = service.settings
    route_docs: RouteDocs = RouteDocs(docs_locale)
    router = APIRouter(prefix=prefix, tags=list(tags or ["session"]))

    db_dep = Depends(session_provider_for(session_factory))
    current_session_required = Depends(make_session_dependency(required=True))

    def _set_session_cookie(response: Response, plaintext: str) -> None:
        """Write the session cookie from ``SessionSettings``.

        Args:
            response (Response): The outgoing response.
            plaintext (str): The session id to send.
        """
        response.set_cookie(value=plaintext, **settings.session_cookie_kwargs())

    def _clear_session_cookie(response: Response) -> None:
        """Delete the session cookie with the attributes it was set with.

        Args:
            response (Response): The outgoing response.
        """
        response.delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs())

    @router.post(
        "/login",
        description=route_docs.description("sessions.login"),
        response_model=SessionResponseSchema,
        status_code=status.HTTP_200_OK,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sessions.login"),
    )
    async def login(
        payload: SessionLoginSchema,
        request: Request,
        response: Response,
        session: AsyncSession = db_dep,
    ) -> SessionResponseSchema:
        """Authenticate and open a server-side session.

        Args:
            payload (SessionLoginSchema): Email and password.
            request (Request): The inbound request, read for client metadata.
            response (Response): The outgoing response, used to set the cookie.
            session (AsyncSession): The request-scoped DB session.

        Returns:
            Response: The session cookie plus the login payload.
        """
        user = await service.authenticate(
            session,
            email=payload.email,
            password=payload.password,
        )
        await session.commit()
        previous = request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)
        new_session, plaintext = await service.login(
            user_id=user.id,
            ip=get_client_ip(request),
            user_agent=request.headers.get("user-agent"),
            previous_session_id=previous,
        )
        _set_session_cookie(response, plaintext)
        return SessionResponseSchema(
            user_id=user.id,
            expires_at=new_session.expires_at,
        )

    @router.post(
        "/logout",
        description=route_docs.description("sessions.logout"),
        status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sessions.logout"),
    )
    async def logout(
        request: Request,
        response: Response,
    ) -> Response:
        cookie = request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)
        if cookie:
            await service.revoke(cookie)
        _clear_session_cookie(response)
        response.status_code = status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT
        return response

    @router.get(
        "/me",
        description=route_docs.description("sessions.me"),
        response_model=Session,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sessions.me"),
    )
    async def me(
        session: Session = current_session_required,
    ) -> Session:
        return session

    @router.get(
        "/list",
        description=route_docs.description("sessions.list_sessions"),
        response_model=list[SessionSummarySchema],
        summary=route_docs.summary("sessions.list_sessions"),
    )
    async def list_sessions(
        request: Request,
        session: Session = current_session_required,
    ) -> list[SessionSummarySchema]:
        """List the caller's active sessions.

        Args:
            request (Request): The inbound request, read for client metadata.
            session (Session): The caller's current server-side session.

        Returns:
            list[SessionInfoSchema]: One entry per active session.
        """
        current_plain: str | None = getattr(request.state, "session_id_plaintext", None)
        return await service.list_sessions(
            session.user_id,
            current_session_id_plaintext=current_plain,
        )

    @router.delete(
        "/{public_id}",
        description=route_docs.description("sessions.revoke_one"),
        status_code=status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sessions.revoke_one"),
    )
    async def revoke_one(
        public_id: str,
        request: Request,
        response: Response,
        session: Session = current_session_required,
    ) -> Response:
        """Revoke one of the caller's sessions by its public id.

        Revoking your own session also clears the cookie, so the browser
        stops presenting an identifier that no longer resolves.

        Args:
            public_id (str): Public id of the session to revoke.
            request (Request): The inbound request.
            response (Response): The outgoing response, used to clear the
                cookie when the caller revoked themselves.
            session (Session): The caller's current session.

        Returns:
            Response: An empty ``204``.
        """
        await service.revoke_by_public_id(session.user_id, public_id)
        if session.session_id.startswith(public_id):
            _clear_session_cookie(response)
        response.status_code = status.HTTP_204_NO_CONTENT
        return response

    return router

    Args:
        user_model (type[UserT]): The concrete user model.
        session_factory (Callable[..., AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]]): The
            request-scoped DB session provider.
        session_auth (SessionAuth | SessionAuthFactory): Resolves the
            cookie, as in :func:`make_session_dependency`.
        on_missing (MissingSessionHandler | None): Exception for no
            session, or a session whose account is gone or inactive —
            :func:`redirect_to_login` for pages. ``None`` raises
            :class:`UnauthorizedException` (``401``).
        require_mfa (bool): Also require the session to have passed the
            second factor (``otp`` in :attr:`Session.amr`); a session
            without it is refused with ``403``, the same answer
            ``make_mfa_required_dependency`` gives a token.

    Returns:
        Callable[..., Awaitable[UserT]]: An async FastAPI dependency.
    """
    resolve_session = make_session_dependency(
        required=False,
        session_auth=session_auth,
    )
    session_provider = session_provider_for(session_factory)

    def _missing(request: Request) -> Exception:
        """Build the refusal for a request without a usable session.

        Args:
            request (Request): The inbound request.

        Returns:
            Exception: ``on_missing(request)`` or a ``401``.
        """
        if on_missing is not None:
            return on_missing(request)
        return UnauthorizedException(message="session required")

    async def _dependency(
        request: Request,
        db: Any = Depends(session_provider),
    ) -> UserT:
        """Return the active account behind the request's session.

        Args:
            request (Request): The inbound request.
            db (Any): The request-scoped ``AsyncSession``.

        Returns:
            UserT: The account.

        Raises:
            Exception: :func:`_missing` without a usable session.
            ForbiddenException: With ``require_mfa`` and no ``otp``.
        """
        session = await resolve_session(request)
        if session is None:
            raise _missing(request)
        user: UserT | None = await db.get(user_model, session.user_id)
        if user is None or not user.is_active:
            raise _missing(request)
        if require_mfa and AMR_OTP not in session.amr:
            raise ForbiddenException(message="this action requires MFA")
        return user

    return _dependency

def redirect_to(
    url: str,
    *,
    status_code: int = status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER,
) -> MissingSessionHandler:
    """Build an ``on_missing`` handler that redirects to ``url``.

    For HTML routes, where a missing session should send the browser to
    the login page instead of answering a JSON ``401``. The dependency
    raises an ``HTTPException`` carrying the status and a ``Location``
    header; FastAPI's handler and the SDK's
    :func:`register_exception_handlers` both keep the header, and the
    browser follows it.

    Args:
        url (str): Where to send the browser, e.g. ``"/login"``.
        status_code (int): Redirect status. ``303 See Other`` (default)
            makes the browser follow with a ``GET`` whatever the original
            method was.

    Returns:
        MissingSessionHandler: A handler for
        ``make_session_dependency(on_missing=...)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``status_code`` is not a ``3xx`` status.
    """
    if not 300 <= status_code < 400:
        raise ValueError(f"redirect_to needs a 3xx status, got {status_code}")

    def _handler(request: Request) -> Exception:
        """Return the redirect exception for ``request``.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request that carried no live session.

        Returns:
            Exception: An ``HTTPException`` with ``Location: url``.
        """
        return HTTPException(status_code=status_code, headers={"Location": url})

    return _handler

def redirect_to_login(
    login_path: str,
    *,
    status_code: int = status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER,
) -> MissingSessionHandler:
    """Build an ``on_missing`` handler that sends the browser to the login.

    Unlike :func:`redirect_to`, it carries the requested path and query
    along as ``?next=``, so the login page can bring the user back. The
    login pages of :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.make_auth_pages_router`
    only follow a ``next`` that is a path on the same site.

    Args:
        login_path (str): The login page, e.g. ``"/login"``.
        status_code (int): Redirect status, ``303`` by default.

    Returns:
        MissingSessionHandler: A handler for ``on_missing=``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``status_code`` is not a ``3xx`` status.
    """
    if not 300 <= status_code < 400:
        raise ValueError(f"redirect_to_login needs a 3xx status, got {status_code}")

    def _handler(request: Request) -> Exception:
        """Return the redirect carrying the requested path as ``next``.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request that carried no live session.

        Returns:
            Exception: An ``HTTPException`` with ``Location``.
        """
        target = request.url.path
        if request.url.query:
            target = f"{target}?{request.url.query}"
        location = f"{login_path}?next={quote(target, safe='/')}"
        return HTTPException(status_code=status_code, headers={"Location": location})

    return _handler

def read_project_version(pyproject_path: Path | None = None) -> str:
    """Return the project version declared in a ``pyproject.toml``.

    With no argument the search starts at the current working directory
    and walks up to the filesystem root, stopping at the first
    ``pyproject.toml`` it finds — the same resolution ``find_pyproject``
    uses. Pass an explicit ``pyproject_path`` when the answer must not
    depend on the working directory: the scaffolded settings module
    anchors it on its own location, so the version is the project's even
    when the app is started from somewhere else.

    Args:
        pyproject_path (Path | None): The file to read. Defaults to the
            nearest ``pyproject.toml`` above the current working
            directory.

    Returns:
        str: The value of ``[project].version``.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When no ``pyproject.toml`` is found. The
            message lists every path the search visited, so a miss names
            what it looked for and where.
        ValueError: When the file has no ``[project].version`` — an
            absent ``[project]`` table, an absent key, or a project that
            declares the version through ``dynamic``. The message names
            the file and the missing key.
    """
    if pyproject_path is None:
        candidates = _candidate_paths(Path.cwd())
        pyproject_path = next(
            (candidate for candidate in candidates if candidate.is_file()),
            None,
        )
        if pyproject_path is None:
            searched = "\n".join(f"  - {candidate}" for candidate in candidates)
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                "No pyproject.toml found walking up from "
                f"{Path.cwd().resolve()} to the filesystem root. Searched:\n"
                f"{searched}\nPass pyproject_path explicitly if the file "
                "lives elsewhere."
            )
    elif not pyproject_path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: no such file. Pass a path to an existing "
            "pyproject.toml with [project].version."
        )

    with pyproject_path.open("rb") as handle:
        data = tomllib.load(handle)
    project = data.get("project")
    if not isinstance(project, dict) or VERSION_KEY not in project:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: missing [project].version. Declare "
            'version = "x.y.z" under [project], or point the helper at a '
            "file that does. A project that resolves its version through "
            'dynamic = ["version"] has none to read.'
        )
    version = project[VERSION_KEY]
    if not isinstance(version, str):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: [project].version is "
            f"{type(version).__name__}, expected a string."
        )
    return version

Mounts two routes:

  • POST <prefix>/ticket — guarded by current_user; answers a :class:SSETicketResponseSchema whose ticket opens the channel channel_for(user).

def make_sse_router(
    broker: SSEBroker | Callable[[Request], SSEBroker],
    *,
    tokens: JWTUtils | Callable[[Request], JWTUtils],
    current_user: Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]],
    fallback_user: Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] | None = None,
    channel_for: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None,
    prefix: str = "/sse",
    tag: str = "SSE",
    ticket_ttl: timedelta | None = None,
    ticket_param: str = "ticket",
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter:
    """Build the router that issues SSE tickets and serves the stream.

    Mounts two routes:

    * ``POST <prefix>/ticket`` — guarded by ``current_user``; answers a
      :class:`SSETicketResponseSchema` whose ticket opens the channel
      ``channel_for(user)``.
    * ``GET <prefix>/stream`` — reads ``?<ticket_param>=``, checks the
      signature, the expiry and ``typ="stream"``, and returns
      ``broker.response(channel)``. Without a ticket it asks
      ``fallback_user``; with neither it answers ``401``.

    The channel travels **inside** the signed ticket, so the stream route
    opens no database session and the client cannot pick a channel of
    its own. A deactivated account stops getting tickets at once (that is
    ``current_user``'s check) and loses the stream on its next reconnect.

    With :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.UserAuthService`, prefer
    :meth:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.UserAuthService.sse_router`, which builds
    ``tokens``, ``current_user`` and ``fallback_user`` from the service.

    Args:
        broker (SSEBroker | Callable[[Request], SSEBroker]): The broker the
            stream subscribes to, or a factory called with each request
            that returns it (``lambda request: request.app.state.broker``).
        tokens (JWTUtils | Callable[[Request], JWTUtils]): The helper that
            signs and verifies tickets — the same one that signs the
            access token, or a factory returning it.
        current_user (Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]]): The
            dependency that authenticates ``POST <prefix>/ticket`` and
            yields the user, raising on a missing or invalid session.
        fallback_user (Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] | None): A
            **soft** user dependency the stream route asks when no ticket
            came — it returns ``None`` instead of raising. Lets a client
            that can send ``Authorization: Bearer`` skip the ticket, and,
            built with ``query_param``, keeps an existing
            ``?access_token=`` client working while it migrates. ``None``
            (default) makes the ticket the only way in.
        channel_for (Callable[[Any], str] | None): Maps the authenticated
            user to the broker channel. ``None`` (default) uses
            ``str(user.id)``.
        prefix (str): URL prefix. Defaults to ``"/sse"``.
        tag (str): OpenAPI tag. Defaults to ``"SSE"``.
        ticket_ttl (timedelta | None): Lifetime of a ticket. ``None``
            (default) uses :data:`DEFAULT_SSE_TICKET_TTL` (60 seconds).
        ticket_param (str): Query parameter the stream route reads the
            ticket from. Defaults to ``"ticket"``.
        docs_locale (str | None): Language of the OpenAPI ``summary``
            and ``description`` text — ``"en-US"`` or ``"pt-BR"``.
            ``None`` (default) reads ``API_DOCS_LOCALE`` through
            :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings`,
            whose default is ``"en-US"``.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: The router, ready for ``app.include_router``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``ticket_ttl`` is shorter than one second.
    """
    resolved_channel_for = channel_for if channel_for is not None else _user_id_channel
    resolved_ttl = ticket_ttl if ticket_ttl is not None else DEFAULT_SSE_TICKET_TTL
    ttl_seconds = int(resolved_ttl.total_seconds())
    if ttl_seconds < 1:
        raise ValueError("ticket_ttl must be at least one second.")

    def resolve_broker(request: Request) -> SSEBroker:
        """Return the broker for this request.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.

        Returns:
            SSEBroker: ``broker`` itself, or what its factory returns.
        """
        if isinstance(broker, SSEBroker):
            return broker
        return broker(request)

    route_docs: RouteDocs = RouteDocs(docs_locale)
    router = APIRouter(prefix=prefix, tags=[tag])

    @router.post(
        "/ticket",
        response_model=SSETicketResponseSchema,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sse.issue_ticket"),
        description=route_docs.description(
            "sse.issue_ticket", prefix=prefix, ticket_param=ticket_param
        ),
    )
    async def issue_ticket(
        request: Request,
        user: Any = Depends(current_user),
    ) -> SSETicketResponseSchema:
        """Sign a ticket for the caller's channel.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.
            user (Any): The authenticated user.

        Returns:
            SSETicketResponseSchema: The ticket and its lifetime.
        """
        ticket = _resolve_tokens(tokens, request).encode(
            {"typ": STREAM_TOKEN_TYPE, SSE_CHANNEL_CLAIM: resolved_channel_for(user)},
            ttl=timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds),
        )
        return SSETicketResponseSchema(ticket=ticket, expires_in=ttl_seconds)

    @router.get(
        "/stream",
        response_class=StreamingResponse,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sse.stream"),
        description=route_docs.description(
            "sse.stream", prefix=prefix, ticket_param=ticket_param
        ),
    )
    async def stream(
        request: Request,
        fallback: Any = Depends(fallback_user or _no_fallback_user),
    ) -> StreamingResponse:
        """Subscribe the caller to the channel its credential names.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.
            fallback (Any): What ``fallback_user`` resolved, or ``None``.

        Returns:
            StreamingResponse: The SSE response.

        Raises:
            UnauthorizedException: When the ticket is absent, expired,
                forged or of another ``typ``, and no fallback user
                resolved.
        """
        ticket = request.query_params.get(ticket_param)
        if ticket is not None:
            payload = _resolve_tokens(tokens, request).decode_or_none(ticket)
            channel = None if payload is None else payload.get(SSE_CHANNEL_CLAIM)
            if (
                payload is None
                or payload.get("typ") != STREAM_TOKEN_TYPE
                or not isinstance(channel, str)
            ):
                raise UnauthorizedException(message=SSE_TICKET_ERROR)
        elif fallback is not None:
            channel = resolved_channel_for(fallback)
        else:
            raise UnauthorizedException(message=SSE_TICKET_ERROR)
        return resolve_broker(request).response(channel)

    return router

Wrap stream in a Starlette text/event-stream response.

Adds the SSE-specific headers (Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no) so intermediate proxies don't buffer or cache the long-lived response. Pass on_disconnect to run cleanup when the client goes away — the response generator's finally is the one place guaranteed to fire on disconnect, so this is where you cancel a bound producer task or call :meth:SSEBroker.unregister. It removes the hand-rolled try/finally wrapper the recipe used to require.

def sse_response(
    stream: AsyncIterable[bytes],
    *,
    status_code: int = 200,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    on_disconnect: Callable[[], object] | None = None,
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Wrap ``stream`` in a Starlette ``text/event-stream`` response.

    Adds the SSE-specific headers (``Cache-Control: no-cache``,
    ``Connection: keep-alive``, ``X-Accel-Buffering: no``) so
    intermediate proxies don't buffer or cache the long-lived
    response. Caller-supplied ``headers`` are layered **below** the
    SSE defaults so the three critical headers above cannot be
    accidentally overridden — pass extra metadata, not replacements.

    Pass ``on_disconnect`` to run cleanup when the client goes away —
    the response generator's ``finally`` is the one place guaranteed to
    fire on disconnect, so this is where you cancel a bound producer
    task or call :meth:`SSEBroker.unregister`. It removes the
    hand-rolled ``try/finally`` wrapper the recipe used to require.

    Args:
        stream (AsyncIterable[bytes]): The byte stream produced by
            :meth:`EventStream.stream` (or any compatible generator).
        status_code (int): HTTP status code. Defaults to ``200``.
        headers (dict[str, str] | None): Extra headers to attach.
        on_disconnect (Callable[[], object] | None): Cleanup callback
            run (and awaited if it returns an awaitable) when the stream
            ends or the client disconnects. ``None`` skips it.

    Returns:
        StreamingResponse: A ready-to-return SSE response.
    """
    merged: dict[str, str] = {**(headers or {}), **_SSE_HEADERS}
    body: AsyncIterable[bytes] = (
        stream if on_disconnect is None else _guard_stream(stream, on_disconnect)
    )
    return StreamingResponse(
        body,
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        status_code=status_code,
        headers=merged,
    )

make_local_storage_router(
    client: LocalObjectStorageClient,
    *,
    as_attachment: bool = False,
    cache_control: str | None = "private, no-store",
) -> APIRouter

Build the GET/PUT/POST routes for a local store's signed links.

  • GET {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key} verifies a download signature and streams the object with its stored content type, honouring Range and the validators (206/304/416) the same way :meth:AsyncMinIOClient.download_response <tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient.download_response> does. A missing object answers 404 NOT_FOUND. A link signed with filename/media_type/as_attachment answers with those, the way S3 answers a link with signed response-* overrides.
  • PUT {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key} verifies an upload signature and stores the raw body with the request's Content-Type. A Content-Length over :attr:LocalObjectStorageClient.max_upload_bytes is refused before reading; without it the body is counted while it streams and cut at the cap — 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE either way, and nothing is stored. Success answers 200 with the ETag, as S3 does.
  • POST {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key} answers a :meth:LocalObjectStorageClient.presigned_post_policy form. The file must fit the signed [min_bytes, max_bytes] — 413 FILE_TOO_LARGE / 400 FILE_TOO_SMALL otherwise — and the key and Content-Type fields must match the signed ones (403 SIGNED_URL_INVALID). Success answers 204 with the ETag, as S3 does. Reading the form needs python-multipart ([upload]).

A tampered, unsigned or wrong-purpose link answers 403 SIGNED_URL_INVALID, an expired one 403 SIGNED_URL_EXPIRED. Both routes stay out of the OpenAPI schema.

With encryption_keys on the client the routes do not change shape: PUT and POST store the body encrypted, the caps count the plaintext, and GET (Range included) answers the plaintext. A stored file whose first served block fails its check answers 500 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR with no byte of it; a later block that fails cuts the connection after the blocks that verified.

    * ``GET {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key}`` verifies a download signature
      and streams the object with its stored content type, honouring
      ``Range`` and the validators (``206``/``304``/``416``) the same way
      :meth:`AsyncMinIOClient.download_response
      <tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.AsyncMinIOClient.download_response>`
      does. A missing object answers ``404 NOT_FOUND``. A link signed with
      ``filename``/``media_type``/``as_attachment`` answers with those,
      the way S3 answers a link with signed ``response-*`` overrides.
    * ``PUT {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key}`` verifies an upload signature
      and stores the raw body with the request's ``Content-Type``. A
      ``Content-Length`` over :attr:`LocalObjectStorageClient.max_upload_bytes`
      is refused before reading; without it the body is counted while it
      streams and cut at the cap — ``413 FILE_TOO_LARGE`` either way, and
      nothing is stored. Success answers ``200`` with the ``ETag``, as S3
      does.
    * ``POST {route_prefix}/{bucket}/{key}`` answers a
      :meth:`LocalObjectStorageClient.presigned_post_policy` form. The file
      must fit the signed ``[min_bytes, max_bytes]`` — ``413 FILE_TOO_LARGE``
      / ``400 FILE_TOO_SMALL`` otherwise — and the ``key`` and
      ``Content-Type`` fields must match the signed ones (``403
      SIGNED_URL_INVALID``). Success answers ``204`` with the ``ETag``, as
      S3 does. Reading the form needs ``python-multipart`` (``[upload]``).

    A tampered, unsigned or wrong-purpose link answers
    ``403 SIGNED_URL_INVALID``, an expired one ``403 SIGNED_URL_EXPIRED``.
    Both routes stay out of the OpenAPI schema.

    With ``encryption_keys`` on the client the routes do not change shape:
    ``PUT`` and ``POST`` store the body encrypted, the caps count the
    plaintext, and ``GET`` (``Range`` included) answers the plaintext. A
    stored file whose first served block fails its check answers
    ``500 STORAGE_INTEGRITY_ERROR`` with no byte of it; a later block that
    fails cuts the connection after the blocks that verified.

    Args:
        client (LocalObjectStorageClient): The store whose links to serve.
        as_attachment (bool): ``True`` makes downloads save as a file;
            ``False`` (default) shows inline-safe types (images, PDF) in the
            browser, which is what an ``<img src>`` needs.
        cache_control (str | None): ``Cache-Control`` of downloads. Default
            ``"private, no-store"``: the link is a short-lived capability,
            so no shared cache keeps the bytes. ``None`` sends none.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: Router with ``prefix=client.route_prefix``; include it at
        the app root.
    """
    router = APIRouter(prefix=client.route_prefix, include_in_schema=False)
    can_upload = client.signature_dependency(LOCAL_STORAGE_PUT_PURPOSE)

    @router.get("/{bucket}/{key:path}")
    async def download_object(
        request: Request,
        bucket: str,
        key: str,
    ) -> StreamingResponse:
        params = client.verify_link(
            request,
            purpose=LOCAL_STORAGE_GET_PURPOSE,
            names=LOCAL_GET_LINK_PARAMS,
        )
        _validated(client, bucket, key)
        disposition = params.get("disposition")
        try:
            return await client.download_response(
                key,
                request=request,
                bucket=bucket,
                filename=params.get("filename"),
                media_type=params.get("media_type"),
                as_attachment=(
                    as_attachment if disposition is None else disposition != "inline"
                ),
                cache_control=cache_control,
            )
        except LocalObjectNotFoundError:
            raise NotFoundException(message="Object not found") from None

    @router.put("/{bucket}/{key:path}", dependencies=[Depends(can_upload)])
    async def upload_object(request: Request, bucket: str, key: str) -> Response:
        _validated(client, bucket, key)
        declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
        if (
            declared is not None
            and declared.isdigit()
            and int(declared) > client.max_upload_bytes
        ):
            raise FileTooLargeException(
                details={"max_size_bytes": client.max_upload_bytes},
            )
        etag = await client.write_stream(
            key,
            request.stream(),
            bucket=bucket,
            content_type=request.headers.get(
                "content-type", "application/octet-stream"
            ),
            max_bytes=client.max_upload_bytes,
        )
        return Response(status_code=200, headers={"etag": f'"{etag}"'})

    @router.post("/{bucket}/{key:path}")
    async def post_object(request: Request, bucket: str, key: str) -> Response:
        params = client.verify_link(
            request,
            purpose=LOCAL_STORAGE_POST_PURPOSE,
            names=LOCAL_POST_LINK_PARAMS,
        )
        _validated(client, bucket, key)
        max_bytes = _bound_int(params, "max_bytes")
        min_bytes = _bound_int(params, "min_bytes")
        declared = request.headers.get("content-length")
        if (
            declared is not None
            and declared.isdigit()
            and int(declared) > max_bytes + POST_FORM_OVERHEAD_BYTES
        ):
            raise FileTooLargeException(details={"max_size_bytes": max_bytes})
        async with request.form(
            max_files=1,
            max_fields=POST_FORM_MAX_FIELDS,
        ) as form:
            if form.get("key", key) != key:
                raise InvalidSignedURLException()
            expected_type = params.get("content_type")
            sent_type = form.get("Content-Type")
            if expected_type is not None and sent_type != expected_type:
                raise InvalidSignedURLException()
            upload = form.get(POST_FILE_FIELD)
            if upload is None or isinstance(upload, str):
                raise InvalidSignedURLException()
            size = upload.size or 0
            if size > max_bytes:
                raise FileTooLargeException(details={"max_size_bytes": max_bytes})
            if size < min_bytes:
                raise FileTooSmallException(details={"min_size_bytes": min_bytes})

            async def chunks() -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
                while chunk := await upload.read(LOCAL_STORAGE_CHUNK_SIZE):
                    yield chunk

            etag = await client.write_stream(
                key,
                chunks(),
                bucket=bucket,
                content_type=(
                    sent_type
                    if isinstance(sent_type, str)
                    else upload.content_type or "application/octet-stream"
                ),
                max_bytes=max_bytes,
            )
        return Response(status_code=204, headers={"etag": f'"{etag}"'})

    return router

Example:

Narrow the tuple to the transient failures you actually mean; a TypeError retried three times is the same bug, later.

def async_retry(
    policy: RetryPolicy | None = None,
    exceptions: tuple[type[BaseException], ...] = (Exception,),
    *,
    logger: RetryLogger | None = None,
) -> Callable[[Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]], Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]]:
    """Retry an async callable with the bounded backoff of ``policy``.

    Example:

        >>> from tempest_fastapi_sdk import RetryPolicy, async_retry
        >>>
        >>> @async_retry(RetryPolicy(max_attempts=5), (ConnectionError,))
        ... async def connect(url: str) -> None:
        ...     ...

    When every attempt fails, the **last** exception propagates rather
    than a wrapper: a caller that could react to a permanent
    ``ConnectionError`` should still see a ``ConnectionError``.

    ``exceptions`` defaults to ``Exception``, which deliberately
    excludes :class:`asyncio.CancelledError` — it derives from
    ``BaseException``, and retrying a cancelled task fights the
    cancellation instead of honoring it. Narrow the tuple to the
    transient failures you actually mean; a ``TypeError`` retried three
    times is the same bug, later.

    Args:
        policy (RetryPolicy | None): Attempt budget and backoff curve.
            ``None`` (default) builds a fresh :class:`RetryPolicy` —
            a shared module-level instance would be mutable state every
            decorated function points at.
        exceptions (tuple[type[BaseException], ...]): Exception types
            that count as transient. Anything outside the tuple
            propagates immediately, without consuming an attempt.
        logger (RetryLogger | None): Where the retry and give-up
            records go. Anything with ``warning`` and ``error`` fits —
            a ``logging.Logger``, or the
            :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.LogUtils` this SDK hands the
            service. ``None`` uses this module's logger.

    Returns:
        Callable: A decorator wrapping the target coroutine function.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``policy.max_attempts`` is below ``1``, which
            would run the callable zero times and return ``None`` from
            something annotated to return ``T``.
    """
    resolved: RetryPolicy = policy if policy is not None else RetryPolicy()
    log: RetryLogger = logger if logger is not None else _LOGGER

    if resolved.max_attempts < 1:
        raise ValueError("policy.max_attempts must be >= 1")

    def decorator(fn: Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]) -> Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]:
        """Wrap ``fn`` in the retry loop.

        Args:
            fn (Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]): The coroutine function.

        Returns:
            Callable[P, Awaitable[T]]: The wrapped function.
        """

        @wraps(fn)
        async def wrapper(*args: P.args, **kwargs: P.kwargs) -> T:
            """Call ``fn``, retrying transient failures.

            Args:
                *args (P.args): Forwarded positionally.
                **kwargs (P.kwargs): Forwarded by keyword.

            Returns:
                T: Whatever ``fn`` returned on the first success.

            Raises:
                BaseException: The last failure, when the budget runs
                    out, or the first one outside ``exceptions``.
            """
            for attempt in range(1, resolved.max_attempts + 1):
                try:
                    return await fn(*args, **kwargs)
                except exceptions as error:
                    if attempt == resolved.max_attempts:
                        log.error(
                            "async_retry: %s gave up after %d attempts: %s",
                            fn.__qualname__,
                            resolved.max_attempts,
                            error,
                        )
                        raise
                    delay: float = resolved.sleep_for(attempt)
                    log.warning(
                        "async_retry: %s failed on attempt %d/%d (%s);"
                        " retrying in %.2fs",
                        fn.__qualname__,
                        attempt,
                        resolved.max_attempts,
                        error,
                        delay,
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(delay)
            raise AssertionError("unreachable: the loop returns or raises")

        return wrapper

    return decorator

Emits both an ASCII filename (with quotes/backslashes stripped as a legacy fallback) and a UTF-8 filename* parameter (RFC 5987) so non-ASCII names survive across clients.

The name is treated as untrusted, because in the documented usage it is UploadFile.filename — a value the client chose. def build_content_disposition(
    filename: str,
    *,
    as_attachment: bool = True,
    media_type: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Build an RFC 6266 ``Content-Disposition`` header value.

    Emits both an ASCII ``filename`` (with quotes/backslashes stripped as a
    legacy fallback) and a UTF-8 ``filename*`` parameter (RFC 5987) so
    non-ASCII names survive across clients.

    The name is treated as untrusted, because in the documented usage it is
    ``UploadFile.filename`` — a value the client chose. Taking the basename
    stops a path from being injected, but on its own left the control
    characters in: a name containing ``\\r\\n`` produced a header value with a
    real line break, which an ASGI server that does not validate header
    values (uvicorn on ``httptools``) writes to the socket verbatim, letting
    the caller append headers of their own to your response. Every character
    below ``0x20`` plus ``DEL`` is dropped here, so what comes out is always
    a single header line.

    ``as_attachment=False`` is a request, not a decision: it yields
    ``inline`` only when ``media_type`` is in
    :data:`INLINE_SAFE_MEDIA_TYPES`. Any other type — ``text/html``,
    ``image/svg+xml``, ``application/octet-stream`` — and ``None`` yield
    ``attachment``.

    Args:
        filename (str): The name the client should see for the download.
            Reduced to its basename, with control characters removed, so
            neither a path nor a header break can be injected.
        as_attachment (bool): ``True`` forces a download
            (``attachment``); ``False`` asks for ``inline``, granted only
            to an inline-safe ``media_type``. Default ``True``.
        media_type (str | None): The type the response carries. Parameters
            are ignored in the check. ``None`` (unknown) is not inline-safe.
            Default ``None``.

    Returns:
        str: A ready-to-use header value, e.g.
        ``attachment; filename="a.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''a.pdf``.
    """
    inline: bool = not as_attachment and _is_inline_safe(media_type)
    disposition: str = "inline" if inline else "attachment"
    sanitized: str = _strip_control_chars(filename)
    safe_name: str = Path(sanitized).name or "download"
    ascii_fallback: str = safe_name.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    ascii_fallback = ascii_fallback.replace("\\", "_").replace('"', "_")
    if not ascii_fallback:
        ascii_fallback = "download"
    encoded: str = quote(safe_name, safe="")
    return f"{disposition}; filename=\"{ascii_fallback}\"; filename*=UTF-8''{encoded}"

def check_password_policy(
    password: str,
    policy: PasswordPolicy | None = None,
) -> PasswordPolicyViolation | None:
    """Check a plaintext password against a policy.

    Returns the violation instead of raising, so a form can put the
    message next to the field while a service turns the same value into
    a ``ValidationException``. That split is the reason this lives here
    and not inside the auth service: the rule was private to
    ``UserAuthService``, so every other surface that accepts a password
    — the admin panel's create form, a provisioning script — either
    skipped it or wrote its own.

    Args:
        password (str): The plaintext to check.
        policy (PasswordPolicy | None): The rules to apply. ``None``
            uses the ``AuthSettings`` defaults.

    Returns:
        PasswordPolicyViolation | None: The first violation found, or
        ``None`` when the password is acceptable.
    """
    policy = policy or PasswordPolicy()
    floor = policy.min_length
    if policy.require_complexity:
        floor = max(floor, 8)
    if len(password) < floor:
        return PasswordPolicyViolation(
            message=f"password must be at least {floor} characters",
            details={"min_length": floor},
            code=PasswordViolationCodeEnum.PASSWORD_TOO_SHORT,
        )
    encoded_length = len(password.encode("utf-8"))
    if encoded_length > policy.max_bytes:
        return PasswordPolicyViolation(
            message=f"password must be at most {policy.max_bytes} bytes",
            details={
                "max_bytes": policy.max_bytes,
                "length_bytes": encoded_length,
            },
            code=PasswordViolationCodeEnum.PASSWORD_TOO_LONG,
        )
    if not policy.require_complexity:
        return None
    missing: list[str] = []
    if not any(c.islower() for c in password):
        missing.append("lowercase")
    if not any(c.isupper() for c in password):
        missing.append("uppercase")
    if not any(c.isdigit() for c in password):
        missing.append("digit")
    if not any(not c.isalnum() for c in password):
        missing.append("special")
    if missing:
        return PasswordPolicyViolation(
            message=(
                "password must contain at least one "
                + ", ".join(missing)
                + " character"
            ),
            details={"missing_classes": missing},
            code=PasswordViolationCodeEnum.PASSWORD_TOO_WEAK,
        )
    return None

def detect_pix_key_type(value: str) -> PixKeyType | None:
    """Return the :class:`PixKeyType` a PIX key belongs to, or ``None``.

    Detection is by shape: ``@`` → e-mail, leading ``+`` → phone, UUID
    shape → random, otherwise digits-only length + check digits decide
    between CPF and CNPJ.

    Args:
        value (str): The raw PIX key (masked CPF/CNPJ accepted).

    Returns:
        PixKeyType | None: The detected type, or ``None`` when ``value``
        is not a valid key of any type, including any value longer than
        77 characters once trimmed.
    """
    candidate = value.strip()
    if not candidate or len(candidate) > _PIX_KEY_MAX_LENGTH:
        return None
    if "@" in candidate:
        return PixKeyType.EMAIL if _PIX_EMAIL_PATTERN.match(candidate) else None
    if candidate.startswith("+"):
        return PixKeyType.PHONE if _PIX_PHONE_PATTERN.match(candidate) else None
    if _PIX_RANDOM_PATTERN.match(candidate):
        return PixKeyType.RANDOM
    digits = only_digits(candidate)
    if len(digits) == 11 and is_valid_cpf(digits):
        return PixKeyType.CPF
    if len(digits) == 14 and is_valid_cnpj(digits):
        return PixKeyType.CNPJ
    return None

def form_encode(payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Flatten a nested payload into bracket-notation form fields.

    Args:
        payload (Mapping[str, Any] | None): The request body as a nested
            mapping. ``None`` yields an empty mapping, so a caller can
            forward an optional body without branching.

    Returns:
        dict[str, str]: Flat ``field -> value`` pairs, ready to hand to
        ``httpx``' ``data=``.

    ``None`` values are **dropped rather than sent empty**: on these APIs
    an empty string is a real value (it clears a field), so serializing
    ``None`` as ``""`` would silently erase data the caller never meant to
    touch. Empty mappings and lists disappear for the same reason — they
    have no bracket path to occupy.

    Examples:
        >>> form_encode({"amount": 1000, "metadata": {"user_id": 42}})
        {'amount': '1000', 'metadata[user_id]': '42'}
        >>> form_encode({"items": [{"price": "price_123", "quantity": 2}]})
        {'items[0][price]': 'price_123', 'items[0][quantity]': '2'}
        >>> form_encode({"paid": True, "note": None})
        {'paid': 'true'}
    """
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    if payload is None:
        return out
    _flatten("", payload, out)
    return out

def format_currency_br(amount: Decimal, *, symbol: bool = True) -> str:
    """Render an amount in Brazilian currency notation.

    Args:
        amount (Decimal): The amount to render; quantized to two places
            before formatting.

        amount carries the sign ahead of the symbol (``"-R$ 0,01"``), which
        is how a credit reads on a Brazilian statement and how a closing
        difference must appear on a worksheet.

    body = _format_fixed(quantize_money(amount), 2)

    return f"-R$ {body[1:]}" if body.startswith("-") else f"R$ {body}"

def generate_opaque_token(nbytes: int = _DEFAULT_NBYTES) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Generate a cryptographically random token and its digest.

    Args:
        nbytes (int): Entropy in bytes for the URL-safe token. Defaults

Every character is ASCII, so the returned length is also the UTF-8 byte count bcrypt measures — max_bytes needs no separate encoding check.

def generate_password(
    *,
    min_length: int = 8,
    max_bytes: int = 72,
    require_complexity: bool = True,
) -> str:
    """Mint a random password that satisfies the configured policy.

    For flows where nobody types a password — the OAuth callback that
    creates an account, an admin provisioning a user — but the column
    is still ``NOT NULL``. The account owner reaches a password of
    their own through the ordinary reset flow; this one only has to be
    unguessable and *accepted*.

    **Compliance is by construction, not by retry.** Drawing from one
    flat alphabet and hoping is the defect this function exists to
    avoid: fed to ``UserAuthService._enforce_password_policy`` with
    complexity on and a 12-character floor, 200 000 samples
    each, ``secrets.token_urlsafe(16)`` was rejected 53.01% of the
    time, ``secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`` 26.54%, and
    ``secrets.token_hex(32)`` 100% (it has neither uppercase nor a
    special character, on every single draw). A generator that passes
    three times in four fails intermittently, in production, inside a
    callback, about a password the user never typed. So one character
    is drawn from each required class first, the rest fills from their
    union, and the result is shuffled with ``secrets.SystemRandom``.

    Every character is ASCII, so the returned length is also the UTF-8
    byte count bcrypt measures — ``max_bytes`` needs no separate
    encoding check.

    Args:
        min_length (int): The policy's ``AUTH_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH``.
            Raised to 8 internally when ``require_complexity`` is set,
            mirroring the floor the policy itself applies.
        max_bytes (int): The policy's ``AUTH_PASSWORD_MAX_BYTES``
            (72 by default — the bcrypt limit).
        require_complexity (bool): The policy's
            ``AUTH_PASSWORD_REQUIRE_COMPLEXITY``. Only affects the
            length floor: all four classes are always represented when
            the target length has room for them, since a stronger
            password is never rejected by a laxer policy.

    Returns:
        str: A fresh random password of at least ``min_length``
        characters and at most ``max_bytes`` bytes.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When the policy cannot be satisfied at all —
            ``max_bytes`` below the effective length floor. That is a
            misconfiguration no password could survive, so it surfaces
            here rather than as a validation error later.
    """
    floor = max(min_length, 8) if require_complexity else min_length
    if max_bytes < floor:
        raise ValueError(
            f"password policy is unsatisfiable: max_bytes={max_bytes} is "
            f"below the effective minimum length of {floor}"
        )
    length = min(max(floor, DEFAULT_GENERATED_PASSWORD_LENGTH), max_bytes)
    alphabet = "".join(_CHARACTER_CLASSES)
    chars: list[str] = []
    if length >= len(_CHARACTER_CLASSES):
        chars.extend(secrets.choice(group) for group in _CHARACTER_CLASSES)
    chars.extend(secrets.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length - len(chars)))
    secrets.SystemRandom().shuffle(chars)
    return "".join(chars)

def get_client_ip(
    request: Request,
    *,
    trusted_header: str | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Resolve the client IP from a Starlette/FastAPI request.

    Args:
        request (Request): The inbound request.
        trusted_header (str | None): Name of the single edge-set header
            to trust (case-insensitive, e.g. ``"x-real-ip"``). ``None``
            uses the direct transport peer only.

    Returns:
        str: The resolved client IP, or ``"unknown"`` when neither the
            trusted header nor the transport peer is available. A header
            value that is not one IP address is ignored (see
            :func:`parse_client_ip`).
    """
    if trusted_header:
        value = request.headers.get(trusted_header)
        parsed = parse_client_ip(value) if value else None
        if parsed is not None:
            return parsed
    return request.client.host if request.client else _UNKNOWN
