docs.title: BasePaginationFilterSchema
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSchema

Base filter schema for paginated list endpoints.

Subclass it to add domain-specific filter fields. The base get_conditions method returns every populated field except the pagination/sort keys, which is the contract expected by :class:tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.repository.BaseRepository.paginate.

Field names and defaults mirror the BaseRepository.paginate keyword arguments so passing the schema straight through works without renaming:

.. code-block:: python

result = await repo.paginate(
    filters=f.get_conditions(),
    order_by=f.order_by,
    page=f.page,
    page_size=f.page_size,
    ascending=f.ascending,
)

Attributes:

Name Type Description page int

The page number to retrieve (1-indexed).

page_size int

The number of items per page.

order_by str | None

The column name to order by. None falls back to the repository default (created_at descending).

ascending bool

Whether to order ascending. Ignored when order_by is None.

is_active bool | None

Filter by active status. None returns both active and inactive rows.

orderable_columns ClassVar[frozenset[str] | None]

The columns order_by accepts. None (the default) accepts any value and leaves the check to the repository; a declared set turns every other value into :class:OrderByNotAllowedException (422, details["allowed"] listing only this set). An empty order_by means "absent" and is never refused.

max_page_size ClassVar[int | None]

Inclusive ceiling on page_size (default :data:DEFAULT_MAX_PAGE_SIZE). Declaring it on a subclass rewrites the field's le= bound, so the refusal is pydantic's own less_than_equal and the OpenAPI parameter shows the maximum. None removes the ceiling. A subclass that redeclares page_size without declaring max_page_size keeps the bound it wrote.

Declaring both on a listing:

.. code-block:: python

class ProducerFilterSchema(BasePaginationFilterSchema):
    orderable_columns = frozenset({"created_at", "name"})
    max_page_size = 50

populate_by_name is on, so a subclass may rename a field on the wire by redeclaring it with an alias and still construct the model by its Python name. See :class:CompactPaginationFilterSchema for the ready-made case.

docs.title: BaseSearchSchema
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSchema

Base request schema for a text-search endpoint.

Searching is an oracle on the searched column (which rows come back says whether each row's value contains the term), so a service that takes fields from the request should declare searchable_columns on the repository and here. The repository refusal is the boundary; this one refuses earlier and documents the accepted columns. The refusal is a :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions.ValidationException, not a pydantic ValueError, so it reaches the client as the SDK's 422 envelope only with :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.register_exception_handlers installed. Only the class-level searchable_columns of a repository can be mirrored: one passed to the repository's constructor has to be repeated here.

Declare the same set on both sides:

.. code-block:: python

class ProductRepository(BaseRepository[ProductModel]):
    searchable_columns = frozenset({"name", "sku"})

class ProductSearchSchema(BaseSearchSchema):
    searchable_columns = ProductRepository.searchable_columns

rows = await repo.search(body.q, fields=body.fields or ["name"])

Name Type Description q str

The search term, 1 to :data:DEFAULT_MAX_SEARCH_TERM characters.

fields list[str]

The columns fields accepts. None (the default) leaves the check to the repository; a declared set refuses every other name with a ValidationException (422, details={"field": <name>, "allowed": [...]}), the envelope :meth:BaseRepository.search <tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseRepository.search> uses.

Bases: BaseSchema

The JSON body the SDK's exception handlers emit on failure.

Every handler registered by :func:tempest_fastapi_sdk.register_exception_handlers — the :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions.AppException handler, the raw HTTPException 5xx handler and the unhandled-error catch-all — writes this exact shape, so a client parses one envelope for every failure mode.

Its reason to exist is the OpenAPI schema: without a declared model a route can only document that it returns a 409, never what the body looks like. Point responses= at this class (or let :func:tempest_fastapi_sdk.error_responses do it) and the generated client gets the envelope for free.

Structured context about the failure (which id was missing, which field conflicted). Empty when the exception attached none.

Name of the input the failure is about, when the exception names one. Absent from the body — not null — when there is no culprit input, so "field" in body is the check a client makes.

docs.title: EventStream
docs.text:
EventStream(
    *,
    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,
    heartbeat_event: ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None = None,
    max_queue: int = 1000,
    overflow: OverflowPolicy = "drop_oldest",
)

Async in-memory queue feeding one SSE HTTP connection.

A handler builds one stream per client request, publish-es events from anywhere in the application (background tasks, websockets, dependency callbacks), and passes :meth:stream to :func:sse_response. A None enqueued by :meth:close terminates the iteration so the response completes cleanly.

Heartbeats are emitted when the queue stays empty for longer than heartbeat_seconds; this keeps load-balancers from closing idle TCP connections. By default the beat is an SSE comment (: keepalive), which the browser never surfaces to JavaScript. Pass heartbeat_event to send a real event instead, for a client that watches the beat to know the connection is alive.

Backpressure. The internal queue is bounded (max_queue) so a slow or stalled client cannot make a busy producer grow the queue without limit and exhaust memory. When the queue fills, the overflow policy decides what gives — evict the oldest event (default), drop the incoming one, or block the producer. The :meth:close sentinel always gets through, evicting a queued event if that is the only way to fit. :attr:dropped_events counts every event lost to overflow so you can surface it in metrics / logs.

Attributes:

Name Type Description heartbeat_seconds float | None

Idle interval that triggers a heartbeat. None disables heartbeats.

heartbeat_event ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None

What the heartbeat puts on the wire. None keeps the comment frame.

max_queue int

Maximum number of buffered events. 0 disables the bound (unbounded — pre-0.91 behavior).

overflow OverflowPolicy

What happens when the queue is full.

Initialize the stream.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default heartbeat_seconds float | None

Idle interval before a heartbeat is emitted.

15.0 heartbeat_event ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None

The frame the heartbeat emits. None (the default) emits ServerSentEvent(comment="keepalive"), which keeps the connection warm without waking the browser. Pass a :class:ServerSentEvent to make the beat visible to the client instead — a comment does not fire onmessage, so a client that treats the beat as proof of a live connection has nothing to listen for. def __init__(
    self,
    *,
    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,
    heartbeat_event: ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None = None,
    max_queue: int = 1000,
    overflow: OverflowPolicy = "drop_oldest",
) -> None:
    """Initialize the stream.

    Args:
        heartbeat_seconds (float | None): Idle interval before
            a heartbeat is emitted.
        heartbeat_event (ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None):
            The frame the heartbeat emits. ``None`` (the default)
            emits ``ServerSentEvent(comment="keepalive")``, which
            keeps the connection warm without waking the browser.
            Pass a :class:`ServerSentEvent` to make the beat visible
            to the client instead — a comment does **not** fire
            ``onmessage``, so a client that treats the beat as proof
            of a live connection has nothing to listen for. Pass a
            callable to build a fresh frame per beat, which is what
            stamping a timestamp into the payload needs.
        max_queue (int): Maximum buffered events before ``overflow``
            kicks in. ``0`` disables the bound. Defaults to ``1000``.
        overflow (OverflowPolicy): Overflow reaction. Defaults to
            ``"drop_oldest"``.

    Notes:
        Only ``"block"`` gets a hard-bounded queue, because only it wants
        real backpressure. The drop policies keep an unbounded queue and
        enforce the bound by hand on data events, which is what keeps the
        close sentinel from ever being blocked or evicted — the stream can
        always be terminated.
    """
    native_maxsize: int = (
        max_queue if (max_queue > 0 and overflow == "block") else 0
    )
    self._queue: asyncio.Queue[ServerSentEvent | None] = asyncio.Queue(
        maxsize=native_maxsize,
    )
    self.heartbeat_seconds: float | None = heartbeat_seconds
    self.heartbeat_event: ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None = (
        heartbeat_event
    )
    self.max_queue: int = max_queue
    self.overflow: OverflowPolicy = overflow
    self._dropped: int = 0

async def stream(self) -> AsyncIterator[bytes]:
    """Yield encoded SSE bytes until :meth:`close` is invoked.

    Yields:
        bytes: An encoded SSE frame ready to write to the wire.
    """
    while True:
        event: ServerSentEvent | None
        if self.heartbeat_seconds is not None:
            try:
                event = await asyncio.wait_for(
                    self._queue.get(),
                    timeout=self.heartbeat_seconds,
                )
            except TimeoutError:
                yield self._heartbeat_frame().encode().encode("utf-8")
                continue
        else:
            event = await self._queue.get()
        if event is None:
            return
        yield event.encode().encode("utf-8")

    self,
    *,
    redis: Redis | None = None,
    channel_prefix: str = _DEFAULT_CHANNEL_PREFIX,
    heartbeat_seconds: float | None = 15.0,
    heartbeat_event: ServerSentEvent | Callable[[], ServerSentEvent] | None = None,
    max_queue: int = 1000,
    overflow: OverflowPolicy = "drop_oldest",

    """Initialize the broker.

    Args:
        redis (Redis | None): Async Redis client (from the ``[cache]``
            extra). ``None`` runs single-process (local fan-out only).
        channel_prefix (str): Prefix for Redis channels. In Redis mode
            give every service its own value (for example
            ``"orders-api:sse"``): Redis pub/sub is shared by every
            client of the instance regardless of the DB index, so the
            prefix is the only thing that keeps one service's events out
            of another's streams. A nested prefix (``app`` next to
            ``app:chat``) is safe since 0.340.0: the ``"<prefix>:*"``
            pattern still receives the longer prefix's messages, but each
            envelope carries the prefix that published it and the
            receiver drops the ones that are not its own. Defaults to
            ``"sse"``, which is kept for
            compatibility; with a Redis client it logs a warning naming
            the risk rather than failing, so existing single-service
            deployments keep working unchanged.

            comment. Set it here rather than subclassing: this is the
            only place a stream is constructed, so a service that
            needs a visible beat has no other seam.

            :meth:`register`. ``0`` disables the bound. Defaults to

            "Redis. Redis pub/sub ignores the DB index, so any other "

def register(self, channel: str) -> EventStream:
    """Open a local stream subscribed to ``channel`` and track it.

    Args:
        channel (str): The logical channel (e.g. a user id or topic).

    Returns:
        EventStream: A fresh stream to hand to
        :func:`tempest_fastapi_sdk.sse_response`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``channel`` is :data:`BROADCAST_CHANNEL`,
            which :meth:`broadcast` reserves.
    """
    _reject_reserved(channel)
    stream = EventStream(
        heartbeat_seconds=self.heartbeat_seconds,
        heartbeat_event=self.heartbeat_event,
        max_queue=self.max_queue,
        overflow=self.overflow,
    )
    self._channels.setdefault(channel, set()).add(stream)
    return stream

    self,
    channel: str,
    *,
    status_code: int = 200,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Subscribe to ``channel`` and return the SSE response in one call.

    Bundles the whole per-connection lifecycle: :meth:`register` opens
    a local stream, :func:`tempest_fastapi_sdk.sse_response` wraps it,
    and an ``on_disconnect`` hook calls :meth:`unregister` when the
    client goes away. This removes the hand-rolled ``try/finally``
    wrapper — forgetting which used to leak a stream per disconnect.

        status_code (int): HTTP status. Defaults to ``200``.

def unregister(self, channel: str, stream: EventStream) -> None:
    """Drop a closed stream from ``channel``.

    Call this from the response generator's ``finally`` so a
    disconnected client is forgotten.

    Args:
        channel (str): The channel the stream was registered under.
        stream (EventStream): The stream to remove.
    """
    streams = self._channels.get(channel)
    if streams:
        streams.discard(stream)
        if not streams:
            del self._channels[channel]

async def publish(
    self,
    channel: str,
    data: SSEData = "",
    *,
    event: str | None = None,
    id: str | None = None,
    retry: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Publish an event to every subscriber of ``channel``.

    In Redis mode the event is ``PUBLISH``-ed and delivered to all
    workers (including this one) by their :meth:`run` loop. In
    single-process mode it fans out to local streams immediately.

    Args:
        channel (str): Target channel.
        data (SSEData): Payload (string, bytes or JSON-serializable).
        event (str | None): Optional SSE event name.
        id (str | None): Optional ``Last-Event-ID``.
        retry (int | None): Optional reconnect hint (ms).

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``channel`` is :data:`BROADCAST_CHANNEL`,
            which :meth:`broadcast` reserves.
    """
    _reject_reserved(channel)
    if self._redis is None:
        await self._emit_local(
            channel,
            ServerSentEvent(data=data, event=event, id=id, retry=retry),
        )
        return
    envelope = self._envelope(data, event=event, id=id, retry=retry)
    await self._redis.publish(self._key(channel), envelope)

async def broadcast(
    self,
    data: SSEData = "",
    *,
    event: str | None = None,
    id: str | None = None,
    retry: int | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Publish an event to every subscriber of every channel.

    The axis :meth:`publish` does not cover: one event to N channels
    instead of one channel to N connections. This is the global notice —
    "maintenance in 5 minutes", "a new version is available" — that a
    service otherwise has to fake by keeping its own registry of open
    channels alongside the broker's.

    In Redis mode the event is ``PUBLISH``-ed under
    :data:`BROADCAST_CHANNEL`, which the ``<prefix>:*`` pattern every
    worker already subscribes to reaches without any new subscription;
    each worker's :meth:`run` loop then fans it to **all** of its local
    streams. In single-process mode it fans out locally right away.

    A stream registered under more than one channel — which
    :meth:`register` does not produce, but a caller holding a stream can
    arrange — receives the event once: the fan-out is over the set of
    streams, not the list of channels.

    Args:
        data (SSEData): Payload (string, bytes or JSON-serializable).
        event (str | None): Optional SSE event name.
        id (str | None): Optional ``Last-Event-ID``.
        retry (int | None): Optional reconnect hint (ms).

    frame = ServerSentEvent(data=data, event=event, id=id, retry=retry)
    if self._redis is None:
        await self._emit_everywhere(frame)
        return
    envelope = self._envelope(data, event=event, id=id, retry=retry)
    await self._redis.publish(self._key(BROADCAST_CHANNEL), envelope)

Long-running: start it as a background task in the app lifespan and cancel it (or call :meth:aclose) on shutdown. A no-op in single-process mode.

Each message is dispatched in isolation. The <prefix>:* pattern receives whatever any client of the Redis instance publishes on a matching channel, not only this broker's envelopes, so a frame that fails to decode or to fan out is logged (channel and error type, never the payload) and skipped. async def run(self) -> None:
    """Consume Redis pub/sub and fan messages to local streams.

    Long-running: start it as a background task in the app lifespan
    and cancel it (or call :meth:`aclose`) on shutdown. A no-op in
    single-process mode.

    Each message is dispatched in isolation. The ``<prefix>:*`` pattern
    receives whatever any client of the Redis instance publishes on a
    matching channel, not only this broker's envelopes, so a frame that
    fails to decode or to fan out is logged (channel and error type,
    never the payload) and skipped. Letting it escape would end the
    loop, and with it every later delivery to this worker's streams,
    while the worker kept accepting connections.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If called without a Redis client.
    """
    if self._redis is None:
        raise RuntimeError("SSEBroker.run() requires a Redis client.")
    pubsub: Any = self._redis.pubsub()
    self._pubsub = pubsub
    await pubsub.psubscribe(f"{self.channel_prefix}:*")
    try:
        async for message in pubsub.listen():
            if message.get("type") != "pmessage":
                continue
            try:
                await self._dispatch_raw(message["channel"], message["data"])
            except Exception as exc:
                _LOGGER.warning(
                    "SSEBroker skipped an undeliverable pub/sub message on %r: %s",
                    message.get("channel"),
                    type(exc).__name__,
                )
    finally:
        await pubsub.aclose()
        self._pubsub = None

Render the event as the wire-format string.

A frame that carries no payload and no event name, but does carry comment, id or retry, is a control frame: it gets no data: line at all. That line is what makes the browser dispatch, even when it looks empty — data: parses to a data buffer holding a single line feed, and the dispatch step strips that feed and delivers the empty string as a message event. Writing it therefore turned the idle : keepalive heartbeat into an event that every consumer listening on onmessage received as business data. Measured in Chromium over EventSource: : keepalive\ndata: \n\n fires onmessage, : keepalive\n\n fires nothing.

A frame that names an event keeps its data: line when the payload is empty, because a named event with an empty body is meant to dispatch; so does a bare ServerSentEvent().

def encode(self) -> str:
    """Render the event as the wire-format string.

    A frame that carries no payload and no ``event`` name, but does
    carry ``comment``, ``id`` or ``retry``, is a **control frame**:
    it gets no ``data:`` line at all. That line is what makes the
    browser dispatch, even when it looks empty — ``data: `` parses to
    a data buffer holding a single line feed, and the dispatch step
    strips that feed and delivers the empty string as a ``message``
    event. Writing it therefore turned the idle ``: keepalive``
    heartbeat into an event that every consumer listening on
    ``onmessage`` received as business data. Measured in Chromium
    over ``EventSource``: ``: keepalive\\ndata: \\n\\n`` fires
    ``onmessage``, ``: keepalive\\n\\n`` fires nothing.

    A frame that names an ``event`` keeps its ``data:`` line when the
    payload is empty, because a named event with an empty body is
    meant to dispatch; so does a bare ``ServerSentEvent()``.

    Returns:
        str: The encoded event, including the trailing blank line
        that marks frame boundaries.
    """
    lines: list[str] = []
    if self.comment is not None:
        lines.append(f": {self.comment}")
    if self.event is not None:
        lines.append(f"event: {self.event}")
    if self.id is not None:
        lines.append(f"id: {self.id}")
    if self.retry is not None:
        lines.append(f"retry: {self.retry}")

    payload: str
    if isinstance(self.data, bytes):
        payload = self.data.decode("utf-8")
    elif isinstance(self.data, str):
        payload = self.data
    else:
        payload = json.dumps(self.data, default=str)

    is_control_frame: bool = (
        payload == ""
        and self.event is None
        and (
            self.comment is not None
            or self.id is not None
            or self.retry is not None
        )
    )
    if not is_control_frame:
        for chunk in payload.splitlines() or [""]:
            lines.append(f"data: {chunk}")
    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"

Adds the SSE-specific headers (Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive, X-Accel-Buffering: no) so intermediate proxies don't buffer or cache the long-lived response. Pass on_disconnect to run cleanup when the client goes away — the response generator's finally is the one place guaranteed to fire on disconnect, so this is where you cancel a bound producer task or call :meth:SSEBroker.unregister. It removes the hand-rolled try/finally wrapper the recipe used to require.

def sse_response(
    stream: AsyncIterable[bytes],
    *,
    status_code: int = 200,
    headers: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    on_disconnect: Callable[[], object] | None = None,
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Wrap ``stream`` in a Starlette ``text/event-stream`` response.

    Adds the SSE-specific headers (``Cache-Control: no-cache``,
    ``Connection: keep-alive``, ``X-Accel-Buffering: no``) so
    intermediate proxies don't buffer or cache the long-lived
    response. Caller-supplied ``headers`` are layered **below** the
    SSE defaults so the three critical headers above cannot be
    accidentally overridden — pass extra metadata, not replacements.

    Pass ``on_disconnect`` to run cleanup when the client goes away —
    the response generator's ``finally`` is the one place guaranteed to
    fire on disconnect, so this is where you cancel a bound producer
    task or call :meth:`SSEBroker.unregister`. It removes the
    hand-rolled ``try/finally`` wrapper the recipe used to require.

    Args:
        stream (AsyncIterable[bytes]): The byte stream produced by
            :meth:`EventStream.stream` (or any compatible generator).
        status_code (int): HTTP status code. Defaults to ``200``.
        headers (dict[str, str] | None): Extra headers to attach.
        on_disconnect (Callable[[], object] | None): Cleanup callback
            run (and awaited if it returns an awaitable) when the stream
            ends or the client disconnects. ``None`` skips it.

    Returns:
        StreamingResponse: A ready-to-return SSE response.
    """
    merged: dict[str, str] = {**(headers or {}), **_SSE_HEADERS}
    body: AsyncIterable[bytes] = (
        stream if on_disconnect is None else _guard_stream(stream, on_disconnect)
    )
    return StreamingResponse(
        body,
        media_type="text/event-stream",
        status_code=status_code,
        headers=merged,
    )

Mounts two routes:

  • POST <prefix>/ticket — guarded by current_user; answers a :class:SSETicketResponseSchema whose ticket opens the channel channel_for(user).

def make_sse_router(
    broker: SSEBroker | Callable[[Request], SSEBroker],
    *,
    tokens: JWTUtils | Callable[[Request], JWTUtils],
    current_user: Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]],
    fallback_user: Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] | None = None,
    channel_for: Callable[[Any], str] | None = None,
    prefix: str = "/sse",
    tag: str = "SSE",
    ticket_ttl: timedelta | None = None,
    ticket_param: str = "ticket",
    docs_locale: str | None = None,
) -> APIRouter:
    """Build the router that issues SSE tickets and serves the stream.

    Mounts two routes:

    * ``POST <prefix>/ticket`` — guarded by ``current_user``; answers a
      :class:`SSETicketResponseSchema` whose ticket opens the channel
      ``channel_for(user)``.
    * ``GET <prefix>/stream`` — reads ``?<ticket_param>=``, checks the
      signature, the expiry and ``typ="stream"``, and returns
      ``broker.response(channel)``. Without a ticket it asks
      ``fallback_user``; with neither it answers ``401``.

    The channel travels **inside** the signed ticket, so the stream route
    opens no database session and the client cannot pick a channel of
    its own. A deactivated account stops getting tickets at once (that is
    ``current_user``'s check) and loses the stream on its next reconnect.

    With :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.UserAuthService`, prefer
    :meth:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.UserAuthService.sse_router`, which builds
    ``tokens``, ``current_user`` and ``fallback_user`` from the service.

    Args:
        broker (SSEBroker | Callable[[Request], SSEBroker]): The broker the
            stream subscribes to, or a factory called with each request
            that returns it (``lambda request: request.app.state.broker``).
        tokens (JWTUtils | Callable[[Request], JWTUtils]): The helper that
            signs and verifies tickets — the same one that signs the
            access token, or a factory returning it.
        current_user (Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]]): The
            dependency that authenticates ``POST <prefix>/ticket`` and
            yields the user, raising on a missing or invalid session.
        fallback_user (Callable[..., Coroutine[Any, Any, Any]] | None): A
            **soft** user dependency the stream route asks when no ticket
            came — it returns ``None`` instead of raising. Lets a client
            that can send ``Authorization: Bearer`` skip the ticket, and,
            built with ``query_param``, keeps an existing
            ``?access_token=`` client working while it migrates. ``None``
            (default) makes the ticket the only way in.
        channel_for (Callable[[Any], str] | None): Maps the authenticated
            user to the broker channel. ``None`` (default) uses
            ``str(user.id)``.
        prefix (str): URL prefix. Defaults to ``"/sse"``.
        tag (str): OpenAPI tag. Defaults to ``"SSE"``.
        ticket_ttl (timedelta | None): Lifetime of a ticket. ``None``
            (default) uses :data:`DEFAULT_SSE_TICKET_TTL` (60 seconds).
        ticket_param (str): Query parameter the stream route reads the
            ticket from. Defaults to ``"ticket"``.
        docs_locale (str | None): Language of the OpenAPI ``summary``
            and ``description`` text — ``"en-US"`` or ``"pt-BR"``.
            ``None`` (default) reads ``API_DOCS_LOCALE`` through
            :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.ServerSettings`,
            whose default is ``"en-US"``.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: The router, ready for ``app.include_router``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When ``ticket_ttl`` is shorter than one second.
    """
    resolved_channel_for = channel_for if channel_for is not None else _user_id_channel
    resolved_ttl = ticket_ttl if ticket_ttl is not None else DEFAULT_SSE_TICKET_TTL
    ttl_seconds = int(resolved_ttl.total_seconds())
    if ttl_seconds < 1:
        raise ValueError("ticket_ttl must be at least one second.")

    def resolve_broker(request: Request) -> SSEBroker:
        """Return the broker for this request.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.

        Returns:
            SSEBroker: ``broker`` itself, or what its factory returns.
        """
        if isinstance(broker, SSEBroker):
            return broker
        return broker(request)

    route_docs: RouteDocs = RouteDocs(docs_locale)
    router = APIRouter(prefix=prefix, tags=[tag])

    @router.post(
        "/ticket",
        response_model=SSETicketResponseSchema,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sse.issue_ticket"),
        description=route_docs.description(
            "sse.issue_ticket", prefix=prefix, ticket_param=ticket_param
        ),
    )
    async def issue_ticket(
        request: Request,
        user: Any = Depends(current_user),
    ) -> SSETicketResponseSchema:
        """Sign a ticket for the caller's channel.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.
            user (Any): The authenticated user.

        Returns:
            SSETicketResponseSchema: The ticket and its lifetime.
        """
        ticket = _resolve_tokens(tokens, request).encode(
            {"typ": STREAM_TOKEN_TYPE, SSE_CHANNEL_CLAIM: resolved_channel_for(user)},
            ttl=timedelta(seconds=ttl_seconds),
        )
        return SSETicketResponseSchema(ticket=ticket, expires_in=ttl_seconds)

    @router.get(
        "/stream",
        response_class=StreamingResponse,
        summary=route_docs.summary("sse.stream"),
        description=route_docs.description(
            "sse.stream", prefix=prefix, ticket_param=ticket_param
        ),
    )
    async def stream(
        request: Request,
        fallback: Any = Depends(fallback_user or _no_fallback_user),
    ) -> StreamingResponse:
        """Subscribe the caller to the channel its credential names.

        Args:
            request (Request): The request being served.
            fallback (Any): What ``fallback_user`` resolved, or ``None``.

        Returns:
            StreamingResponse: The SSE response.

        Raises:
            UnauthorizedException: When the ticket is absent, expired,
                forged or of another ``typ``, and no fallback user
                resolved.
        """
        ticket = request.query_params.get(ticket_param)
        if ticket is not None:
            payload = _resolve_tokens(tokens, request).decode_or_none(ticket)
            channel = None if payload is None else payload.get(SSE_CHANNEL_CLAIM)
            if (
                payload is None
                or payload.get("typ") != STREAM_TOKEN_TYPE
                or not isinstance(channel, str)
            ):
                raise UnauthorizedException(message=SSE_TICKET_ERROR)
        elif fallback is not None:
            channel = resolved_channel_for(fallback)
        else:
            raise UnauthorizedException(message=SSE_TICKET_ERROR)
        return resolve_broker(request).response(channel)

    return router

docs.title: SSETicketResponseSchema
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSchema

A ticket that opens one SSE stream.

The ticket goes in the stream URL (?ticket=...) because the browser EventSource cannot send a header. It is a JWT with typ="stream": every guard built on :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.token_type_allowed refuses it, so a ticket copied out of an access log opens that one stream until it expires and calls nothing else. It is not single-use: until it expires it opens the stream every time it is presented.

The signed ticket to pass as the stream's query parameter.

expires_in int

Seconds until the ticket can no longer open a stream. A stream already open is not cut when it expires; a reconnect after it needs a new ticket.

async def paginate(
    self,
    filters: dict[str, Any] | None = None,
    order_by: str | None = None,
    page: int = 1,
    page_size: int = 20,
    ascending: bool = True,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Return an offset page with items mapped to responses.

    Args:
        filters (dict[str, Any] | None): Column name to the value it must match,
            ANDed together, e.g. ``{"user_id": 1234, "is_active": True}``. A
            list is ``IN``, ``None`` is ``IS NULL``, and a ``<column>__<op>``
            key applies an operator (``{"price__gte": 10}``); every convention
            is listed on :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseRepository`.
            An unknown column or operator raises ``UnknownFilterKeyException``.
        order_by (str | None): Column name to order by.
        page (int): 1-indexed page number.
        page_size (int): Items per page.
        ascending (bool): Whether to order ascending.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Any]: Mapping with ``items`` (mapped),
        ``total``, ``page``, ``size`` and ``pages``.
    """
    result = await self.repository.paginate(
        filters=filters,
        order_by=order_by,
        page=page,
        page_size=page_size,
        ascending=ascending,
    )
    items = [await self._map_to_response(i) for i in result["items"]]

async def update(self, id: UUID, data: UpdateT) -> ResponseT:
    """Apply a partial update to a record and map it to a response.

    Fetches the row by primary key, copies the fields present in
    ``data`` onto the instance, persists, and returns the mapped
    response. Because :meth:`BaseSchema.to_dict` drops unset and
    ``None`` fields, only the values the caller actually supplied are
    applied — so the same method serves both full (PUT) and partial
    (PATCH) updates.

    Override this in a concrete service when an update needs
    orchestration (cross-repository writes, domain rules, side
    effects); leave it untouched for plain field copies.

    Args:
        id (UUID): The primary key of the record to update.
        data (UpdateT): The update payload (a :class:`BaseSchema`).
            Fields left unset (or ``None``) are not applied.

    Returns:
        ResponseT: The mapped, updated response.

    Raises:
        AppException: ``repository.not_found_exception`` when no
            record with ``id`` exists.
        ConflictException: On integrity violations while persisting.
    """
    instance = await self.repository.get_by_id(id)
    for field, value in data.to_dict().items():
        setattr(instance, field, value)
    updated = await self.repository.update(instance)
    return await self._map_to_response(updated)

Bases: Generic[ModelType]

Manage a single object-storage key field on a service's model.

Mix into a service that already owns a repository (e.g. a :class:tempest_fastapi_sdk.BaseService subclass) and exposes an upload_utils and a storage collaborator::

class UserService(
    BaseService[UserRepository, UserResponseSchema],
    StoredFileServiceMixin[UserModel],
):
    def __init__(self, repository, storage, upload_utils):
        super().__init__(repository)
        self.storage = storage
        self.upload_utils = upload_utils

user = await service.set_file(
    user, image, field="profile_picture", subdir="profiles"
)
url = await service.file_url(user.profile_picture)

The mixin does not construct its collaborators — it reads them off self so the owning service stays in charge of configuration (size limits, allowed types, bucket).

async def set_file(
    self,
    ref: UUID | ModelType,
    file: UploadFile,
    *,
    field: str,
    subdir: str = "",
    filename: str | None = None,
    keep_original_name: bool = False,
) -> ModelType:
    """Upload ``file`` and store its key on ``field``, replacing any old one.

    The new object is written **before** the old one is deleted (via
    :meth:`SupportsUpload.replace`), so a failed upload leaves the
    existing file untouched. The entity is re-resolved on the
    repository's session first, so a detached instance (e.g. the
    authenticated user) is safely re-attached before the write.

    Args:
        ref (UUID | ModelType): The entity to update, by id or instance.
        file (UploadFile): The uploaded file.
        field (str): Name of the model attribute holding the storage key.
        subdir (str): Optional key prefix / sub-directory.
        filename (str | None): Explicit final filename. When omitted the
            upload helper derives one.
        keep_original_name (bool): Preserve the upload's original
            filename when ``filename`` is not given.

    Returns:
        ModelType: The persisted entity with the new key on ``field``.

    Raises:
        AppException: ``repository.not_found_exception`` when ``ref`` is
            an id with no matching row.
    """
    entity: ModelType = await self.repository.resolve(ref)
    old_key: Any = getattr(entity, field)
    new_key = await self.upload_utils.replace(
        old_key,
        file,
        subdir=subdir,
        filename=filename,
        keep_original_name=keep_original_name,
    )
    setattr(entity, field, str(new_key))
    updated: ModelType = await self.repository.update(entity)
    return updated

    self,
    ref: UUID | ModelType,
    *,
    field: str,

    A no-op write is avoided when the field is already empty: the
    resolved entity is returned without a commit.

        ref (UUID | ModelType): The entity to update, by id or instance.
        field (str): Name of the model attribute holding the storage key.

        only when there was a key to clear).

    Raises:
        AppException: ``repository.not_found_exception`` when ``ref`` is
            an id with no matching row.

    entity: ModelType = await self.repository.resolve(ref)
    old_key: Any = getattr(entity, field)

    await self.upload_utils.delete(old_key)
    setattr(entity, field, None)
    updated: ModelType = await self.repository.update(entity)
    return updated

async def file_urls(
    self,
    keys: Iterable[str | None],
    *,
    expires: timedelta = _DEFAULT_URL_TTL,
    max_concurrency: int = 16,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Return presigned download URLs for many keys at once.

    The batch counterpart of :meth:`file_url` for list endpoints that
    must resolve one stored key per row (e.g. a page of profiles).
    Presigning is dispatched concurrently by the storage client, so a
    page of N rows costs one bounded fan-out instead of N sequential
    round-trips. Empty / ``None`` keys are dropped and duplicates are
    collapsed, so the result holds one entry per distinct non-empty
    key — look each row's URL up with ``result.get(row.key)``, which
    yields ``None`` for a row whose key was empty.

    Args:
        keys (Iterable[str | None]): The stored object keys, typically
            one field value per row. ``None`` / empty entries are
            skipped.
        expires (timedelta): URL lifetime for every key. Defaults to
            one hour.
        max_concurrency (int): Maximum signings awaited at once.

    Returns:
        dict[str, str]: Mapping of each distinct non-empty key to its
        presigned download URL.
    """
    valid = [key for key in keys if key]
    if not valid:
        return {}
    return await self.storage.presigned_get_urls(
        valid, expires=expires, max_concurrency=max_concurrency
    )

docs.title: Controller
docs.text:
Root of the controller layer, for controllers that orchestrate.

Subclass it when a controller coordinates several services — under one lock, one commit, one audit entry — and has no CRUD of a single resource to pass through. It ships no methods on purpose: inheriting :class:BaseController there would hand the router get_by_id, update and delete methods that mean nothing for that controller.

What it fixes is the convention of the layer, the same one :class:BaseController follows:

  • services are injected through __init__ (built by a FastAPI dependency provider, never inside the controller);
  • the controller never touches the database — no session, no repository, no engine. Persistence goes through the services it receives.

The convention is not checked at runtime: the constructor belongs to the subclass, and telling a service from a repository by annotation would need the subclass's forward references resolved.

Examples:

>>> from tempest_fastapi_sdk import Controller
>>> class BillingController(Controller):
...     def __init__(self, invoices: object, ledger: object) -> None:
...         self.invoices: object = invoices
...         self.ledger: object = ledger
>>> isinstance(BillingController(object(), object()), Controller)
True

Thin orchestration layer between routers and one CRUD service.

The CRUD specialization of :class:Controller: it takes a single service and passes its CRUD methods through. For a controller that orchestrates several services without single-resource CRUD, subclass :class:Controller instead.

Following the SDK layering rules (router → controller → service → repository), controllers are kept present even when no orchestration is required so the import graph stays uniform. Override methods here when a single endpoint needs to call multiple services or apply cross-cutting policy; leave the pass-throughs untouched otherwise.

docs.title: BaseAppSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseSettings

Shared configuration for Settings classes across projects.

Provides the canonical pydantic-settings config block; concrete projects subclass this and add their domain-specific fields (database URLs, secrets, third-party keys, etc.).

Every SDK settings mixin (DatabaseSettings, RedisSettings, …) subclasses this class, so a composed Settings must list BaseAppSettings last::

class Settings(DatabaseSettings, RedisSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ...

Listing it earlier is an invalid MRO and fails at class creation with the actionable message raised by :class:AppSettingsMeta.

The defaults:

  • env_file=".env" — load environment variables from a local .env file when present.
  • extra="ignore" — silently drop unexpected env vars instead of raising at startup.
  • case_sensitive=True — env var names are matched exactly.
  • frozen=True — settings are immutable after construction.
  • str_strip_whitespace=True — trim accidental whitespace around env values.
  • from_attributes=True — allow building from objects with attribute access (rarely needed for settings, but harmless).
  • hide_input_in_errors=True — a validation error never echoes the input. On a BaseSettings the input of a model-level error is the whole merged environment: without this flag a missing required field prints input_value={'JWT_SECRET': ...} into the boot traceback and the container log, and a malformed value (a URL carrying a password) is echoed as is. Override it in your own model_config to get the input back.

Three extension points live here because every mixin needs them:

  • :meth:production_violations — the cooperative hook :class:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.EnvironmentSettings calls when ENV=production. Each mixin overrides it, calls super() and appends the development values it owns.
  • :meth:disabled_integrations — the same cooperative shape, for the integrations a <NAME>_ENABLED flag switched off.

docs.text:
Bases: ModelMetaclass

Metaclass that validates the position of settings bases.

Every settings mixin the SDK ships subclasses :class:BaseAppSettings, so C3 linearization forbids BaseAppSettings from preceding a mixin in the base list. Python already rejects that, but the message it emits (Cannot create a consistent method resolution order (MRO) for bases BaseAppSettings, RedisSettings) never names the fix, and under the pydantic mypy plugin the same line also reports a misleading [metaclass] error. This metaclass pre-checks the base ordering and raises an instruction instead.

    settings_cls: type[BaseSettings], sources: tuple[PydanticBaseSettingsSource, ...]

Refuse a deprecated env var set next to its replacement.

A renamed field reads both names through validation_alias=AliasChoices(new, old), and AliasChoices resolves a clash by taking the first name it finds. Left alone, STORAGE_SECRET_KEY set by the new deploy script and a stale MINIO_SECRET_KEY in the .env would both look configured while only one of them reaches the client. Setting both names to the same value is accepted, so a deploy can carry the two during a migration window.

Values are compared as the raw strings the sources read, across the environment and the .env file together: the old name in one and the new name in the other still counts as a clash.

When at least one pair clashes. The message names every clashing pair and never includes a value.

def reject_conflicting_env_aliases(
    settings_cls: type[BaseSettings],
    sources: tuple[PydanticBaseSettingsSource, ...],
) -> None:
    """Refuse a deprecated env var set next to its replacement.

    A renamed field reads both names through
    ``validation_alias=AliasChoices(new, old)``, and ``AliasChoices``
    resolves a clash by taking the first name it finds. Left alone,
    ``STORAGE_SECRET_KEY`` set by the new deploy script and a stale
    ``MINIO_SECRET_KEY`` in the ``.env`` would both look configured
    while only one of them reaches the client. Setting both names to
    the **same** value is accepted, so a deploy can carry the two during
    a migration window.

    Values are compared as the raw strings the sources read, across the
    environment and the ``.env`` file together: the old name in one and
    the new name in the other still counts as a clash.

    Args:
        settings_cls (type[BaseSettings]): The settings class being
            built; its MRO supplies ``DEPRECATED_ENV_ALIASES``.
        sources (tuple[PydanticBaseSettingsSource, ...]): The sources to
            inspect. Only environment-backed ones
            (``EnvSettingsSource`` and its ``.env`` subclass) are read.

    Raises:
        SettingsError: When at least one pair clashes. The message names
            every clashing pair and never includes a value.
    """
    aliases: dict[str, str] = _deprecated_env_aliases(settings_cls)
    if not aliases:
        return
    clashes: list[str] = []
    for old, new in aliases.items():
        old_value: str | None = None
        new_value: str | None = None
        for source in sources:
            if not isinstance(source, EnvSettingsSource):
                continue
            fold: bool = not source.case_sensitive
            env_vars: Mapping[str, str | None] = source.env_vars
            if old_value is None:
                old_value = env_vars.get(old.lower() if fold else old)
            if new_value is None:
                new_value = env_vars.get(new.lower() if fold else new)
        if old_value is not None and new_value is not None and old_value != new_value:
            clashes.append(f"{new} and {old}")
    if clashes:
        raise SettingsError(
            "Conflicting environment variables: "
            + "; ".join(clashes)
            + ". Each pair is one setting under its current and its "
            "deprecated name, set to different values. Remove the "
            "deprecated name (the second of each pair) from the "
            "environment and the .env file."
        )

def read_project_version(pyproject_path: Path | None = None) -> str:
    """Return the project version declared in a ``pyproject.toml``.

    With no argument the search starts at the current working directory
    and walks up to the filesystem root, stopping at the first
    ``pyproject.toml`` it finds — the same resolution ``find_pyproject``
    uses. Pass an explicit ``pyproject_path`` when the answer must not
    depend on the working directory: the scaffolded settings module
    anchors it on its own location, so the version is the project's even
    when the app is started from somewhere else.

    Args:
        pyproject_path (Path | None): The file to read. Defaults to the
            nearest ``pyproject.toml`` above the current working
            directory.

    Returns:
        str: The value of ``[project].version``.

    Raises:
        FileNotFoundError: When no ``pyproject.toml`` is found. The
            message lists every path the search visited, so a miss names
            what it looked for and where.
        ValueError: When the file has no ``[project].version`` — an
            absent ``[project]`` table, an absent key, or a project that
            declares the version through ``dynamic``. The message names
            the file and the missing key.
    """
    if pyproject_path is None:
        candidates = _candidate_paths(Path.cwd())
        pyproject_path = next(
            (candidate for candidate in candidates if candidate.is_file()),
            None,
        )
        if pyproject_path is None:
            searched = "\n".join(f"  - {candidate}" for candidate in candidates)
            raise FileNotFoundError(
                "No pyproject.toml found walking up from "
                f"{Path.cwd().resolve()} to the filesystem root. Searched:\n"
                f"{searched}\nPass pyproject_path explicitly if the file "
                "lives elsewhere."
            )
    elif not pyproject_path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: no such file. Pass a path to an existing "
            "pyproject.toml with [project].version."
        )

    with pyproject_path.open("rb") as handle:
        data = tomllib.load(handle)
    project = data.get("project")
    if not isinstance(project, dict) or VERSION_KEY not in project:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: missing [project].version. Declare "
            'version = "x.y.z" under [project], or point the helper at a '
            "file that does. A project that resolves its version through "
            'dynamic = ["version"] has none to read.'
        )
    version = project[VERSION_KEY]
    if not isinstance(version, str):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{pyproject_path}: [project].version is "
            f"{type(version).__name__}, expected a string."
        )
    return version

docs.title: mixins
docs.text:
Composable settings mixins covering common service dependencies.

Each mixin is a fully-typed Pydantic model with sensible defaults so projects can opt in by listing the mixins they need alongside their own concrete Settings class:

class Settings(DatabaseSettings, RedisSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ...

Every mixin inherits :class:BaseAppSettings (not raw pydantic_settings.BaseSettings), so each one carries the canonical model_config — env_file=".env", extra="ignore", case_sensitive=True — materialized on its own class. This makes the value of .env loading independent of mixin ordering: pydantic materializes a complete model_config onto every settings class, so a mixin listed before BaseAppSettings would otherwise overwrite the whole config (resetting env_file to None) even though it never declared that key. Inheriting BaseAppSettings keeps .env in the materialized config no matter where the mixin sits.

Because the mixins now subclass BaseAppSettings, BaseAppSettings must be the last base of the composed Settings. Listing it before any mixin violates Python's C3 linearization (a base cannot precede its own subclass) and raises TypeError: Cannot create a consistent method resolution order (MRO) at import — so keep BaseAppSettings at the end of the bases, as shown above.

Every field carries title, description and examples so JSON-Schema consumers (FastAPI /docs, /redoc, IDE tooling, pydantic.model_json_schema()) render rich metadata out of the box.

docs.title: EnvironmentSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAppSettings

Deployment environment plus the production guard.

Compose it like any mixin. With ENV=production the settings refuse to build while any composed mixin still holds a development value, listing every offending field at once; with development or test nothing changes::

class Settings(EnvironmentSettings, DatabaseSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ...

What counts as a development value is declared by each mixin in its :meth:~BaseAppSettings.production_violations override, so the guard only checks the mixins the service actually lists:

  • :class:ServerSettings — SERVER_DEBUG or SERVER_RELOAD on.
  • :class:DatabaseSettings — a SQLite DATABASE_URL.
  • :class:JWTSettings — JWT_SECRET equal to the declared placeholder.
  • :class:CORSSettings — "*" in CORS_ORIGINS.
  • :class:TokenSettings — an empty TOKEN_SECRET.
  • :class:TaskIQSettings — an empty TASKIQ_BROKER_URL.
  • :class:StorageSettings — the MinIO default access or secret key, STORAGE_SECURE off, or STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE explicitly off.
  • :class:EmailSettings — a Mailpit/MailHog host, loopback on port 1025, or a placeholder SMTP_FROM_ADDR domain.
  • :class:RevenueCatSettings — both webhook secrets empty.

A third-party integration can be switched off instead of configured (STORAGE_ENABLED, EMAIL_ENABLED, FIREBASE_ENABLED, REVENUECAT_ENABLED set to false): its checks are skipped, the boot succeeds, and :meth:~BaseAppSettings.disabled_integrations names it so the app can log the switch.

The error message names fields and reasons, never values.

ENV has no default. A missing value refuses to build: with a development default, a production host that forgot to set it booted with every development value and the guard never ran.

Name Type Description ENV AppEnvironment

"development", "test" or "production". Required.

    passes ``ENV="test"`` to the constructor) so it never inherits the
    developer's configuration. Without this hook the ``.env`` in the
    working directory was still read, and every value the suite did
    not pin itself -- a real ``DATABASE_URL``, an SMTP host, an API
    key -- leaked into the tests.

    The decision reads only the constructor keyword arguments and the
    process environment, never the ``.env`` itself: ``ENV=test``
    written **in** the ``.env`` sets the field like any other value
    and the file is read as usual, because a source cannot be the
    reason it is discarded. With ``ENV`` resolving to anything else,
    or absent from both, the sources are the ones
    :meth:`BaseAppSettings.settings_customise_sources` returns,
    including the deprecated-alias check.

    A ``Settings`` class that overrides this hook itself replaces the
    behaviour; call ``super().settings_customise_sources(...)`` from
    the override to keep it.

    Args:
        settings_cls (type[BaseSettings]): The class being built.
        init_settings (PydanticBaseSettingsSource): Keyword
            arguments passed to the constructor.
        env_settings (PydanticBaseSettingsSource): The process
            environment.
        dotenv_settings (PydanticBaseSettingsSource): The ``.env``
            file.
        file_secret_settings (PydanticBaseSettingsSource): The
            secrets directory.

    Returns:

        priority order, without ``dotenv_settings`` when the suite
        pinned ``ENV=test``.

    Raises:
        SettingsError: When a deprecated environment variable and
            its replacement are both set to different values.
    """
    explicit: Any = init_settings().get("ENV", env_settings().get("ENV"))
    if isinstance(explicit, str) and explicit.strip() == "test":
        reject_conflicting_env_aliases(settings_cls, (env_settings,))
        return init_settings, env_settings, file_secret_settings
    return super().settings_customise_sources(
        settings_cls,
        init_settings,
        env_settings,
        dotenv_settings,
        file_secret_settings,
    )

CORS middleware configuration.

.. warning:: The default CORS_ORIGINS=["*"] is permissive on purpose so local development works out of the box. Never ship this default to production — set CORS_ORIGINS to the explicit list of trusted frontend origins. Do not combine "*" with CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS=True: Starlette's CORSMiddleware then answers every request with the caller's own Origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true, so every site may make credentialed reads. With ENV=production (:class:EnvironmentSettings) the settings refuse to build in that case, and also when credentials are allowed together with a CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX that accepts arbitrary origins or with the "null" origin. Refuse wildcard and credential-reflecting origins in production.

With CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS=True, Starlette's CORSMiddleware answers an accepted origin with that exact Origin plus Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any rule that accepts origins nobody listed therefore hands credentialed cross-origin reads to arbitrary sites: "*" in CORS_ORIGINS, a CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX that fully matches a reserved .invalid probe origin (:data:_CORS_PROBE_ORIGINS), and the "null" origin that sandboxed iframes and data: documents send. A regex that does not compile is left to the middleware, which raises on it.

def production_violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """Refuse wildcard and credential-reflecting origins in production.

    With ``CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS=True``, Starlette's ``CORSMiddleware``
    answers an accepted origin with that exact ``Origin`` plus
    ``Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true``. Any rule that accepts
    origins nobody listed therefore hands credentialed cross-origin
    reads to arbitrary sites: ``"*"`` in ``CORS_ORIGINS``, a
    ``CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX`` that fully matches a reserved ``.invalid``
    probe origin (:data:`_CORS_PROBE_ORIGINS`), and the ``"null"``
    origin that sandboxed iframes and ``data:`` documents send. A
    regex that does not compile is left to the middleware, which
    raises on it.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The parent's entries plus one per offending rule.
    """
    violations: list[str] = super().production_violations()
    if "*" in self.CORS_ORIGINS:
        violations.append(
            'CORS_ORIGINS: contains "*" (list the trusted frontend origins)'
        )
    if not self.CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS:
        return violations
    if "*" in self.CORS_ORIGINS:
        violations.append(
            'CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: true with "*" in CORS_ORIGINS '
            "(every origin is echoed back with credentials)"
        )
    if "null" in self.CORS_ORIGINS:
        violations.append(
            'CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: true with "null" in CORS_ORIGINS '
            "(any sandboxed document sends that origin)"
        )
    if self.CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX:
        try:
            pattern: re.Pattern[str] = re.compile(self.CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX)
        except re.error:
            return violations
        if any(pattern.fullmatch(origin) for origin in _CORS_PROBE_ORIGINS):
            violations.append(
                "CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS: true with a CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX "
                "that accepts arbitrary origins (anchor it to your domains)"
            )
    return violations

Bases: BaseAppSettings

SMTP / transactional email configuration.

Mirrors the constructor arguments of :class:tempest_fastapi_sdk.EmailUtils so a service can wire it up with EmailUtils(**settings.email_kwargs()).

Each attribute below is also the name of the environment variable that sets it (matched case-sensitively, no prefix).

Attributes:

Name Type Description SMTP_HOST str

Hostname of the SMTP server. Default: "localhost".

SMTP_PORT int

TCP port for the SMTP connection. Default: 587.

SMTP_USERNAME str | None

Auth username; None disables SMTP auth. Default: None.

SMTP_PASSWORD str | None

Auth password, paired with the username. Default: None.

SMTP_FROM_ADDR str

Default From address when the caller omits one. Default: "noreply@example.com".

SMTP_USE_TLS bool

Negotiate STARTTLS after connect (port 587). Default: True.

SMTP_USE_SSL bool

Wrap the connection in TLS from the start (SMTPS, port 465). Default: False.

SMTP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS float

Network timeout for SMTP operations. Default: 30.0.

EMAIL_ENABLED bool

Kill-switch for the whole integration. False skips the production checks below, lists "email" in :meth:disabled_integrations and makes :meth:email_kwargs build an :class:EmailUtils whose every send raises IntegrationDisabledException (503). Default: True.

In ENV=production (see :class:EnvironmentSettings), with EMAIL_ENABLED on, three values are refused because they can only be a development setup:

  • SMTP_HOST whose first DNS label is mailpit or mailhog;
  • SMTP_PORT=1025 together with a loopback SMTP_HOST (localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1) — the port Mailpit and MailHog publish;
  • SMTP_HOST still at its declared default (localhost) with no SMTP_USERNAME — an unauthenticated default is the development catcher, not a configured relay. A local relay keeps booting by setting SMTP_USERNAME or addressing it as 127.0.0.1;
  • SMTP_FROM_ADDR that is empty, has no @, or whose domain is reserved and can never send real mail: example.com, example.net, example.org or localhost (and any subdomain of them), or anything under .example, .invalid, .localhost or .test. The declared default (noreply@example.com) is refused by itself as well;
  • a TLS mode that contradicts itself or the port: SMTP_USE_SSL and SMTP_USE_TLS both on; SMTP_USE_SSL=true on 587 (implicit TLS against the STARTTLS port — the handshake fails with [SSL: WRONG_VERSION_NUMBER] on every send); SMTP_USE_TLS=true on 465 (STARTTLS against a port that expects TLS from the first byte). Other ports are not judged: a custom relay picks its own.

Gmail (smtp.gmail.com:587, STARTTLS, an app password in SMTP_USERNAME/SMTP_PASSWORD, a real SMTP_FROM_ADDR) produces no violation.

def production_violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """Refuse a dev mail catcher, a placeholder sender or a TLS mismatch.

    Skipped entirely when ``EMAIL_ENABLED`` is off. The declared
    defaults compared against are read from
    ``EmailSettings.model_fields``, not copied literals. ``localhost``
    is refused only paired with port ``1025`` or as the untouched
    default without ``SMTP_USERNAME``, so an authenticated local relay
    (or one addressed as ``127.0.0.1``) keeps booting. The rule is
    listed in the class docstring.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The parent's entries plus one per offending field.
    """
    violations: list[str] = super().production_violations()
    if not self.EMAIL_ENABLED:
        return violations
    fields = EmailSettings.model_fields
    host: str = self.SMTP_HOST.strip().lower()
    if host.split(".", 1)[0] in _DEV_SMTP_HOSTS:
        violations.append("SMTP_HOST: a development mail catcher")
    elif host in _LOOPBACK_SMTP_HOSTS and self.SMTP_PORT == _DEV_SMTP_PORT:
        violations.append(
            "SMTP_PORT: loopback on 1025 is the Mailpit/MailHog development pair"
        )
    elif fields["SMTP_HOST"].default == self.SMTP_HOST and not self.SMTP_USERNAME:
        violations.append(
            "SMTP_HOST: still the declared default, with no SMTP_USERNAME"
        )
    sender: str = self.SMTP_FROM_ADDR.strip().lower()
    domain: str = sender.rpartition("@")[2] if "@" in sender else ""
    if (
        fields["SMTP_FROM_ADDR"].default == self.SMTP_FROM_ADDR
        or not domain
        or is_reserved_domain(domain)
    ):
        violations.append(
            "SMTP_FROM_ADDR: empty or a reserved placeholder domain that "
            "cannot send real mail"
        )
    violations.extend(self._tls_mode_violations())
    return violations

def firebase_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Map these settings onto :class:`FirebaseAuth` kwargs.

    Empty strings are dropped rather than forwarded, so an unset
    variable leaves the corresponding constructor default in place
    instead of configuring an empty path.

    With ``FIREBASE_ENABLED`` off the result is ``{"enabled": False}``
    and nothing else: the credentials are not forwarded, so the
    ``FirebaseAuth`` it builds never initializes an app (nor falls
    back to an application-default credential) and refuses every
    verification with ``IntegrationDisabledException``.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Any]: Keyword arguments ready to splat into
        ``FirebaseAuth(**settings.firebase_kwargs())``.
    """
    if not self.FIREBASE_ENABLED:
        return {"enabled": False}
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {}
    if self.FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_JSON:
        kwargs["credentials_json"] = self.FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_JSON
    if self.FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH:
        kwargs["credentials_path"] = self.FIREBASE_CREDENTIALS_PATH
    if self.FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID:
        kwargs["project_id"] = self.FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID
    return kwargs

Every field in :data:AUTH_EMAIL_LINK_FIELDS is checked with :func:email_link_violation: the host must be reachable from outside (not localhost, loopback, 0.0.0.0 or a reserved name) and the scheme must be https. The defaults (http://localhost:3000/...) fail both.

def production_violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """Refuse e-mailed links that a real user could not open.

    Every field in :data:`AUTH_EMAIL_LINK_FIELDS` is checked with
    :func:`email_link_violation`: the host must be reachable from
    outside (not ``localhost``, loopback, ``0.0.0.0`` or a reserved
    name) and the scheme must be ``https``. The defaults
    (``http://localhost:3000/...``) fail both.

    Skipped when the e-mail integration cannot send — ``EMAIL_ENABLED``
    off on a composed :class:`EmailSettings` — because the link then
    never leaves the process. Without ``EmailSettings`` composed the
    attribute is absent and the check applies.

    ``AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE`` is refused regardless of
    ``EMAIL_ENABLED``: it hands the activation, reset, e-mail change
    and recovery links to whoever sent the request.
    ``AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE`` is refused the same way: it activates
    every signup without proof that the address belongs to whoever
    signed up.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The parent's entries, one for
        ``AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE`` and one for
        ``AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE`` when each is on, plus at most
        one per template.
    """
    violations: list[str] = super().production_violations()
    if self.AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE:
        violations.append(
            "AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE: activates every signup without proof "
            "that the e-mail address belongs to whoever signed up"
        )
    if self.AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE:
        violations.append(
            "AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE: hands the e-mailed links to "
            "the anonymous caller instead of the mailbox"
        )
    if getattr(self, "EMAIL_ENABLED", True) is False:
        return violations
    for field in AUTH_EMAIL_LINK_FIELDS:
        entry = email_link_violation(field, getattr(self, field))
        if entry is not None:
            violations.append(entry)
    return violations

Credentials for the bundled social-login providers.

Splits cleanly from :class:AuthSettings along one line: this mixin says who you are at the provider, and the AUTH_OAUTH_* fields of AuthSettings say what the bundled router does. The router never reads this mixin — it receives clients the application already built — so a project that gets its credentials from a secret manager instead of the environment can skip it entirely and still use every /auth/oauth/* endpoint.

The redirect URI is derived rather than declared. def oauth_redirect_uri(self, provider: str, *, prefix: str = "/auth") -> str:
    """Build the callback URL to register with ``provider``.

    The value must match the provider's registered redirect URI
    exactly — a trailing slash or an ``http`` where the console
    holds ``https`` is rejected at the *authorize* step, before the
    user ever sees a consent screen, which makes it look like a
    credential problem. Deriving it here keeps the string that
    reaches the provider and the string the router serves as one
    expression.

    Args:
        provider (str): Provider key as the router routes it
            (``"google"``, ``"github"``, or whatever key the
            application registered an ``OIDCProvider`` under).
        prefix (str): The ``make_auth_router`` prefix. Defaults to
            ``"/auth"``; pass the same value you passed the router
            if you changed it.

    Returns:
        str: The absolute callback URL.
    """
    return (
        f"{self.OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE_URL.rstrip('/')}"
        f"{prefix}/oauth/{provider}/callback"
    )

docs.title: StorageSettings
docs.text:
Bases: BaseAppSettings

S3-compatible object storage configuration.

Consumed by :class:tempest_fastapi_sdk.AsyncMinIOClient, which speaks the S3 API to any compatible target (AWS S3, MinIO, Backblaze B2, Cloudflare R2, Wasabi, DigitalOcean Spaces) — the MinIO in the client's name is the library it uses, not a requirement on the server.

Each attribute below is also the name of the environment variable that sets it (matched case-sensitively, no prefix). Every field that used to be MINIO_* (when this mixin was MinIOSettings) still reads the old name as a fallback through validation_alias=AliasChoices(new, old); the pairs are listed in :attr:DEPRECATED_ENV_ALIASES. Setting both names of a pair to different values refuses to build — see :func:~tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings.reject_conflicting_env_aliases. The pydantic mypy plugin flags each AliasChoices field as a "required dynamic alias" (pydantic-alias) and is silenced on those lines rather than with validate_by_name=True: that flag would merge into the consumer's composed Settings and make every aliased field of theirs readable from the environment by its field name as well.

The defaults are a local MinIO's (minioadmin/minioadmin over plain HTTP). In ENV=production (see :class:EnvironmentSettings) those keys, STORAGE_SECURE=False and an explicit STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE=False are refused — except that STORAGE_SECURE=False is accepted for the split-endpoint shape described in :meth:private_plain_http_allowed (a private bucket behind an HTTPS public endpoint).

@staticmethod
def decode_local_encryption_keys(value: Mapping[str, str]) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """Decode the base64 keys of ``STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS``.

    Args:
        value (Mapping[str, str]): Key id to base64 key.

    Returns:
        dict[str, bytes]: Key id to raw key, in the same order.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When a value is not valid base64; the message names
            the key id only.
    """
    decoded: dict[str, bytes] = {}
    for key_id, encoded in value.items():
        try:
            decoded[key_id] = base64.b64decode(encoded, validate=True)
        except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
            raise ValueError(
                f"STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS[{key_id!r}] is not valid base64"
            ) from None
    return decoded

def local_storage_kwargs(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Map these settings onto :class:`LocalObjectStorageClient` kwargs.

    With ``STORAGE_ENABLED`` off the dictionary carries
    ``enabled=False``, as :meth:`storage_kwargs` does for S3. With
    ``STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS`` set it carries the decoded
    ``encryption_keys`` and ``allow_plaintext_read``; without keys
    neither key is present, so the dictionary is the one it always was.

    Returns:
        dict[str, Any]: Keyword arguments ready to splat into
        ``LocalObjectStorageClient(**settings.local_storage_kwargs())``.
    """
    kwargs: dict[str, Any] = {
        "base_dir": self.STORAGE_LOCAL_DIR,
        "public_url": self.STORAGE_LOCAL_PUBLIC_URL,
        "signing_secret": self.STORAGE_LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET,
        "default_bucket": self.STORAGE_DEFAULT_BUCKET,
        "route_prefix": self.STORAGE_LOCAL_ROUTE_PREFIX,
        "max_upload_bytes": self.STORAGE_LOCAL_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES,
    }

def build_storage_client(self) -> AsyncMinIOClient | LocalObjectStorageClient:
    """Build the object-storage client ``STORAGE_BACKEND`` names.

    Both clients satisfy
    :class:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.privacy.SubjectStorageClient`, so the
    rest of the service does not care which one it got. With ``local``,
    mount :func:`~tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage.make_local_storage_router`
    so the links it signs have a route to land on.

    Returns:
        AsyncMinIOClient | LocalObjectStorageClient: The client, built
        from :meth:`storage_kwargs` or :meth:`local_storage_kwargs`.

    Raises:
        ImportError: For ``s3`` without the ``[minio]`` extra.
    """
    from tempest_fastapi_sdk.storage import (
        AsyncMinIOClient,
        LocalObjectStorageClient,
    )

    if self.STORAGE_BACKEND == "local":
        return LocalObjectStorageClient(**self.local_storage_kwargs())
    return AsyncMinIOClient(**self.storage_kwargs())

def production_violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """Refuse the local MinIO credentials and plain HTTP in production.

    The defaults compared against are read from
    ``StorageSettings.model_fields``, so they follow the declared
    default instead of a copied literal. ``STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE``
    is only refused when explicitly ``False``: ``None`` inherits
    ``STORAGE_SECURE``, which is checked on its own.

    Skipped entirely when ``STORAGE_ENABLED`` is off. With
    ``STORAGE_BACKEND=local`` the S3 fields are not checked — nothing
    reads them — and :meth:`local_storage_violations` runs instead.

    A local store without ``STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS`` is **not** a
    violation: refusing it would stop, on upgrade and without notice,
    every service that already runs the local backend in production. It
    logs a ``WARNING`` on the ``tempest_fastapi_sdk.settings`` logger
    instead, each time the production guard runs.

    Returns:
        list[str]: The parent's entries plus one per offending field.
    """
    violations: list[str] = super().production_violations()
    if not self.STORAGE_ENABLED:
        return violations
    if self.STORAGE_BACKEND == "local":
        violations.extend(self.local_storage_violations())
        if not self.STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS:
            _settings_logger.warning(
                "STORAGE_BACKEND=local in production without "
                "STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS: stored files stay in "
                "plaintext on the disk, its snapshots and its backups"
            )
        return violations
    fields = StorageSettings.model_fields
    if fields["STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY"].default == self.STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY:
        violations.append("STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY: still the MinIO default credential")
    if fields["STORAGE_SECRET_KEY"].default == self.STORAGE_SECRET_KEY:
        violations.append("STORAGE_SECRET_KEY: still the MinIO default credential")
    if not self.STORAGE_SECURE and not self.private_plain_http_allowed():
        violations.append(
            "STORAGE_SECURE: storage traffic over plain HTTP (allowed only "
            "for a private STORAGE_ENDPOINT behind an HTTPS "
            "STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT)"
        )
    if self.STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE is False:
        violations.append("STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE: presigned URLs over plain HTTP")
    return violations

def local_storage_violations(self) -> list[str]:
    """List what the local backend cannot ship to production with.

    * ``STORAGE_LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET`` still the development placeholder
      (anyone could forge a link) or empty;
    * ``STORAGE_LOCAL_PUBLIC_URL`` not ``https`` (the signed link travels
      in the clear);
    * ``STORAGE_LOCAL_DIR`` relative (it would follow the working
      directory, which differs between the API and the worker).

    Returns:
        list[str]: One entry per offending field; empty when none.
    """
    violations: list[str] = []
    if self.STORAGE_LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET in {"", DEV_LOCAL_STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET}:
        violations.append(
            "STORAGE_LOCAL_SIGNING_SECRET: empty or still the development "
            "placeholder"
        )
    if urlsplit(self.STORAGE_LOCAL_PUBLIC_URL).scheme != "https":
        violations.append("STORAGE_LOCAL_PUBLIC_URL: local links over plain HTTP")
    if not self.STORAGE_LOCAL_DIR.startswith("/"):
        violations.append("STORAGE_LOCAL_DIR: relative path (use an absolute one)")
    return violations

@staticmethod
def is_private_endpoint(endpoint: str) -> bool:
    """Tell whether a ``host[:port]`` endpoint is reachable only privately.

    Private means a single-label hostname (a Docker service name such
    as ``bucket``, or ``localhost``), or an IP in
    :data:`_PRIVATE_STORAGE_NETWORKS` (RFC 1918, loopback, link-local,
    IPv6 ULA). A scheme and a path, if present, are ignored; an IPv6
    address may come bracketed (``[fd00::1]:9000``).

    Args:
        endpoint (str): The endpoint, as ``STORAGE_ENDPOINT`` holds it.

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` for a private host, ``False`` for anything with
        a dot that is not a private IP (a public DNS name).
    """
    value = endpoint.strip().lower().split("://", 1)[-1].split("/", 1)[0]
    if value.startswith("["):
        host = value[1:].split("]", 1)[0]
    elif value.count(":") == 1:
        host = value.split(":", 1)[0]
    else:
        host = value
    try:
        address = ipaddress.ip_address(host)
    except ValueError:
        return bool(host) and "." not in host
    return any(address in network for network in _PRIVATE_STORAGE_NETWORKS)

Plain HTTP between the app and the bucket is a legitimate production setup when the bucket is only reachable on a private network (STORAGE_ENDPOINT=bucket:9000 inside a compose network) and clients only ever see presigned URLs signed for an HTTPS public host. All three must hold:

def private_plain_http_allowed(self) -> bool:
    """Whether ``STORAGE_SECURE=False`` is the split-endpoint shape.

    Plain HTTP between the app and the bucket is a legitimate
    production setup when the bucket is only reachable on a private
    network (``STORAGE_ENDPOINT=bucket:9000`` inside a compose
    network) and clients only ever see presigned URLs signed for an
    HTTPS public host. All three must hold:

    * ``STORAGE_ENDPOINT`` is private (:meth:`is_private_endpoint`);
    * ``STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT`` is set;
    * the public scheme is HTTPS — ``STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE=True``, or
      ``None`` with an ``https://`` public endpoint (what
      ``AsyncMinIOClient`` resolves the same way).

    Returns:
        bool: ``True`` when plain HTTP is confined to the private hop.
    """
    public = self.STORAGE_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT
    if not public or not self.is_private_endpoint(self.STORAGE_ENDPOINT):
        return False
    if self.STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE is not None:
        return self.STORAGE_PUBLIC_SECURE
    return public.strip().lower().startswith("https://")

Bases: BaseAppSettings

Where model weights live, and whether loads may use the network.

The genai loaders read these three variables as defaults: an argument passed to a loader always wins, so a service pins the cache and the offline switch once — compose, chart, systemd unit — and a call that needs something different still says so per model.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, GenAISettings


class Settings(GenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    pass

# .env — read by the loaders even without the class above
GENAI_CACHE_DIR=/models      # survives a container restart
GENAI_OFFLINE=true           # never reach the Hub at load time
GENAI_HF_TOKEN=hf_xxx        # gated repos, and no anonymous rate limit

Declaring the class is what makes the values typed, documented and visible in tempest check-config; the loaders themselves read the environment directly, so a service that never declares it still gets the same behaviour.
