                    tag="input",
                    attrs={"name": "title", "placeholder": "New task", "required": "required"},
                ),
                Button(label="Add", attrs={"type": "submit"}),
            ],
        )
        items = [task_widget(i, t, d) for i, t, d in self.tasks]
        return Column(
            tag="main",
            children=[
                Text(content="Tasks", tag="h1"),
                form,
                Column(tag="ul", attrs={"id": "tasks"}, children=items),
            ],
        )

docs.title: The routes
docs.text:
GET / returns the full document (htmx=True injects the local HTMX); each action returns just the fragment (document=False) that HTMX swaps in place:

from collections.abc import AsyncGenerator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from tempest_core import Text

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseRepository
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.ssr import html_response, make_htmx_router

from src.api.dependencies.resources import db
from src.db.models import TaskModel
from src.web.pages import TasksPage
from src.web.widgets import task_widget


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(_: FastAPI) -> AsyncGenerator[None, None]:
    await db.connect()
    await db.create_tables()
    yield
    await db.disconnect()


app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
app.include_router(make_htmx_router())   # serves /_ssr/htmx.js locally


@app.get("/")
async def index() -> object:
    async with db.get_session_context() as session:
        rows = await BaseRepository(session, model=TaskModel).list()
    page = TasksPage(
        title="Tasks",
        tasks=[(str(r.id), r.title, r.done) for r in rows],
    )
    return html_response(page, title="Tasks", htmx=True)


@app.post("/tasks")
async def create_task(title: str = Form(...)) -> object:
    async with db.get_session_context() as session:
        repo = BaseRepository(session, model=TaskModel)
        task = await repo.add(TaskModel(title=title))
        await session.commit()
        await session.refresh(task)
    return html_response(
        task_widget(str(task.id), task.title, task.done), document=False
    )


@app.post("/tasks/{task_id}/toggle")
async def toggle_task(task_id: UUID) -> object:
    async with db.get_session_context() as session:
        repo = BaseRepository(session, model=TaskModel)
        task = await repo.get_by_id(task_id)
        task.done = not task.done
        await repo.update(task)
        await session.commit()
    return html_response(
        task_widget(str(task.id), task.title, task.done), document=False
    )


@app.delete("/tasks/{task_id}")
async def delete_task(task_id: UUID) -> object:
    async with db.get_session_context() as session:
        await BaseRepository(session, model=TaskModel).delete(task_id)
        await session.commit()
    return html_response(Text(content="", tag="span"), document=False)

Run it with uvicorn app:app --reload and open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

What this project shows

  • Typed Page + html_response (document and fragment).
  • make_htmx_router serving the bundled HTMX — no CDN, offline, CSP-friendly.
  • BaseRepository for the CRUD, all async.
  • Real interactivity (add/toggle/delete) without writing any JavaScript.

docs.title: Project 2 — WASM SPA (Python in the browser)
docs.text: Now the same Python runs in the browser via Pyodide. You compile the frontend with tempestweb build --mode wasm and the SDK serves the static dist/ with make_web_app_router — plus a FastAPI JSON API behind it for the data.

docs.title: The tempestweb app (web/app.py)
docs.text:
The tempestweb contract is make_state + view (the same code runs in both modes — the transport is chosen at build time):

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass

from tempest_core import App, Button, Column, Row, Style, Text, Widget
from tempest_core.style import Edge


@dataclass
class State:
    value: int = 0


def make_state() -> State:
    return State()


def view(app: App[State]) -> Widget:
    return Column(
        style=Style(gap=8.0, padding=Edge.all(16)),
        children=[
            Text(content=f"Count: {app.state.value}", key="label"),
            Row(
                style=Style(gap=4.0),
                children=[
                    Button(label="-", key="dec",
                           on_click=lambda: app.set_state(
                               lambda s: setattr(s, "value", s.value - 1))),
                    Button(label="+", key="inc",
                           on_click=lambda: app.set_state(
                               lambda s: setattr(s, "value", s.value + 1))),
                ],
            ),
        ],
    )

docs.title: The build
docs.text:
cd web
tempestweb build --mode wasm     # emits web/dist/wasm/ (index.html + bootstrap + wasm + sw)

The SDK does not build — building stays in the tempestweb CLI/CI flow. The SDK only serves the finished dist/.

docs.title: The FastAPI host
docs.text:
make_web_app_router returns an APIRouter that serves the SPA with a history fallback (unknown client-side route → index.html). Include it last, so the API routes beat the catch-all:

from fastapi import APIRouter, FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.ssr import make_web_app_router

app = FastAPI()

# 1) Your JSON API — registered FIRST.
api = APIRouter(prefix="/api")


@api.get("/count")
async def count() -> dict[str, int]:
    return {"value": 42}


app.include_router(api)

# 2) The static SPA — registered LAST (root catch-all).
app.include_router(make_web_app_router("web/dist/wasm"))

Run it with uvicorn app:app. GET /api/count returns JSON; any other route serves the SPA, which runs Python in the browser and calls your API.

Mount at the root, include last

The wasm artifact references /sw.js at the site root, so mount it at the app root. And because the router is a catch-all (/{resource:path}), include it after your API routers.

No magic in the serving

index.html and sw.js are always no-cache; other assets use asset_cache_control. Correct MIME for .wasm/.mjs/.webmanifest, Service-Worker-Allowed: / on the worker, traversal blocked, and no imposed CSP (Pyodide needs wasm-unsafe-eval) — pass security_headers= to add your own.

docs.title: Project 3 — Server-mode (live WebSocket/SSE)
docs.text: The same web/app.py as Project 2, now compiled to run on the server: the UI is driven live over WebSocket/SSE. You compile with --mode server and mount with build_web_app.

docs.title: The build
docs.text:
cd web
tempestweb build --mode server   # emits web/dist/server/ (server.py + app.py + static)

docs.title: The FastAPI host
docs.text:
build_web_app loads the artifact's app.py, wires the tempestweb server engine (/ws + /sse routes), serves the client under /static and the shell at / — the same wiring the generated server.py does, in-process. Since the server build references /ws at the root, it owns the root; add your API routes to that app:

from fastapi import APIRouter

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.ssr import build_web_app

# The tempestweb app is already a FastAPI — add your API to it.
app = build_web_app("web/dist/server", title="Counter")

api = APIRouter(prefix="/api")


@api.get("/health")
async def health() -> dict[str, bool]:
    return {"ok": True}


app.include_router(api)

Run it with uvicorn app:app. The browser opens /, connects to /ws, and every click runs the view on the server — the tree is diffed and sent back. GET /api/health still answers normally.

The shell is the only part of the HTML an application owns

The artifact's index.html comes out of tempestweb build with lang="en", no <meta name="description">, no favicon and nowhere to put a CSP nonce. Pass shell= to serve your own:

from pathlib import Path

from fastapi import Request

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.ssr import build_web_app

generated: str = (Path("web/dist/server") / "index.html").read_text()


def shell(request: Request) -> str:
    """Serve the generated shell with the language and nonce fixed."""
    nonce = getattr(request.state, "csp_nonce", "")
    return generated.replace('<html lang="en">', '<html lang="pt-BR">').replace(
        "<script", f'<script nonce="{nonce}"', 1
    )


app = build_web_app("web/dist/server", shell=shell)

Three forms are accepted: a str (the document), a Path (read from disk) or a callable — invoked per request, which is what makes a per-response nonce possible. The callable may declare Request or no parameter at all. The same applies to make_web_app_router, where the shell also answers the SPA fallback.

A str with no < in it is rejected: that is a path written where a document was expected, and it would serve a blank page silently.

The application's palette enters here too

theme= hands a Theme to every session's App, and the view reads it back as app.theme:

from tempest_core import Theme, ThemeMode
from tempest_core.style import Color

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.ssr import build_web_app

brand: Theme = Theme.from_seed(Color(r=39, g=58, b=79), mode=ThemeMode.SYSTEM)

app = build_web_app("web/dist/server", theme=brand)

The components the view builds resolve their colours against that palette on their own — the build installs the theme around the view call. This needs tempestweb 0.67.0 or newer: that is where the capability reaches tempest-core 0.12.0, where the connection lives. A theme= passed straight to a widget still wins. The full recipe, with both halves of a rebrand, is in SSR.

Which mode?

  • WASM — the client is self-contained (runs offline), the server is optional (just API + files). Heavier boot (downloads Pyodide).
  • Server — instant boot and state lives on the server (great for sensitive data or heavy logic), but needs a live connection.

The best part: web/app.py is identical in both — just swap the build --mode.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• SSR + HTMX — Page + html_response + make_htmx_router: server-rendered, no build, interactivity via local HTMX.
  • WASM SPA — tempestweb build --mode wasm + make_web_app_router: Python in the browser, served as static with a history fallback + your API.
  • Server-mode — tempestweb build --mode server + build_web_app: live UI over WebSocket/SSE, with your API on the same app.
  • detect_build_mode(dir) tells a wasm dist/ from a server one.
  • The SDK only serves a finished build — compiling stays in tempestweb. Per-API details in SSR.

docs.title: GenAI examples — complete flows
docs.text: The generative-AI recipe documents each piece; here they combine into real flows, self-hosted end to end. Install the extras per example: uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai,genai-rag,genai-audio,genai-tts-coqui]".

docs.title: 1. Load the model only if it fits
docs.text:
Before downloading gigabytes, check; let the SDK pick the precision that fits:

import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextGenerator, recommend

MODEL = "Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct"
rec = recommend(model_id=MODEL)          # native (bf16 GPU, fp32 CPU) -> int8 -> int4

if not rec.fits:
    raise RuntimeError(rec.reason + " " + (rec.suggestion or ""))

gen = TextGenerator(
    MODEL,
    device=rec.device,
    quantization=rec.dtype if rec.dtype in ("int8", "int4") else None,
    idle_unload_seconds=300,             # threshold for unload_if_idle()
)


async def main() -> None:
    """Run this example."""
    answer = await gen.generate("Explain PIX in one sentence.")
    print(answer)


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 2. RAG over a PDF knowledge base
docs.text:
Index the PDFs once, answer grounded questions afterwards. In-memory here (dev); swap for PgVectorStore(db, dim=384) in production.

import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import Embedder, TextGenerator
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.rag import InMemoryVectorStore, PdfReader, Retriever

rag = Retriever(
    Embedder("sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2", normalize=True),
    InMemoryVectorStore(),
)
gen = TextGenerator("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", quantization="int4")


async def index_corpus() -> None:
    """Index the PDFs once, at service start-up or in a job."""
    for pdf in ("manual.pdf", "faq.pdf", "policies.pdf"):
        await rag.index(PdfReader().chunks(f"/kb/{pdf}", max_chars=1500, overlap=150))


async def answer(question: str) -> str:
    """Answer one question from the indexed PDFs; cheap, per request."""
    context = await rag.retrieve(question, top_k=5)
    prompt = f"{context}\n\nAnswer only from the sources above.\n{question}"
    return await gen.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=400)


async def main() -> None:
    """Index the corpus, then answer one question."""
    await index_corpus()
    print(await answer("How do I ask for a refund?"))


asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: 3. Web-grounded answer (SearXNG)
docs.text:
No own corpus — search the web, extract, answer:

import httpx

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import HTTPClient
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextGenerator
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.rag import ContentExtractor, SearxngBackend, WebSearch

search = WebSearch(SearxngBackend("http://localhost:8080", http_client=HTTPClient()))
extractor = ContentExtractor(http_client=httpx.AsyncClient())
gen = TextGenerator("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", quantization="int4")


async def answer_from_web(question: str) -> str:
    context = await search.retrieve(question, extractor=extractor, max_results=5)
    return await gen.generate(f"{context}\n\n{question}", max_new_tokens=400)

docs.title: 4. Fully local voice assistant
docs.text:
The full loop: audio → text → RAG/LLM → text → audio. Nothing leaves the box.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextGenerator
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio import LanguageEnum, SpeechToText, TextToSpeech

stt = SpeechToText("base")
gen = TextGenerator("Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", quantization="int4")
tts = TextToSpeech.for_language(LanguageEnum.EN_US)


async def voice_turn(audio_wav_path: str) -> bytes:
    """Take speech, return speech."""
    heard = await stt.transcribe(audio_wav_path, language=LanguageEnum.EN_US)
    reply = await gen.chat([
        {"role": "system", "content": "You are a concise assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": heard.text},
    ])
    return await tts.synthesize(reply)          # WAV bytes

Combine with RAG: swap gen.chat(...) for gen.generate(await rag.retrieve(heard.text)) to get a voice assistant that answers about your PDFs.

docs.title: 5. FastAPI transcription endpoint
docs.text:
from fastapi import APIRouter, UploadFile

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio import LanguageEnum, SpeechToText

router = APIRouter()
stt = SpeechToText("base")                      # load in the lifespan in prod


@router.post("/transcribe")
async def transcribe(file: UploadFile) -> dict[str, object]:
    result = await stt.transcribe(await file.read(), language=LanguageEnum.EN_US)
    return {"text": result.text, "duration": result.duration}

docs.title: Scale and economy
docs.text:
• Batch: wrap await embedder.embed(texts) in a BatchScheduler to coalesce concurrent embeddings into one forward pass — the full recipe is in GenAI. Use the public embed, not _embed_many: besides being private, it is synchronous, so the BatchScheduler, which does await handler(batch), would raise TypeError.
  • Share models: ModelRegistry(max_models=2) reuses loaded models across call sites and unloads the LRU.
  • Free VRAM: idle_unload_seconds + gen.unload_if_idle() in a @tq.interval(60) TaskQueue task.
  • Embedding cache: Embedder(cache=...) skips the model for text already seen.

Full reference for each piece: Self-hosted generative AI.

docs.title: TL;DR
docs.text:
pip install tempest-fastapi-sdk

Requires Python 3.12+ (3.12, 3.13 and 3.14).

Use uv instead

uv add tempest-fastapi-sdk is faster and writes to pyproject.toml for you.

The tempest command is the [cli] extra (or [cli-ops] on a server)

Since 0.308.0 the CLI (tempest new, tempest check, tempest db, …) is not part of the base package — the quality gate brings ruff, which has no place in a production image. In development, install it as a tool: uv tool install "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cli]", or in the project's dev group: uv add --dev "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cli]". To have tempest on a server (doctor, db, shell and the project's commands), use [cli-ops], which brings neither tempest-cli nor ruff: uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cli-ops]".

First time with modern Python?

This page assumes you already have a working environment. If you do not, follow the beginner track, which starts from absolute zero: Install uv » → Pick your Python version » → Your first project » → Official reference docs ».

docs.title: Optional extras
docs.text:
Feature-rich helpers pull in third-party dependencies that you only need when you actually use the helper. Pick the extras your service consumes:

Extra Pulls in Unlocks [admin] jinja2, itsdangerous AdminSite, AdminModel, make_admin_router [admin-sql] sqlglot admin SQL console: SqlShellService + SqlShellPolicy (capabilities, allowed/denied tables, row cap), real statement parsing, every attempt audited [auth] bcrypt, PyJWT PasswordUtils, JWTUtils, bundled UserAuthService + make_auth_router flow [cache] redis AsyncRedisManager + @cached + RedisIdempotencyStore [cli] tempest-cli (which requires ruff), typer, click the whole tempest command (new, check, db, …), quality gate included. Dev tooling: uv add --dev "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cli]" or uv tool install "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cli]". Without it or [cli-ops], tempest prints the install line and exits with code 2. Included in [all]. Recipe [cli-ops] typer, click the tempest command without the gate, for a server: doctor, db, shell, user, routes and [tool.tempest] commands run; tempest lint and the other gate commands exit 2 naming [cli]. No tempest-cli, no ruff. [cli] contains it. Recipe [genai-onnx] onnxruntime, tokenizers Local-model inference from an ONNX export, with no PyTorch at runtime [genai-structured] lm-format-enforcer Grammar-enforced structured output: the local model can only emit JSON matching the schema [genai-vlm] pillow, torchvision Local vision-language model: describe an image, answer a question about one [openapi] pyyaml Read a YAML OpenAPI spec for tempest openapi-client / tempest openapi-errors [pdf-read] pypdf Read PDFs (extract text/pages); [pdf] is for generating them [pdf-layout] pdfplumber Read PDFs with layout and tables (columns recovered, tables as grids); slower than [pdf-read] [spreadsheet] openpyxl .xlsx spreadsheets: typed reading, writing and bulk import [websocket] websockets Protocol driver for make_websocket_router — without it the handshake 404s [email] aiosmtplib, jinja2, email-validator EmailUtils (with render_template + Jinja2 templates) [faces] onnxruntime, pillow, numpy Face recognition on ONNX Runtime, no opencv and no torch: FaceRecognizer (detect/embed/compare), compare_faces. 16 MB models fetched by ensure_models(). No system libraries [firebase] firebase-admin Firebase ID token verification: FirebaseAuth (idempotent init, get_identity / get_uid / get_optional_identity), FirebaseIdentity, FirebaseUserResolver, FirebaseSettings. Heavy — 33 packages, 52 MB measured on firebase-admin 7.5.0 — and therefore out of [all] [genai] transformers, torch, accelerate, safetensors, huggingface-hub local (heavy) GenAI: TextGenerator, Embedder, MusicGenerator, BarkSpeech, AIChatPipeline, make_genai_router via HuggingFace/torch [genai-audio] faster-whisper, torch STT (Whisper). Since 0.349.0 it no longer brings Coqui: its torchaudio broke Bark on a GPU (details) [genai-tts-coqui] coqui-tts, torch, torchaudio, torchcodec, six TTS (Coqui XTTS v2) — the Coqui runtime ships with it; no transformers<5 cap since 0.342.0 (details) [genai-chroma] chromadb Chroma vector store for RAG [genai-diarization] sherpa-onnx Speaker diarization (who spoke when) via sherpa-onnx on ONNX Runtime, no PyTorch: SpeakerDiarizer, ConversationTranscriber. Models (46 MB) fetched by ensure_models() [genai-hosted] httpx (already in the base package) hosted providers: AnthropicGenerator, OpenAICompatGenerator (OpenAI, DeepSeek), OpenAICompatEmbedder, HostedGenAISettings. No vendor SDK [genai-hub] huggingface-hub weight lifecycle: resolve_revision (pin a sha), download_model (fetch before serving, with a disk preflight), list_cached_models/remove_cached_model, tempest model pull/cache-list/cache-rm [genai-image] diffusers, pillow local image generation: ImageGenerator (generate text→image, edit image→image), ImageGenerationConfig, POST /image route [genai-sound] diffusers local sound effects and music (with [genai]): AudioGenerator, AudioGenerationConfig, GeneratedAudio, POST /audio route [genai-ollama] httpx Ollama backend: OllamaGenerator, OllamaEmbedder, OllamaSpeech (speech and transcription) [genai-quant] bitsandbytes 4/8-bit quantization for the local [genai] models [genai-rag] trafilatura, pymupdf, pgvector, httpx RAG ingestion: web scraping, PDF extraction, and pgvector embeddings [geo] httpx geospatial helpers: haversine_km, estimate_travel, NominatimBackend/OSRMBackend (geocoding + routing), GeoPointMixin [http] httpx (already in the base package) HTTPClient + RetryPolicy + circuit-breaker. The extra is optional: HTTPClient works on the base install, and declaring the extra only records the intent in the service's pyproject.toml [image] pillow strip_image_metadata: re-encodes a user's photo in the same format without EXIF (GPS, device), XMP, IPTC, ICC and text chunks, with a pixel ceiling against decompression bombs [metrics] psutil, nvidia-ml-py MetricsUtils [mfa] pyotp, segno TOTPHelper + MFA/2FA (TOTP) endpoints on the bundled auth flow + enrollment QR code (provisioning_qr_terminal, provisioning_qr_data_uri) [minio] minio AsyncMinIOClient, MinIOUploadStorage [modelops] psutil, nvidia-ml-py, numpy benchmark any callable: latency, RAM, GPU and energy (benchmark, NvmlPowerSampler, RaplEnergySampler); drift monitoring (baseline_from_samples, PredictionMonitor) and reading the compact format (read_compact, predict_compact) [modelops-compose] ort-vision-sdk[compose] fuse a detector and a classifier into one .onnx: fuse_detect_classify. Running the fused graph is [vision] (DetectClassify), which pulls no onnx [modelops-onnx] onnx, onnxruntime static analysis, ONNX benchmarking, .onnx → .ort, graph optimization and quantization — of raw graphs (analyze_onnx, benchmark_onnx, export_onnx_to_ort, quantize_onnx_dynamic) and of transformers exports (optimize_hf_onnx, quantize_hf_onnx) [modelops-sklearn] skl2onnx export scikit-learn models to ONNX for the edge: export_sklearn_to_onnx, verify_sklearn_onnx, edge_bundle [oidc] PyJWT, cryptography offline verification of OIDC realm access tokens (Keycloak, Auth0, Okta …): OIDCTokenVerifier, and OIDCProvider(token_verifier=...) for social login [otel] opentelemetry-sdk, OTLP exporter + FastAPI/SQLAlchemy/httpx instrumentations OpenTelemetry instrumentation via setup_tracing [pdf] weasyprint, jinja2, segno PDF generation from HTML templates: PdfRenderer, five bundled typed documents, make_pdf_router, tempest pdf. Needs Pango + fontconfig on the system — see the recipe [postgres] asyncpg PostgreSQL async driver for postgresql+asyncpg:// URLs (production) [prometheus] prometheus-client PrometheusMiddleware, make_prometheus_router, make_prometheus_registry [queue] faststream[rabbit] AsyncBrokerManager [slides] weasyprint, jinja2, python-pptx, python-docx, markdown Slides and answer keys from structured text (HTML, PDF, PPTX, DOCX, Markdown) and Markdown to PDF with your own or the ABNT stylesheet: parse_slides, SlideRenderer, AnswerKeyRenderer, MarkdownPdfRenderer. Needs Pango + fontconfig on the system, like [pdf]. Recipe [slides-mermaid] playwright Drawing ```mermaid blocks in MarkdownPdfRenderer (render_mermaid=True). Needs playwright install chromium; that is why it stays out of [all] [sqlite] aiosqlite SQLite async driver for sqlite+aiosqlite:// URLs (dev default) [ssr] tempestweb HTMX-based SSR: build_web_app, make_htmx_router, Page, the htmx helper [storage-encryption] cryptography Encryption at rest of LocalObjectStorageClient (encryption_keys, STORAGE_LOCAL_ENCRYPTION_KEYS) and the tempest storage encrypt-local / reencrypt-local commands. Recipe [tasks] taskiq, taskiq-aio-pika AsyncTaskBrokerManager, AsyncTaskScheduler [tasks-redis] taskiq, taskiq-redis TaskQueue.redis / TaskQueue.from_settings over Redis Streams, the result backend and the scheduler lease [tests] pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-xdist the service's suite and tempest test in parallel (the default since tempest-cli 0.6.0). No bound of its own; inherits pytest<10 from pytest-asyncio and pluggy<2 from pytest. Test tooling, not a helper — kept out of [all]. Recipe [upload] aiofiles, python-multipart UploadUtils, DownloadUtils, LocalUploadStorage [vision] ort-vision-sdk vision helpers (Detector, Classifier, Segmenter + to_detection_schemas/to_classification_schema/to_segmentation_schemas) [webauthn] fido2 Passkeys / security keys: WebAuthnService, make_web_authn_credential_model, the /auth/webauthn/* routes — passwordless, phishing-resistant login [webpush] pywebpush, cryptography WebPushDispatcher [all] everything above except the 18 extras that pull a heavy stack or a native binary: [genai], [genai-audio], [genai-tts-coqui], [genai-diarization], [genai-hub], [genai-image], [genai-onnx], [genai-sound], [genai-quant], [genai-rag], [genai-structured], [genai-vlm], [faces], [modelops-onnx], [modelops-sklearn], [admin-sql], [firebase], [slides-mermaid] the application helpers — install the 18 above separately (and [tests], which is test tooling, in the dev group) Subset (recommended)Everythinguv addpyproject.toml 
pip install "tempest-fastapi-sdk[auth,upload,cache]"

pip install "tempest-fastapi-sdk[all]"

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[auth,upload,postgres]>=0.171.0"

dependencies = [
    "tempest-fastapi-sdk[auth,upload,postgres]>=0.171.0",
]

Since 0.349.0 Coqui (XTTS) lives in [genai-tts-coqui]

[genai-audio] used to bring coqui-tts and, with it, torchaudio. Bark does not use torchaudio, but transformers imports it when it is installed, while building the AutoProcessor. On a GPU the PyPI torchaudio 2.11.1 is a CUDA 13 build that does not load next to a CUDA 12 torch, so POST /audio/speech answered 500 (measured on tempest-ai, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, SDK 0.348.0 — issue #723).

Now [genai-audio] is speech-to-text only (faster-whisper + torch) and Coqui has an extra of its own. Resolved with uv pip compile (Python 3.12) on 2026-11-10:

Extra brings does not bring [genai-audio] faster-whisper 1.2.1, ctranslate2 4.8.5, torch 2.15.0 torchaudio, transformers, coqui-tts [genai-tts-coqui] coqui-tts 0.28.0, torchaudio 2.11.1, transformers 5.22.2, torch 2.15.0 —

If you use TextToSpeech (XTTS), replace [genai-audio] with [genai-audio,genai-tts-coqui] (or just [genai-tts-coqui], without STT).

Since 0.342.0 the Coqui extra no longer caps transformers<5

Up to 0.341.0 the extra carried transformers<5: coqui-tts 0.27.5 imported isin_mps_friendly, a symbol transformers 5.1 removed. That held anyone installing the extra on transformers 4.57.6, and with it huggingface-hub, tokenizers and, next to [genai-image], diffusers. coqui-tts 0.28.0 no longer imports the symbol, and the extra now requires that version.

Resolved with uv pip compile (Python 3.12) on 2026-11-01, while Coqui was still in [genai-audio] (it is in [genai-tts-coqui] today, see above), the extra held nothing back any more:

Extras transformers huggingface-hub tokenizers diffusers [genai-audio] 5.22.1 2.4.0 0.23.3 — [genai-audio,genai-image] 5.22.1 2.4.0 0.23.3 0.42.1 [genai-image] without [genai-audio] — 2.4.0 — 0.42.1

The extra declares six because coqui-tts 0.28.0 imports it without declaring it: in a clean venv without it, import TTS.api dies with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'six'.

The SDK ships no database driver by default

sqlalchemy[asyncio] is core, but the async DBAPI is your deploy choice: install [sqlite] (aiosqlite, dev default) or [postgres] (asyncpg, production). Without one, the engine raises ModuleNotFoundError for the driver on first connection. Services scaffolded with tempest new already pin both aiosqlite and asyncpg in pyproject.toml — the latter is what the generated docker-compose.yaml's prod profile uses.

Lazy imports

Since 0.7.1 every optional dependency is imported lazily at first instantiation, so import tempest_fastapi_sdk works even when only a subset of extras is installed. Instantiating a helper whose extra is missing raises ImportError with a clear hint pointing at the right extra. Since 0.326.0 the SDK's own modules load on demand too: import tempest_fastapi_sdk loads one module instead of 269 plus SQLAlchemy, FastAPI, Alembic, Jinja2 and bcrypt, and tempest --help went from 0.94 s to 0.14 s (best of 5, measured on this repository). from tempest_fastapi_sdk import X and strict type checking work as before.

docs.title: GPU with [genai-audio]
docs.text:
[genai-audio] transcribes with faster-whisper, which runs on CTranslate2. The ctranslate2 4.x wheels are linked against CUDA 12 and, on the first transcription with device="cuda", look up libcublas.so.12. The torch PyPI ships since 2.14 is a CUDA 13 build: it installs the .so.13 libraries, not the .so.12 ones. With the default resolution, then, the first GPU transcription dies like this:

RuntimeError: Library libcublas.so.12 is not found or cannot be loaded

The way out is to install torch from PyTorch's CUDA 12 index, which brings CUDA 12 cuBLAS and cuDNN as nvidia-*-cu12 packages.

docs.title: Step 1: torch from the cu126 index
docs.text:
In your service's pyproject.toml, declare the index as explicit (only the packages you point at it come from it) and point torch there:

[project]
name = "my-service"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai-audio]>=0.349.0",
    "torch>=2.14.0",
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu126"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126"
explicit = true

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu126" }

torch is listed in dependencies even though the extra already brings it: [tool.uv.sources] only applies to a direct dependency. Then uv sync.

Also using Coqui ([genai-tts-coqui])?

PyPI's torchaudio is a CUDA 13 build too, and it does not load next to a CUDA 12 torch (libcudart.so.13: cannot open shared object file). Point it at the same index — and, again, as a direct dependency:

[project]
name = "my-service"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai-audio,genai-tts-coqui]>=0.349.0",
    "torch>=2.14.0",
    "torchaudio>=2.11.0",
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-cu126"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu126"
explicit = true

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = { index = "pytorch-cu126" }
torchaudio = { index = "pytorch-cu126" }

STT-only users do not need these lines: since 0.349.0 [genai-audio] brings no torchaudio (why). Up to 0.348.0 it did, so on those versions declare torchaudio as above even without Coqui.

docs.title: Step 2: CTranslate2's LD_LIBRARY_PATH
docs.text:
The nvidia-cublas-cu12 and nvidia-cudnn-cu12 packages live inside site-packages, outside the dynamic loader's search path. torch finds them on its own; CTranslate2 does not. Point LD_LIBRARY_PATH at them before starting the process:

SITE_PACKAGES="$(python -c 'import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_paths()["purelib"])')"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$SITE_PACKAGES/nvidia/cublas/lib:$SITE_PACKAGES/nvidia/cudnn/lib:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:-}"

In a Dockerfile, write the image's venv path, for example ENV LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/app/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cublas/lib:/app/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/nvidia/cudnn/lib.

Why it sometimes works without LD_LIBRARY_PATH

When the process imports torch before loading Whisper, torch leaves CUDA 12 cuBLAS and cuDNN loaded, and CTranslate2 reuses them. That is what happens with SpeechToText(device="auto"), which imports torch to detect the GPU, or after a probe_hardware(). With an explicit device="cuda", nothing imports torch first, and without the variable the transcription fails. Export the variable anyway: relying on import order is fragile.

On a host with CUDA 12 installed system-wide (libcublas.so.12 in ldconfig), neither failure in this section shows up — the loader finds the system library. A python:3.12-slim container has none.

docs.title: Step 3: check it
docs.text:
Generate a short WAV (here with espeak-ng) and transcribe it on the GPU:

espeak-ng -v en -w hello.wav "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog."

import asyncio

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.audio import SpeechToText


async def main() -> None:
    """Transcribe a short WAV on the GPU."""
    stt = SpeechToText("small", device="cuda")
    with open("hello.wav", "rb") as handle:
        result = await stt.transcribe(handle.read())
    print(stt.device, result.text)


asyncio.run(main())

cuda The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.

probe_hardware() also flags the wrong pair before the first transcription: with a CUDA 13 torch and ctranslate2 installed, HardwareInfo.warnings says what will fail and points to this section (see Probing the hardware).

What was measured

In this repository, on 2026-11-10, in a python:3.12-slim container with --gpus all on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (WSL2, Windows driver 591.86), Python 3.12, faster-whisper 1.2.1 and ctranslate2 4.8.5, model small in float16, transcribing the WAV above:

torch LD_LIBRARY_PATH torch imported first result 2.15.0+cu132 (PyPI) no no libcublas.so.12 is not found 2.15.0+cu132 (PyPI) no yes libcublas.so.12 is not found 2.15.0+cu132 (PyPI) nvidia/{cublas,cudnn}/lib no libcublas.so.12 is not found 2.14.1+cu126 (cu126 index) no no libcublas.so.12 is not found 2.14.1+cu126 (cu126 index) no yes transcribes 2.14.1+cu126 (cu126 index) nvidia/{cublas,cudnn}/lib no transcribes

The rows above call WhisperModel directly; with the SDK installed on top, SpeechToText(device="cuda") gave the same pair (fails without the variable, transcribes with it) and SpeechToText(device="auto") transcribed without it. The venv was built from the step 1 pyproject.toml with tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai-audio] swapped for faster-whisper, which is what the extra brings, and the branch's SDK installed on top. The audio was the WAV above converted to 16 kHz with ffmpeg; the original WAV (22,050 Hz) gave the same text through SpeechToText on the CPU. On the WSL2 host outside the container, which has the system libcublas.so.12 in ldconfig, the cu126 venv transcribed without the variable and without importing torch — which is why the table comes from the container.

In tempest-ai (issue #723; python:3.12-slim, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, SDK 0.348.0) the same fix was applied to the service, with torch==2.14.1+cu126 and torchaudio==2.11.0+cu126 from the cu126 index: BarkSpeech (suno/bark-small) synthesized Portuguese — 5.95 s of audio in 9.6 s and 16.76 s in 23.6 s, with the model already loaded.

Not measured: Coqui ([genai-tts-coqui]) on the GPU with the cu126 torchaudio in this repository, and other GPUs, drivers or CUDA 12.x besides 12.6.

Recap: faster-whisper needs CUDA 12; PyPI's torch is CUDA 13. Take torch (and torchaudio, if you use Coqui) from the cu126 index, as a direct dependency, and export LD_LIBRARY_PATH to nvidia/{cublas,cudnn}/lib.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
The tempest CLI ships in the base install (no extra needed):

tempest --version              # show installed SDK version
tempest new                    # scaffold a layered service in cwd
tempest new myproject          # scaffold inside ./myproject
tempest generate --docker      # regenerate docker-compose.yaml from chosen extras
tempest db init                # bootstrap alembic dir (alembic.ini with no credentials)
tempest db revision -m "msg"   # autogenerate revision with the reorder hook applied
tempest db upgrade             # run upgrade to head (reads DATABASE_URL from .env)
tempest db downgrade -1        # roll back one revision
tempest db current             # show current revision
tempest db history             # revision log
tempest user create --email admin@local --admin   # `--email` required; password prompted interactively
tempest user list --admin      # list admins only (drop `--admin` to list everyone)
tempest fix                    # ruff check --fix-only . + ruff format . + ruff check .
tempest check                  # lint + fmt-check + mypy + pytest

See Recipes → CLI » for the full breakdown.

docs.title: Verify the install
docs.text: python -c "import tempest_fastapi_sdk; print(tempest_fastapi_sdk.__version__)"

docs.title: Python version policy
docs.text: Python Status 3.14 Supported 3.13 Supported — the version the repository's .python-version pins 3.12 Supported (minimum) 3.11 Not supported since 0.314.0 — stays on 0.313.x (migration) 3.10 and older Not supported (uses X | None PEP 604 syntax)

docs.title: Integrated example — Pix checkout
docs.text:
The SDK tour shows each piece in isolation. Here they work together in a real flow: an authenticated customer pays an order via Pix, and the system prices it with a cache, writes the order + event in the same transaction (outbox), fires a background email, and notifies the customer in real time over SSE + Web Push — all with SDK blocks.

Components exercised at once: settings + db, auth (JWT), validated fields + PixKeyField, cache (@cached), repository + service, transactional outbox, MessageBroker, TaskQueue, SSE and Web Push.

docs.title: 1. Resources (one place)
docs.text:
# src/core/resources.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AsyncDatabaseManager
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.cache import AsyncRedisManager
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.queue import MessageBroker
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.sse import SSEBroker
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.tasks import TaskQueue
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import EmailUtils

from src.core.settings import settings

db = AsyncDatabaseManager(settings.DATABASE_URL)
cache = AsyncRedisManager(settings.REDIS_URL)
email = EmailUtils(**settings.email_kwargs())
mq = MessageBroker.rabbitmq(settings.RABBITMQ_URL)      # cross-service events
tq = TaskQueue.rabbitmq(settings.TASKIQ_BROKER_URL)     # work off the request
events = SSEBroker(redis=cache.client_proxy, channel_prefix="checkout:sse")  # real-time status

They all start/stop in the lifespan (connect/disconnect) — see the Tutorial and the Safe deploy recipe.

docs.title: 2. Checkout schema (self-validating fields)
docs.text:
# src/schemas/checkout.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseSchema
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import PixKeyField, PositiveIntField


class CheckoutSchema(BaseSchema):
    product_id: str
    quantity: PositiveIntField        # > 0, else 422
    pix_key: PixKeyField              # validates CPF/CNPJ/email/phone/random

docs.title: 3. Price with a cache
docs.text:
The product rarely changes; cache the read and invalidate on write.

# src/services/catalog.py

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.cache import CacheInvalidator, cached

from src.core.resources import cache


async def load_price_from_db(sku: str) -> int:
    """Read the price in cents straight from the database."""
    return 1990


@cached(cache, ttl=300, key_prefix="catalog:", namespace="products")
async def get_product_cents(product_id: str) -> int:
    """Unit price in cents; 5-minute cache."""
    return await load_price_from_db(product_id)


async def invalidate_product(product_id: str) -> None:
    await CacheInvalidator(cache, key_prefix="catalog:").invalidate_namespace("products")

docs.title: 4. Service: write order + event in one transaction (outbox)
docs.text:
Writing the order and publishing "order paid" as two separate operations is unsafe. Write the order row and the outbox row together — save_with_outbox does it in a single transaction.

# src/services/orders.py
from uuid import UUID, uuid4

from src.core.resources import db
from src.db.models import OrderModel, OutboxModel
from src.db.repositories import OrderRepository
from src.schemas import CheckoutSchema
from src.services.catalog import get_product_cents


class OrderService:
    async def checkout(self, *, user_id: str, data: CheckoutSchema) -> OrderModel:
        unit_cents = await get_product_cents(data.product_id)     # cache
        total = unit_cents * data.quantity
        order_id: UUID = uuid4()

        async with db.get_session_context() as session:
            repo = OrderRepository(session)
            order = OrderModel(
                id=order_id,
                user_id=user_id,
                product_id=data.product_id,
                total_cents=total,
                pix_key=data.pix_key,
                status="paid",
            )
            # order + outbox event commit together (or neither):
            await repo.save_with_outbox(
                order,
                OutboxModel.new_event(
                    "orders.paid",
                    {"order_id": str(order_id), "user_id": user_id, "total": total},
                ),
            )
        return order

Generate the id before building the event

BaseModel's id has default=uuid4 on the column, and that default only runs at flush: OrderModel(...).id is None before it (measured). Since the event payload is built before save_with_outbox, str(order.id) would write "None" into the outbox. Generating the uuid4() and passing it as id= puts the same value on the row and on the event.

docs.title: 5. Authenticated endpoint
docs.text:
The user comes from the JWT; an invalid payload never reaches here (422 automatically).

# src/api/routers/checkout.py

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from src.api.dependencies import current_user, get_order_service
from src.db.models import UserModel
from src.schemas import CheckoutSchema
from src.services import OrderService


router = APIRouter(prefix="/api/checkout")


@router.post("")
async def checkout(
    data: CheckoutSchema,
    user: UserModel = Depends(current_user),        # JWT (header/cookie/query)
    service: OrderService = Depends(get_order_service),
) -> dict[str, str]:
    order = await service.checkout(user_id=str(user.id), data=data)
    return {"order_id": str(order.id), "status": order.status}

current_user comes from make_jwt_user_dependency / UserAuthService — see Auth flow.

docs.title: 6. Outbox relay → publishes to the broker
docs.text:
One process drains the outbox and publishes to the MessageBroker (with backoff and locking). The relay's publish plugs straight in:

# src/tasks/relay.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import OutboxRelay

from src.core.resources import db, mq
from src.db.models import OutboxModel

relay = OutboxRelay(db, model=OutboxModel,
                    publish=lambda e: mq.publish(e.topic, e.payload))
# asyncio.create_task(relay.run()) in the lifespan (or a dedicated process)

docs.title: 7. Consumer reacts: background email + SSE push
docs.text:
Whoever listens to "orders.paid" fires the email (TaskQueue, off the request) and pushes the status to the user's SSE channel.

# src/queue/consumers.py

from src.core.resources import email, events, mq, tq
from src.schemas.events import OrderPaid


@tq.task
async def send_receipt(to: str, order_id: str) -> None:
    await email.send(to, "Receipt", f"Order {order_id} paid.")


@mq.on("orders.paid")
async def on_order_paid(event: OrderPaid) -> None:
    await send_receipt.enqueue(to=event.user_email, order_id=event.order_id)   # background
    await events.publish(event.user_id, {"order_id": event.order_id, "status": "paid"},
                         event="order_update")                                 # SSE

docs.title: 8. Live payment notification (SSE + Web Push)
docs.text:
Section 7 pushed the status with a raw events.publish — perfect with the tab open. But the Pix confirmation is a domain event that deserves both channels: SSE for whoever is online and Web Push (VAPID) for whoever closed the app.

What "fan-out" means here: the same business event goes out over two different transports in the same call. The same payload (data) goes to SSE (arrives instantly if the app is open) and to Web Push (arrives even with the app closed, via a Service Worker). A NotificationService wraps that fan-out in a single notify function — the caller never has to know there are two channels.

docs.title: The notification service
docs.text:
# src/services/notification.py
from uuid import UUID

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    SSEBroker,
    WebPushPayloadSchema,
    WebPushSubscriptionService,
)


class NotificationService:
    """Fan one domain event out to SSE (foreground) and Web Push (background)."""

    def __init__(self, broker: SSEBroker, push: WebPushSubscriptionService) -> None:
        self.broker = broker
        self.push = push

    async def notify(
        self, user_id: UUID, event: str, title: str, body: str, data: dict
    ) -> None:
        """Deliver the same event over SSE (live) and Web Push (closed app)."""
        await self.broker.publish(str(user_id), data, event=event)
        await self.push.notify_user(
            user_id,
            WebPushPayloadSchema(title=title, body=body, tag=event, data=data),
        )

The body of notify is two lines, one per channel:

  • self.broker.publish(str(user_id), data, event=event) — the live channel (SSE). The 1st argument is the channel (the user id as a string); the 2nd is the payload (data, serialized to JSON); event= is the name of the event the front listens for with addEventListener. Reaches only whoever is connected right now.
  • self.push.notify_user(user_id, WebPushPayloadSchema(...)) — the background channel (Web Push). notify_user looks up that user's VAPID subscriptions and sends the push to each device; WebPushPayloadSchema carries the title/body the Service Worker shows as a system notification, plus the same data (and tag=event to group/replace notifications of the same kind).

Note both get the same data — that's what keeps the channels in sync. Wire notifications with the global events (section 1) and a WebPushSubscriptionService(BaseRepository(session, model=WebPushSubscriptionModel), dispatcher) — the dispatcher comes from WebPushDispatcher(**settings.webpush_kwargs()).

docs.title: Triggering from the handler
docs.text:
On confirmation, section 7's handler swaps the raw events.publish for a single notify:

# src/queue/consumers.py

from src.queue import OrderPaid, mq
from src.services.notification import notifications
from src.tasks import send_receipt


@mq.on("orders.paid")
async def on_order_paid(event: OrderPaid) -> None:
    await send_receipt.enqueue(to=event.user_email, order_id=event.order_id)   # background
    await notifications.notify(                                                # SSE + Web Push
        event.user_id,
        event="payment_confirmed",
        title="Payment approved",
        body=f"Order {event.order_id} confirmed.",
        data={"order_id": event.order_id},
    )

The handler just calls notify — it never touches EventStream, an HTTP response, or a Web Push subscription. The whole "which channels this goes out on" decision lives inside NotificationService; the handler only describes what to notify (title, body, data), not how to deliver it.

docs.title: The subscribe endpoint (SSE)
docs.text:
Whoever has the app open subscribes to the channel over SSE. One line does it all: broker.response(channel).

# src/api/routers/notifications.py

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

from src.db.models import UserModel
from src.services.notification import notifications

current_user = UserModel(name="Ana", email="ana@example.com")
router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/notifications/stream")
async def stream(user: UserModel = Depends(current_user)) -> StreamingResponse:
    return notifications.broker.response(str(user.id))

Step by step, what happens on each GET /notifications/stream:

  1. Depends(current_user) resolves who the client is from the JWT. Their id becomes the channel name — the same id notify uses in broker.publish(str(user_id), ...), so both sides agree on the same string.
  2. broker.response(str(user.id)) does three things in one call:
    • register — creates a fresh EventStream and subscribes it to the user's channel;
    • stream — returns a StreamingResponse with the SSE headers already set (the client starts receiving);
    • unregister — wires an on_disconnect that removes this stream from the channel when the client drops, with no hand-written try/finally.

When notify runs broker.publish on that channel, the frame lands on the open stream:

event: payment_confirmed
id: 42
data: {"order_id": "ord_123"}

docs.title: The Web Push subscriptions
docs.text:
The register/unregister of Web Push (VAPID) subscriptions — enrolling each device to receive push with the app closed — is mounted via make_web_push_router(...). The concrete model (WebPushSubscriptionModel, a subclass of BaseWebPushSubscriptionModel) and the router live in the Web Push recipe; that's where notify_user reads the subscriptions from at fan-out time.

SSE is core (no extra); Web Push needs the extra: uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[webpush]". Each channel's primitives live in SSE and Web Push — here we only compose them.

docs.title: 9. Frontend gets the status in real time
docs.text:
# src/api/routers/feed.py

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse

from src.core.resources import events
from src.db.models import UserModel

current_user = UserModel(name="Ana", email="ana@example.com")


router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/api/feed")
async def feed(user: UserModel = Depends(current_user)) -> StreamingResponse:
    return events.response(str(user.id))    # register + stream + unregister

docs.title: The flow, end to end
docs.text:
1. POST /api/checkout — JWT authenticates, the schema validates (quantity > 0, Pix ok).
  2. The service prices with the cache, writes order + outbox event in one transaction.
  3. The relay publishes orders.paid to the broker once the commit landed.
  4. The consumer enqueues the email (TaskQueue) and fans the confirmation out with the NotificationService: SSE for the open tab, Web Push for the closed one.
  5. The browser gets the update immediately on GET /api/feed / GET /notifications/stream; whoever is away receives the Web Push.

Each capability has its own recipe (see the recipe index); the point here is how they compose with no manual glue: exceptions become the right HTTP status, tokens gate the route, fields reject junk, the outbox guarantees the event, and real time closes the loop.

docs.title: Integrated example — neighbourhood marketplace
docs.text:
The Pix checkout wires the payment blocks together. Here we combine the SDK's newest modules into a local-commerce flow: an authenticated buyer finds nearby sellers, sees the distance and time to each, chats over real-time chat, gets live notifications (new order, new message), and finally rates the seller with stars.

Components exercised at once: geo (GeoPointMixin + GeoRepositoryMixin, NominatimBackend, estimate_travel), chat (ChatService + make_chat_router + SSEBroker), notifications (SSEBroker + WebPushSubscriptionService, one event on two channels), reviews (ReviewService + make_reviews_router) and the SDK auth for the current user.

What you need

The SDK core + the [geo] extra. The httpx the geocoder and OSRM use already ships with the base package, and the extra pulls only that same httpx: declaring [geo] records the intent in the service's pyproject.toml. Chat, reviews and the notification SSE are core (no extra); Web Push needs the [webpush] extra — uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[webpush]". Redis is optional (multi-worker SSE fan-out).

docs.title: 1. Models
docs.text:
The seller carries a geographic point; chat and reviews use the SDK's base tables pointing at your UserModel.

# src/db/models.py
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey, String, UniqueConstraint
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from uuid import UUID

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseModel, BaseUserModel
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.chat import (
    BaseConversationModel,
    BaseConversationParticipantModel,
    BaseMessageModel,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo import GeoPointMixin
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.reviews import BaseCommentModel, BaseRatingModel


class UserModel(BaseUserModel):
    __tablename__ = "users"


class SellerModel(GeoPointMixin, BaseModel):
    """A seller pinned to a location (latitude/longitude from the mixin)."""

    __tablename__ = "sellers"
    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(String(120))


class ConversationModel(BaseConversationModel):
    __tablename__ = "conversations"


class ParticipantModel(BaseConversationParticipantModel):
    __tablename__ = "conversation_participants"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint("conversation_id", "user_id", name="uq_participant"),
    )
    conversation_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("conversations.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )
    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )


class MessageModel(BaseMessageModel):
    __tablename__ = "messages"
    conversation_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("conversations.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )
    sender_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )


class CommentModel(BaseCommentModel):
    __tablename__ = "comments"
    author_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )


class RatingModel(BaseRatingModel):
    __tablename__ = "ratings"
    __table_args__ = (
        UniqueConstraint(
            "target_type", "target_id", "user_id", name="uq_rating_target_user"
        ),
    )
    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )

docs.title: 2. Find nearby sellers (geo)
docs.text:
The buyer sends an address (or CEP). We geocode it with Nominatim, search sellers in a radius straight from the database, and attach a motorcycle travel estimate — all with no paid API.

Nominatim on the request path

The public instance (https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org, the default base_url) has a strict usage policy — about one request per second and a User-Agent that identifies your application — and becomes a third party on the critical path of every search. Before production:

  • pass your own user_agent= (the default is "tempest-fastapi-sdk");
  • cache the result per normalized address or CEP, so the same search does not go back to Nominatim;
  • with volume, point base_url= at your own Nominatim instance.
# src/services/discovery.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseRepository
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo import (
    Coordinate,
    GeoRepositoryMixin,
    NominatimBackend,
    TravelModeEnum,
    estimate_travel,
)

from src.db.models import SellerModel


class SellerRepository(GeoRepositoryMixin, BaseRepository[SellerModel]):
    """Repository with the radius search mixin."""


class DiscoveryService:
    """Find nearby sellers from a buyer's address."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        sellers: SellerRepository,
        geocoder: NominatimBackend,
    ) -> None:
        self.sellers = sellers
        self.geocoder = geocoder

    async def nearby(
        self,
        address: str,
        *,
        radius_km: float = 5.0,
    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        """Return active sellers within ``radius_km`` of the address.

        Each entry carries the seller plus a motorcycle travel estimate.

        Args:
            address: The buyer's address or CEP.
            radius_km: Search radius in kilometres.

        Returns:
            Nearest-first sellers with a `TravelEstimate` each (`[]` when
            the address cannot be geocoded or nothing is nearby).
        """
        hit = await self.geocoder.geocode(address)
        if hit is None:
            return []
        origin: Coordinate = hit.coordinate
        found = await self.sellers.nearby(
            origin,
            radius_km=radius_km,
            extra_filters={"is_active": True},
            limit=20,
        )
        return [
            {
                "seller": seller,
                "eta": estimate_travel(
                    origin,
                    seller.coordinate(),
                    TravelModeEnum.MOTORCYCLE,
                ),
            }
            for seller in found
        ]

Cheap first, precise later

nearby already pre-filters by bounding box in SQL and refines with Haversine. Use estimate_travel (offline) for the list; call OSRMBackend.route only for the chosen seller, when real time matters.

docs.title: 3. Chat with the seller (real time)
docs.text:
An SSEBroker on the ChatService publishes every message to the conversation's channel; make_chat_router exposes /stream.

# src/services/chat.py
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseRepository
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.chat import ChatService
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.sse import SSEBroker

from src.db.models import ConversationModel, MessageModel, ParticipantModel

broker = SSEBroker()  # pass redis=<client> for multi-worker


def build_chat_service(session: AsyncSession) -> ChatService:
    return ChatService(
        conversations=BaseRepository(session, model=ConversationModel),
        participants=BaseRepository(session, model=ParticipantModel),
        messages=BaseRepository(session, model=MessageModel),
        broker=broker,
    )

The frontend opens an EventSource at /api/chat/conversations/{id}/stream and receives message events as the seller replies. No hand-rolling: the router registers and unregisters the stream for you.

docs.title: 4. Rate the seller (0–5 stars)
docs.text:
After the purchase, the buyer rates. The target is polymorphic (("seller", seller_id)), so the same table later serves products, posts, or anything else.

# src/services/reviews.py
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseRepository
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.reviews import ReviewService

from src.db.models import CommentModel, RatingModel


def build_review_service(session: AsyncSession) -> ReviewService:
    return ReviewService(
        comments=BaseRepository(session, model=CommentModel),
        ratings=BaseRepository(session, model=RatingModel),
    )

The storefront shows the average: await service.aggregate("seller", seller_id) returns average, count and the per-star distribution — the numbers behind a "4.7 ★ (321 reviews)" badge.

docs.title: 5. Wiring the app
docs.text:
The SDK's three routers plug in with the same shape: a service factory, a session factory and the current-user dependency.

# src/api/app.py
import httpx
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.chat import make_chat_router
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.geo import NominatimBackend
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.reviews import make_reviews_router

from src.core.resources import db, get_current_user_id
from src.services.chat import build_chat_service
from src.services.discovery import DiscoveryService, SellerRepository
from src.services.reviews import build_review_service
from src.db.models import SellerModel


async def get_session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    async with db.get_session_context() as session:
        yield session


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="Neighbourhood marketplace")
    http = httpx.AsyncClient()

    @app.get("/api/discovery")
    async def discovery(
        address: str,
        session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_session),
        _user_id: UUID = Depends(get_current_user_id),
    ) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
        service = DiscoveryService(
            SellerRepository(session, model=SellerModel),
            NominatimBackend(http_client=http, user_agent="marketplace/1.0"),
        )
        return await service.nearby(address)

    app.include_router(
        make_chat_router(
            service_factory=build_chat_service,
            session_factory=get_session,
            current_user_id=get_current_user_id,
        )
    )
    app.include_router(
        make_reviews_router(
            service_factory=build_review_service,
            session_factory=get_session,
            current_user_id=get_current_user_id,
        )
    )
    return app

docs.title: 6. Live notifications (SSE + Web Push)
docs.text:
A domain event — a new order for the seller, a new message for the recipient — has to arrive both ways: live with the app open (SSE) and in the background with the app closed (Web Push). A NotificationService takes the event once and fans it out to both channels.

What "fan-out" means here: you call notify(...) a single time, and under the hood the same event leaves through two independent paths — an SSE frame (for the app that's open right now) and a Web Push notification (for the app that's closed, delivered by the Service Worker). Both carry the same payload (data), so the client handles the notification the same way whether it arrived over SSE or push. One notify → two deliveries.

This step has three parts: (1) the Web Push subscription table, (2) the service that does the fan-out, and (3) wiring it into the app (the SSE subscribe endpoint + the push router). One at a time.

docs.title: Part 1 — the Web Push subscription table
docs.text:
The SSE side reuses the same SSEBroker as chat (section 3), now on a per-user channel (str(user_id)) instead of the conversation channel — no new moving part. Web Push, on the other hand, needs a per-device subscription table: the SDK ships the base row BaseWebPushSubscriptionModel and you create the concrete one with the FK to your UserModel (just like the recipe »):

# src/db/models.py (alongside the section 1 models)

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseWebPushSubscriptionModel


class WebPushSubscriptionModel(BaseWebPushSubscriptionModel):
    """A user's Web Push subscription (one row per device)."""

    __tablename__ = "web_push_subscriptions"
    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"), index=True
    )

docs.title: Part 2 — the fan-out service
docs.text:
The NotificationService is tiny: it holds the two pieces (the broker and the push service) and exposes a single notify(...) method. That method is what actually does the fan-out.

# src/services/notification.py
from uuid import UUID

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    SSEBroker,
    WebPushPayloadSchema,
    WebPushSubscriptionService,
)


class NotificationService:
    """Fan one domain event out to SSE (foreground) and Web Push (background)."""

    def __init__(self, broker: SSEBroker, push: WebPushSubscriptionService) -> None:
        """Wire the SSE broker and the Web Push subscription service.

        Args:
            broker (SSEBroker): Per-user fan-out for live (app-open) delivery.
            push (WebPushSubscriptionService): Delivers to a user's devices
                when the app is closed, pruning dead subscriptions.
        """
        self.broker = broker
        self.push = push

    async def notify(
        self,
        user_id: UUID,
        *,
        event: str,
        title: str,
        body: str,
        data: dict[str, object],
    ) -> None:
        """Deliver the same event on both channels.

        Args:
            user_id (UUID): The recipient — SSE channel and Web Push target.
            event (str): Event name (SSE `event:` field and push `tag`).
            title (str): Notification title (Web Push).
            body (str): Notification body / preview (Web Push).
            data (dict[str, object]): Shared payload carried by both channels.
        """
        await self.broker.publish(str(user_id), data, event=event)
        await self.push.notify_user(
            user_id,
            WebPushPayloadSchema(title=title, body=body, tag=event, data=data),
        )

The body of notify is two lines, one per channel:

  • await self.broker.publish(str(user_id), data, event=event) — the live (SSE) delivery. Publishes on the SSEBroker using the user id as the channel; every stream subscribed to that channel (the recipient's open app) gets the frame instantly. It's fire-and-forget: if nobody is connected, it does nothing and raises nothing.
  • await self.push.notify_user(user_id, WebPushPayloadSchema(...)) — the background (Web Push) delivery. notify_user looks up every subscription for that user, fires the push to each device and prunes dead ones on its own (expired or unsubscribed). The WebPushPayloadSchema wraps the title/body (the text the system notification shows), uses event as the tag, and carries the same data as the SSE frame.

Notice both lines get the same user_id as the target and the same data as the payload — that's what guarantees the open app (SSE) and the closed app (push) see exactly the same thing.

With the service in place, each business event calls notify once, passing the id of whoever should hear about it. The new order notifies the seller; the new chat message notifies the recipient:

import asyncio
from uuid import uuid4

from src.db.models import OrderModel, UserModel
from src.services.notification import notifications

conversation_id = uuid4()

user = UserModel(name="Ana", email="ana@example.com")
order = OrderModel(user_id=user.id, total=100)

preview = "Ainda está disponível?"

recipient_id = uuid4()

seller_id = uuid4()

sender_name = "Ana"


async def main() -> None:
    """Run this example."""
    # New order -> notify the seller (after persisting the order):
    await notifications.notify(
        seller_id,
        event="order_created",
        title="New order",
        body=f"Order for R$ {order.total}",
        data={"order_id": str(order.id), "total": str(order.total)},
    )

    # New chat message -> notify the recipient (after persisting the message):
    await notifications.notify(
        recipient_id,
        event="chat_message",
        title=sender_name,
        body=preview,
        data={"room_id": str(conversation_id)},
    )


asyncio.run(main())

Why each call's user_id is different:

  • New order → seller_id. The one who needs to know about the order is the seller, so the channel (and the push target) is their id. The buyer who placed the order gets nothing — they already know they bought.
  • New message → recipient_id. The one who needs to be told is whoever will receive the message, not whoever sent it. The channel is the recipient's id; the sender sees their own message through the chat's normal response.

In both cases, the id passed to notify is the same the recipient uses to subscribe over SSE (GET /notifications/stream, below): both sides must agree on the same channel string, otherwise the frame is published on a channel nobody is listening to.

docs.title: Part 3 — wiring it into the app
docs.text:
In the app, the client subscribes to its own channel with GET /notifications/stream, and Web Push plugs in via the ready-made make_web_push_router (/api/push/subscribe + /unsubscribe):

# src/api/app.py (additions to create_app)

from uuid import UUID

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseRepository,
    WebPushDispatcher,
    WebPushSubscriptionService,
    make_web_push_router,
)

from src.api.dependencies.auth import get_current_user_id
from src.api.dependencies.resources import get_session
from src.core.resources import settings
from src.db.models import WebPushSubscriptionModel
from src.services.chat import broker

app = FastAPI()


def build_push_service(session: AsyncSession) -> WebPushSubscriptionService:
    return WebPushSubscriptionService(
        BaseRepository(session, model=WebPushSubscriptionModel),
        WebPushDispatcher(**settings.webpush_kwargs()),
    )


@app.get("/notifications/stream")
async def notifications_stream(
    user_id: UUID = Depends(get_current_user_id),
) -> StreamingResponse:
    """Subscribe the caller to their live notification channel."""
    return broker.response(str(user_id))


app.include_router(
    make_web_push_router(
        service_factory=build_push_service,
        session_factory=get_session,
        current_user_id=get_current_user_id,
    )
)

Step by step, what happens on each GET /notifications/stream:

  1. Depends(get_current_user_id) resolves who the client is from the token. Their id becomes the channel name — each user has their own, isolated from the others.
  2. broker.response(str(user_id)) does three things in one call (the same shortcut the chat endpoint uses, now on a per-user channel):
    • register — creates a fresh EventStream and subscribes it to the user_id channel;
    • stream — returns a StreamingResponse with the SSE headers already set, and the client starts receiving;
    • unregister — wires an on_disconnect that removes this stream from the channel when the client drops, no hand-rolled try/finally.

It's the same broker as chat (imported from src.services.chat): a single SSEBroker in the process serves both uses, only the channel string changes — conversation_id in chat, user_id here.

With the app open, whoever holds the GET /notifications/stream gets the frame instantly — the same data the push would carry:

event: chat_message
data: {"room_id": "8c2f..."}

SSE can't send headers — authenticate via cookie or query

The native EventSource can't send Authorization. Use a session cookie on the same origin, or a short-lived access token in the query string. Both seams and the primitives (broker.response, backpressure, Redis bridge) live in the SSE recipe »; VAPID, the subscription table and dead-device pruning in the Web Push recipe ».

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
A whole local-commerce flow, from SDK blocks only:

  • Discovery — NominatimBackend geocodes the address, GeoRepositoryMixin.nearby finds sellers in the radius, estimate_travel gives the ETA. No paid API.
  • Chat — ChatService + make_chat_router with SSEBroker for live messages.
  • Notifications — NotificationService.notify sends one domain event (new order, new message) on both channels with the same payload: SSE (broker.publish, app open) and Web Push (notify_user, app closed).
  • Rating — ReviewService upserts one vote per user and aggregate yields the storefront numbers.
  • The SDK routers follow the same shape (service + session + current-user factories), so swapping auth or database never touches the module.

See the individual recipes: Geolocation », Chat », SSE », Web Push » and Comments + ratings ».

docs.title: 0.336.0 — security fixes (real time)
docs.text: Where What changes What to do SSEBroker with Redis With the default channel_prefix "sse", construction logs a WARNING: Redis pub/sub ignores the DB index, and another service on the same instance with the same prefix exchanges events with this one Pass a service-specific channel_prefix ("orders-api:sse") on every worker at once — workers with different prefixes do not see each other Web Push subscription (WebPushSubscriptionService.subscribe, make_web_push_router, web registration on make_push_router) An endpoint that is or resolves to a non-public address answers 422 PUSH_ENDPOINT_NOT_PUBLIC and is not stored; send_many returns for pruning a previously stored endpoint that is not https or whose host is a non-public IP literal Nothing, if the push service is public. Self-hosted push service on the internal network: allow_private_networks=True on the WebPushDispatcher opens subscription and delivery together

docs.title: 0.336.0 — password-change returns a fresh pair, set-password deletes passkeys
docs.text: Where What changes What to do POST /auth/password-change Answers 200 with LoginResponseSchema instead of 204 with no body, and the body takes an optional code. Account without MFA: a fresh pair, issued after every session is revoked (in cookies for a caller that authenticated with the access cookie). Account with MFA and no code: the password changes and the response is the login challenge (mfa_required: true, mfa_token), with no pair. With a valid code: a pair with an MFA amr; a wrong code: 401 and nothing changes Bearer client: store the response's pair and drop the old one; on an MFA account, send the code along or handle mfa_required as at login. A client that treated any 2xx as success does not break, but still gets signed out when the access token's TTL ends unless it stores the pair tempest user set-password Deletes the user's WebAuthn passkeys in the same transaction when it finds the table (--webauthn-credential-model, default src.db.models:UserWebAuthnCredentialModel) --keep-passkeys keeps the old behaviour; tell the user they register their passkey again signup(fields=...) and signup_schema totp_secret, totp_enabled_at, totp_last_step and every __secret_columns__ column of the user model are refused (ValueError in the service, dropped by the route) Nothing for the MFA columns, which only the enrollment flow writes. If your signup writes a __secret_columns__ column of your own, move that write to on_signup IntrospectionAuth New audiences=; without it, one WARNING per instance at construction Pass audiences= with the service's client id at the provider. See Bind the token to this service

docs.text: Where What changes What to do CORSSettings with ENV=production With CORS_ALLOW_CREDENTIALS=true, "null" in CORS_ORIGINS or a CORS_ORIGIN_REGEX that matches a .invalid origin (.*, https://.*) stop the boot, as "*" already did List the frontend origins in CORS_ORIGINS, or anchor the regex to your domain accel_redirect_response, serve_object(accel_redirect=True) A media_type outside type/subtype (parameter, comma, CR/LF) raises ValueError, as in presigned_get_url; text/plain; charset=utf-8 is no longer accepted on this path Pass the type without parameters (text/plain) Text search (search, search_condition, full_text_search) hashed_password and the __secret_columns__ answer 422; the message becomes ... has no searchable column ..., and details["allowed"] only appears when the repository declares searchable_columns If the search takes the field from the request, declare searchable_columns on the repository StripeClient create, retrieve, update and delete raise StripeObjectMismatchError when the response's object is not the resource's Handle it where you handle StripeError today (it is a subclass) ps_single_quote (hostbridge) Also doubles the typographic quotes U+2018–U+201B Nothing

docs.title: 0.335.0 — BaseUserModel gains the email_verified_at column
docs.text:
BaseUserModel now maps email_verified_at (timezone-aware timestamp, nullable): when the account holder proved they read the current address. Since the column is mapped on the base, migrate the database before upgrading the package: without it, every query on the user model fails (no such column: users.email_verified_at, measured with SQLite).

The behaviour change: social login's link by email (AUTH_OAUTH_LINK_BY_VERIFIED_EMAIL=true) now requires the column to be set. An existing account has NULL, so it stops being linked by email (409 OAUTH_EMAIL_TAKEN) until it proves the address — through POST /auth/email-verify/request and the link that arrives in the mailbox. A service with the knob off (the default) changes nothing beyond the migration. What sets and what clears the column is in What counts as a verified email.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
1. Generate the migration (uv run tempest db revision -m "email verified at", or alembic revision --autogenerate) or write it by hand:

    import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import op

revision: str = "email_verified_at"
down_revision: str | None = "<the previous revision>"


def upgrade() -> None:
    """Add the proof of email ownership."""
    op.add_column(
        "users",
        sa.Column("email_verified_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True), nullable=True),
    )


def downgrade() -> None:
    """Drop the proof of email ownership."""
    op.drop_column("users", "email_verified_at")

  2. Run uv run tempest db upgrade (or alembic upgrade head) and only then deploy the new version.

docs.title: Backfilling existing accounts — your decision
docs.text:
The SDK fills nothing for you: it does not know how each existing account became active. Backfill only if you know the active accounts in the database were activated through the mailed link — that is, the service always ran with AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=false, AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE=false and EmailUtils wired, and nobody activated an account from the admin site or through tempest user activate. If any of that failed for part of the database, narrow the WHERE to the rest (by created_at, for instance) or do not backfill.

There is no column holding the activation time; created_at is the lower bound the database knows, and it is the value the step below writes. Add to the migration's upgrade():

import sqlalchemy as sa
from alembic import op


def upgrade() -> None:
    """Mark the active accounts, activated by email, as verified."""
    users = sa.table(
        "users",
        sa.column("is_active", sa.Boolean()),
        sa.column("created_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True)),
        sa.column("email_verified_at", sa.TIMESTAMP(timezone=True)),
    )
    op.execute(
        users.update()
        .where(users.c.is_active.is_(True), users.c.email_verified_at.is_(None))
        .values(email_verified_at=users.c.created_at)
    )

Without this step, an account that wants to link social login by email verifies its address once, and linking works again.

docs.title: 0.335.0 — security fixes that change behaviour
docs.text:
This release closes vulnerabilities, and several fixes swap an unsafe default for a safe one. The table says what changes for existing users of the SDK and what to do. Each item is detailed in the CHANGELOG and in the recipe named.

Where What changes What to do ENV=production AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=true or AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE=true stop the boot; without EmailUtils on UserAuthService (with an auth_settings that composes EnvironmentSettings), the flows that send a link answer 503 INTEGRATION_DISABLED Turn both flags off in production and pass email= to the service key_by_header is_known= is required; without it, TypeError Pass a synchronous check that says whether the header value is a key you issued IdempotencyMiddleware Requests without a credential are not deduplicated; entries written by an older version answer 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED until they expire Pass allow_anonymous=True only if you need to deduplicate anonymous POSTs; wait out the TTL of old entries WebhookSignatureVerifier, make_stripe_webhook_dependency An empty secret raises ValueError at construction Configure the webhook secret before booting POST /auth/webauthn/register/begin Requires a WebAuthnRegisterBeginSchema body (current_password and, with MFA, code); without it, 422 Update the client to ask for the password before registering a passkey Password reset and mfa_reset Delete the user's passkeys revoke_passkeys=False keeps the old behaviour; tell users they register their passkey again make_admin_router with access_policy The SQL console, tasks and logs are denied to everyone Pass surface_policy= granting whoever should see them Admin The SDK's credential columns (totp_secret, push keys, token digests) disappear from the screens, list_display included;
