get_api_v1_cashback_fidelity_balance_by_tax_id get_cashback_fidelity_balance get_api_v1_charge list_charges post_api_v1_charge create_charge delete_api_v1_charge_by_id delete_charge get_api_v1_charge_by_id get_charge patch_api_v1_charge_by_id update_charge get_api_v1_charge_by_id_refund list_charge_refunds post_api_v1_charge_by_id_refund refund_charge get_api_v1_company get_company get_api_v1_customer list_customers post_api_v1_customer create_customer patch_api_v1_customer_by_correlation_id update_customer get_api_v1_customer_by_id get_customer post_api_v1_decode_emv decode_emv get_api_v1_dispute list_disputes get_api_v1_dispute_by_id get_dispute post_api_v1_funds_recovery create_funds_recovery get_api_v1_funds_recovery_by_id get_funds_recovery post_api_v1_funds_recovery_by_id_cancel cancel_funds_recovery get_api_v1_installments_by_id get_installment post_api_v1_installments_by_id_cobr create_installment_cobr post_api_v1_installments_by_id_cobr_retry retry_installment_cobr get_api_v1_invoice list_invoices post_api_v1_invoice create_invoice get_api_v1_invoice_integration get_invoice_integration 2. Three methods have no direct replacement.

Before Now What was wrong post_api_v1_dispute_id_evidence(body=...) upload_dispute_evidence(id, *, body=...) The path was /api/v1/dispute/:id/evidence, colon and all, and no argument named the dispute get_api_v1_account_register() get_account_register(id) The docstring said "by CorrelationID" and the method took nothing delete_api_v1_payment_by_id(id) removed The endpoint does not exist: the published document has only get on that path, and the DELETE Woovi documents is on /api/v1/charge/{id}

3. Operation-derived schema classes were renamed. The components ones were not — Charge, ChargePayload, ChargeStatus, Transaction, Customer are unchanged. The inline ones moved:

The name up to v0.259.0 was GetApiV1ChargeResponsePageInfo. From v0.260.0:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.openpix import (
    ListChargesResponsePageInfo,
)

The pattern follows the method: GetApiV1ChargeResponse… becomes ListChargesResponse…, PostApiV1PaymentBody… becomes CreatePaymentBody….

4. OpenPixEnvironment.PRODUCTION is now https://api.woovi.com. That is servers[0] of the refreshed document. The old host is still up — measured 2026-08-28, GET /api/v1/charge answers 401 on api.openpix.com.br, api.woovi.com and api.woovi-sandbox.com alike — so a service pinned to the old URL keeps working. If you assert the value in a test, update it.

5. If you read model_extra from a model that is also a payload. A class reachable from a response and from a request body goes back to extra="ignore". That is 4 classes on OpenPix — PreRegistrationPayloadObject, which is the body and the 200 of the same operation, plus the three it reaches — and 25 on Mercado Pago. The reason is what v0.259.0 already stated and could not enforce: an unexpected key on a payload is the caller's own typo, and carrying it to the provider is worse than dropping it.

docs.title: What you get for free
docs.text:
• 24 new operations: anticipation (7), stablecoin payout and wallets (7), boleto-transaction (2), kyc-validation (2), files, webhook/public-keys.
  • Transaction.webhook_sent[].status becomes an int — it is an HTTP code.
  • to_cents and reais_to_cents refuse with ValueError, always. Before, "abc" raised decimal.InvalidOperation, None raised TypeError and float("inf") raised OverflowError.

docs.title: 0.259.0 — OpenPix money becomes int
docs.text: Breaks anyone who annotated a variable with the generated model's type, or who compares a dump against an expected JSON string.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
154 fields of the integrations/payment/openpix package stop being float:

  • monetary values — Charge.value, ChargePayload.value, ChargeRefundPayload.value, Transaction.value, SubAccount.balance, every pix*Limit, and the rest of the document's 50 value fields;
  • counts and day offsets — skip and limit, installmentsCount, dayDue, daysForDueDate, expiresIn. The pagination pair appeared 27 times as a response field (pageInfo, Pagination) and on 6 operations as a query parameter.

Woovi settles in whole centavos — the specification says so in the field's own description on 58 numeric schemas — and typed all of it number. The visible effect is on the wire:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.openpix import ChargePayload

ChargePayload(correlation_id="abc-1", value=1000).model_dump(
    by_alias=True, mode="json", exclude_none=True
)
# up to v0.258.0: {"correlationID": "abc-1", "value": 1000.0, ...}
# from v0.259.0:  {"correlationID": "abc-1", "value": 1000, ...}

19 fields stay float: basePrice (an exchange rate), inputAmount/outputAmount on the stablecoin quote (the first is documented as "currency unit, not cents"), rate, the rate-limit token bucket, annualRevenue and Installment.expiration — the last two with no unit stated in the document, which is why they were left alone.

Corrected in v0.260.0

This section originally said "18 fields", and that they were "the only ones where the fraction is real". There were 19, and one of them was Transaction.webhookSent[].status, described in the document itself as "HTTP response status code of the webhook delivery attempt" — an HTTP status code is never fractional. It became an int in v0.260.0.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
Nothing, in most cases — an int satisfies at runtime wherever a float was expected. Check three things:

  • Your own annotations. amount: float = charge.value is now a type error. Change it to int.
  • Dump comparisons in tests. assert dumped == {"value": 1000.0} still passes (1000 == 1000.0), but a comparison against a JSON string, or a snapshot of model_dump_json(), does not.
  • to_cents over a generated model. It still works and still validates (refusing negatives and fractions), it simply narrows nothing any more. For a raw payload — the dictionary out of the JSON, a webhook — it is still the right call.

docs.title: The other half: your fields stop disappearing
docs.text:
Generated response models now use extra="allow". A field the provider returns and the specification does not declare lands in model_extra instead of being dropped during validation:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.openpix import Charge

charge = Charge.model_validate({"value": 1000, "wooviAddedThis": "later"})
(charge.model_extra or {})["wooviAddedThis"]   # "later"

Payload models are unchanged: they keep extra="ignore", because there an unexpected key is the caller's own typo.

Three fields that were in exactly that situation are now declared and typed: Charge.fee, Charge.discount and Charge.value_with_discount. If you were reading any of them through the raw HTTPClient because of this, the generated method is now enough.

docs.title: 0.258.0 — log files now rotate
docs.text: No signature breaks. What changes is what sits on disk: anyone reading logs/info.log from outside the SDK now sees a window, not the whole history.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
The per-level handlers were logging.FileHandler — unbounded growth. They are now RotatingFileHandler with max_bytes=10_000_000 and backup_count=5, so each level stops at ~60 MB (five rotated files plus the one being written), and info.log.1, info.log.2, … appear next to the current file.

The reason already closed the reader side of this pair: the /logs router caps reads at DEFAULT_MAX_RECORDS_PER_FILE = 20_000 records per file, added after a service whose log directory had grown to gigabytes answered with a dead worker. On a service that logs one line per request, running on a long-lived host, info.log is what fills the disk — and a full disk takes down the service along with whatever else shares the partition.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
Nothing, in most cases. Check two things:

  • A collector that follows the file by name. Filebeat, Promtail, Fluent Bit and friends handle rotation, but a hand-rolled tail -F, or a script that opens the file once at boot, misses the turnover. Point the pattern at info.log* if you need the rotated files.
  • GET /logs shows the current window. The endpoint reads the exact names (info.log, error.log, …), so rotated files are not in the response. Longer retention is a collector's job, not the endpoint's.

docs.title: If you want the old behavior
docs.text:
max_bytes=0 restores the plain FileHandler — for a host where logrotate or a sidecar already owns retention:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import configure_logging

configure_logging(level="INFO", max_bytes=0)

Both knobs are keyword-only and independent: backup_count is only read when rotation is on.

docs.title: 0.257.0 — the agent fakes rename the parameter to tools
docs.text: Breaks callers passing chat_with_tools(..., specs=[...]) by keyword.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
ScriptedBackend and FailingBackend exist to fake the ChatBackend / ToolCallingBackend protocols — and satisfied neither under mypy. The protocol names the parameter tools and accepts **kwargs; the fakes named it specs and accepted nothing else. A protocol member is only implemented by a signature with the same parameter name, so the opening line of the testing recipe was a type error:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.agents import Agent
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.agents.testing import ScriptedBackend, replies

agent = Agent(ScriptedBackend([replies("ok")]))
# up to v0.256.0:
# Argument 1 to "Agent" has incompatible type "ScriptedBackend";
# expected "ChatBackend | ToolCallingBackend"  [arg-type]

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
Nothing, if you call positionally — which is what Agent does internally and what the recipe shows. If your test calls the fake directly, by keyword:

-decision = await backend.chat_with_tools(messages, specs=specs)
+decision = await backend.chat_with_tools(messages, tools=specs)

The specs_seen attribute — where the fake records the tool names offered each turn — did not change name.

docs.title: What started compiling
docs.text:
Three annotations that rejected the argument the docs themselves told you to pass:

  • EventStream.response(on_disconnect=task.cancel), because Task.cancel returns bool and the annotation asked for None;
  • RedisIdempotencyStore(Redis.from_url(...)), RedisResponseCacheStore(...) and RedisWebAuthnChallengeStore(...), because the protocols demanded the parameter name key/name and a Coroutine return, while redis-py returns an Awaitable;
  • require_authenticated(identity) with a FirebaseIdentity, because the TypeVar was bound to BaseUserModel.

None of them changes runtime — they only stop demanding a workaround (# type: ignore, cast) from anyone running a type checker.

docs.title: 0.256.0 — the RateLimitMiddleware 429 becomes JSON
docs.text: Breaks clients that read the 429 body as text.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
Up to v0.255.0 the middleware answered text/plain with the raw error_message:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8

Too many requests

It now answers the same envelope register_exception_handlers writes in every handler:

HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
retry-after: 60

{"detail": "Too many requests",
 "code": "TOO_MANY_REQUESTS",
 "details": {"retry_after_seconds": 60, "limit": 15}}

The reason is a contradiction inside the SDK itself: error_responses() always pointed 429 at ErrorResponseSchema, so a client generated from the OpenAPI schema broke deserializing the text -- and anyone adopting register_exception_handlers alongside the middleware ended up with two error shapes in one API.

docs.title: What to do
docs.text:
• A client branching on status === 429: nothing. The status and Retry-After are unchanged.
  • A client reading the body as text: read JSON instead, using detail to display and code to branch.
// before
const message = await response.text();

// after
const { detail, code } = await response.json();
  • A service that rewrote the response (a middleware subclass turning the text into an envelope) can delete the workaround: error_message plus the new error_code cover it.

docs.title: If you need the text back
docs.text: There is no flag for it. The old body was incompatible with the schema the route itself documents, and keeping both shapes would keep the defect behind an option. A service that genuinely needs another format can subclass the middleware and override the response, the way it did before.

docs.title: 0.252.0 — SQLite :memory: gets one connection per session
docs.text: No API break. It changes the connection topology of a :memory: database, so read this before upgrading if you rely on the old behaviour.

docs.title: What changes
docs.text:
AsyncDatabaseManager("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:") now builds the engine over a shared-cache in-memory database (file:<unique-name>?mode=memory&cache=shared&uri=true) with a normal pool, instead of letting SQLAlchemy pick StaticPool with a single connection. The manager holds one connection open for its lifetime, because a shared-cache database dies with its last connection.

This fixes the error introduced in v0.200.0, when the explicit BEGIN started being emitted for every SQLite engine:

sqlite3.OperationalError: cannot start a transaction within a transaction
[SQL: BEGIN]

Two overlapping sessions work again on :memory:, and RELEASE SAVEPOINT still is not a commit in disguise.

docs.title: If you rely on a single connection
docs.text:
Pass the pool explicitly — a pool the caller names is never overridden:

from sqlalchemy.pool import StaticPool
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AsyncDatabaseManager

db = AsyncDatabaseManager("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:", poolclass=StaticPool)

That restores the previous topology, including its failure on overlapping sessions.

docs.title: If you swapped :memory: for a temp file as a workaround
docs.text: You can go back to :memory:. The workaround keeps working, so there is no rush.

docs.title: 0.251.0 — the Mercado Pago webhook signature now follows the provider's algorithm
docs.text: Breaks anyone passing manifest_template= or unpacking the return of parse_signature_header. If you only call verify_signature, nothing in your code changes — it simply starts verifying deliveries it used to reject.

docs.title: The manifest omits absent pairs, so it is no longer a template
docs.text:
The previous implementation rendered "id:{data_id};request-id:{request_id};ts:{ts};". Mercado Pago's official validator (mercadopago/sdk-nodejs, src/utils/webhook/index.ts, commit 99857f33) omits the pair whose value is absent. A delivery without data.id signs request-id:...;ts:...;, while the fixed template signed id:;request-id:...;ts:...; — a different hash, and verification that always failed.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.mercado_pago import build_manifest

# before: DEFAULT_MANIFEST_TEMPLATE + str.format
# now: the rule, exported
build_manifest(data_id="", request_id="req-1", timestamp="1771891200")
# "request-id:req-1;ts:1771891200;"

DEFAULT_MANIFEST_TEMPLATE and the manifest_template= parameter were removed: they existed because the algorithm was unknown, and a template cannot express the omission rule. If you had measured a different manifest and were passing your own, compare it against build_manifest and open an issue if it still differs.

docs.title: parse_signature_header returns an object, not a tuple
docs.text:
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.mercado_pago import parse_signature_header

# before
# timestamp, digest = parse_signature_header(header)

# now
parsed = parse_signature_header("ts=1771891200,v1=abc123")
parsed.timestamp        # "1771891200"
parsed.digest()         # "abc123" — the first supported version
parsed.hashes           # {"v1": "abc123"} — a header may carry v1 and v2

docs.title: What is new
docs.text:
• versions= on verify_signature, defaulting to ("v1",). A provider migration to v2 becomes versions=("v2", "v1"), with no release to wait for.
  • tolerance_seconds= (and now=, for tests), which is what makes the manifest's ts work against replay. Still opt-in, as upstream has it.
  • Case-insensitive header keys, whitespace-only values treated as absent, and a non-numeric ts rejected as a malformed header — three upstream rules that were missing.

docs.title: 0.234.0 — a generated model is built with its Python names, and the type-checker agrees
docs.text: Nothing changes at runtime. What changes is what pyright accepts.

docs.title: Construct with the field name, not the alias
docs.text:
Fields carrying a wire name moved from Field(alias=...) to Field(validation_alias=..., serialization_alias=...). Runtime is identical — the models already set populate_by_name=True, so both spellings always validated. What changes is the parameter a type-checker sees:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.openpix import ChargePayload

# before: it ran, but pyright reported "No parameter named correlation_id"
# now: both accept it
payload = ChargePayload(correlation_id="order-1", value=1990)

If your code used the alias purely to silence the checker (ChargePayload(correlationID="order-1")), it still runs — validation takes the alias — but the checker now objects. Switch to the Python name.

Reading and writing are unchanged: model_validate({"correlationID": ...}) still accepts the provider's spelling, and model_dump(by_alias=True) still emits it.

docs.title: 0.233.0 — two generated OpenPix enums were renamed
docs.text: One change, and it only breaks code importing the two payment enums by name.

docs.title: PaymentType and PaymentDestinationAliasType were renamed
docs.text:
The generator now emits the variants of PaymentCreatePayload (a oneOf with four shapes: Pix key, QR Code, Manual, Boleto), and those are what register the enums first. The name now comes from the variant:

Before Now PaymentType PaymentCreatePayloadPixKeyType PaymentDestinationAliasType PaymentCreatePayloadPixKeyDestinationAliasType

Same members, same values — only the class name changed:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.integrations.payment.openpix import (
    PaymentCreatePayloadPixKeyType,
)

assert PaymentCreatePayloadPixKeyType.PIX_KEY.value == "PIX_KEY"

If you compared the value instead of importing the class (payment.type == "PIX_KEY"), there is nothing to do.

docs.title: What did not break
docs.text: PaymentCreatePayload and PostApiV1PaymentBody are still importable: they became union aliases over the variants, so an annotation like body: PostApiV1PaymentBody stays valid. What changed is that they now carry the payment's fields — before they were models with no properties at all, and extra="ignore" silently dropped everything you passed.

docs.title: 0.229.0 — Ollama structured output moves from /api/generate to /api/chat
docs.text: One change, and it only breaks tests, not runtime.

docs.title: generate_structured now talks to /api/chat
docs.text:
OllamaGenerator.generate_structured posted to /api/generate with the schema in the format field. That is broken on a reasoning model: against gpt-oss:20b the daemon answers 200 OK with a non-zero eval_count and an empty response, because the reply lands in a channel that endpoint does not surface. On /api/chat the JSON arrives in message.content, and a non-reasoning model behaves identically on either.

There is nothing to adjust at runtime — the call that returned junk (or nothing) now returns the instance. What breaks is a test whose mock is pinned to the old endpoint:

import httpx
from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import OllamaGenerator
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import HTTPClient


class Person(BaseModel):
    name: str


async def before() -> Person:
    """A mock that matched /api/generate — it stops matching."""

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        return httpx.Response(200, json={"response": '{"name": "Ana"}', "done": True})

    client = HTTPClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    gen = OllamaGenerator("llama3.2", http_client=client)
    return await gen.generate_structured("Any person.", Person)


async def after() -> Person:
    """The reply now comes in message.content."""

    def handler(request: httpx.Request) -> httpx.Response:
        return httpx.Response(
            200,
            json={"message": {"content": '{"name": "Ana"}'}, "done": True},
        )

    client = HTTPClient(transport=httpx.MockTransport(handler))
    gen = OllamaGenerator("llama3.2", http_client=client)
    return await gen.generate_structured("Any person.", Person)

Two behaviour changes come with it:

  • Empty content raises ValueError instead of returning nothing. If you had a try/except treating an empty result as "the model said nothing", switch it to except ValueError.
  • system= is a new optional parameter. Use it for the instruction when prompt is a long document: an instruction glued above the document is ignored — measured, 0 items extracted against 20 with the instruction in its own system turn.

docs.title: 0.174.0 — crashes become 422s, and order_by is validated
docs.text: Robustness fixes. Each trades a crash for a correct answer; none requires a code change, but four change the status or the exception your service sees.

docs.title: A long password is now a 422
docs.text:
There is a ceiling: AUTH_PASSWORD_MAX_BYTES, default 72 — bcrypt's hard limit, counted in UTF-8 bytes. A password past it used to raise ValueError from hashpw and surface as a 500 on signup / reset / change. It is now a ValidationException (422).

If your frontend does not validate length, it starts receiving 422 where it received 500. If you swapped the hasher for one without the limit, raise the value.

docs.title: An invalid order_by is now a ValidationException
docs.text:
BaseRepository.paginate and cursor_paginate resolve order_by through the model's mapper. A name that is not a mapped column raises ValidationException (422) instead of AttributeError (500).

Contract change in cursor_paginate: it used to raise ValueError there. Code catching ValueError around it needs updating:

import asyncio

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession, create_async_engine
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseRepository
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions import ValidationException

from src.db.models import UserModel

# In a service the session comes from `db.get_session_context()`; here, SQLite.
session = AsyncSession(create_async_engine("sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:"))

repo = BaseRepository(session, model=UserModel)


async def main() -> None:
    """Run this example."""
    try:
        page = await repo.cursor_paginate(order_by="not_a_column")
    except ValidationException:
        ...


asyncio.run(main())

ValueError still signals a malformed cursor.

docs.title: BodySizeLimitMiddleware: a streaming oversize body answers 413
docs.text:
The 413 is now emitted the moment the count is exceeded, and whatever the app sends afterwards is dropped. It used to go out in a finally, after the app had answered — and FastAPI does answer, converting the guard's ClientDisconnect into a 400. The second http.response.start made uvicorn raise RuntimeError: Response already started.

In practice: a streaming upload over the limit answers 413 where it recently answered 400 (with a RuntimeError in the log). A handler that never reads the body still answers whatever it answered before — a sent response cannot be retracted.

docs.title: make_csrf_token_dependency sets the cookie
docs.text:
It used to only return the token, so the cookie stayed absent and the following POST was rejected with a 403. It now sets it (Secure + SameSite=Lax, and not HttpOnly — the client must read it to echo the header).

If you were already setting the cookie by hand in the handler, the value is the same (request.state.csrf_token) and nothing changes: the dependency does not overwrite an existing cookie. On a plain-HTTP dev server pass secure=False, or the browser will not send it back.

docs.title: OAuthUser.email_verified
docs.text: A new field (default None), so nothing breaks. But read the note: if you link a social login to an existing account by email, require profile.email_verified is True. On GitHub the value is always None — GET /user carries no verification field, and the email it returns is the public profile one, which GitHub does not require verifying.

docs.title: GET /logs reads at most 20,000 records per file
docs.text: Tune it with make_logs_router(max_records_per_file=...). They are the newest ones; the endpoint sorts newest-first and paginates, so what was left out was unreachable. A WARNING is logged when the cap bites.

docs.title: 0.173.0 — a token only works where it was meant to, and caches stop being shared
docs.text: Three security fixes change default behavior. None requires a code change, but check whether you were relying on the old behavior.

docs.title: Refresh and MFA-pending tokens no longer authorize a route
docs.text:
make_bearer_token_dependency, make_jwt_user_dependency, make_role_dependency, make_permission_dependency and UserAuthService.current_user_dependency() now accept only access-type tokens.

Before, the three JWTs UserAuthService mints with one secret verified identically, so the refresh token and the step-one mfa_token worked as a bearer on any authenticated route — the second factor was bypassable with just the password.

You are affected if you deliberately sent a refresh token to a regular route:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    JWTUtils,
    REFRESH_TOKEN_TYPE,
    make_bearer_token_dependency,
)

from src.core.settings import settings

tokens = JWTUtils(settings)


# Take that type again, on that one route:
require_refresh = make_bearer_token_dependency(tokens, accepted_typ=(REFRESH_TOKEN_TYPE,))

A token hand-signed with JWTUtils.encode() and carrying no typ is still accepted — the upgrade does not log live sessions out. Only the markers the SDK itself stamped (refresh: True, purpose: "mfa_pending") are now rejected as access.

docs.title: ResponseCacheMiddleware: private by default, credentials skip the store
docs.text:
Two defaults changed:

  • The emitted Cache-Control went from public, max-age=N to private, max-age=N. If you served genuinely shared content and relied on CDN caching, declare it again: cache_control="public, max-age=N".
  • A request with Authorization or Cookie neither reads nor writes the shared store (ETag/304 still apply). To get caching back on an authenticated route, pass cache_credentialed=True — the credential joins the key, so each caller gets its own entry.

The X-Cache header now only appears when a store= is configured; it used to report MISS even in ETag-only mode.

docs.title: IdempotencyMiddleware: key scoped to the caller
docs.text:
The key went from (method, path, key) to (caller, method, path, key), the caller being a digest of Authorization/Cookie. Reusing someone else's key no longer returns their response.

If your client swaps credentials between the original request and the retry (a token rotation mid-backoff), the retry no longer hits the earlier entry. Point identity at something stable there:

from fastapi import FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import IdempotencyMiddleware, MemoryIdempotencyStore

store = MemoryIdempotencyStore()

app = FastAPI()


app.add_middleware(
    IdempotencyMiddleware,
    store=store,
    principal_resolver=lambda request: request.headers.get("x-api-key-id", ""),
)

Also changed: 5xx is no longer cached (cache_server_errors=True restores it), Set-Cookie is left out of the stored copy, and concurrent requests sharing a key are serialized within a process.

docs.title: 0.138.1 — BaseAppSettings must be the last base
docs.text:
0.138.1 made every settings mixin inherit BaseAppSettings (they used to extend raw pydantic_settings.BaseSettings). That fixes .env silently not loading when a mixin was listed before the base — the canonical model_config is now materialized onto every mixin regardless of ordering.

In exchange, base ordering stopped being style and became a hard rule: because the mixins subclass BaseAppSettings, Python's C3 linearization forbids the base from preceding its own subclass.

# docs-guard: skip — the first two examples are the mistake this section describes
# ❌ fails at import time

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, DatabaseSettings, RedisSettings


class Settings(DatabaseSettings, BaseAppSettings, RedisSettings): ...

# ❌ also fails
class Settings(BaseAppSettings, DatabaseSettings): ...

# ✅ BaseAppSettings last
class Settings(DatabaseSettings, RedisSettings, BaseAppSettings): ...

Before 0.159.1 the symptom was pydantic's raw TypeError, which never names the fix:

TypeError: Cannot create a consistent method resolution order (MRO) for bases BaseAppSettings, RedisSettings

and mypy (with the pydantic plugin) reported twice on the same line, the second one misleading — it suggests a metaclass conflict when the cause is just the position of one base:

settings.py:4: error: Cannot determine consistent method resolution order (MRO) for "Settings"  [misc]
settings.py:4: error: Metaclass conflict: the metaclass of a derived class must be a (non-strict) subclass of the metaclasses of all its bases  [metaclass]

As of 0.159.1, BaseAppSettings uses the AppSettingsMeta metaclass, which pre-checks base ordering and swaps the message for an instruction:

TypeError: Settings: BaseAppSettings must be the LAST base — RedisSettings already subclasses it, so listing BaseAppSettings before it is an invalid method resolution order (MRO). Move BaseAppSettings to the end of the base list: class Settings(RedisSettings, BaseAppSettings).

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
# look for a Settings whose BaseAppSettings is not the last base
grep -rn "class Settings(" -A 12 src/core/settings.py
  • Move BaseAppSettings to the last position in the base list.
  • Ordering among the mixins stays free — only the base's position matters.
  • No env var, field or value change: this is purely inheritance order.

docs.title: 0.92.0 — payload column on the user token
docs.text:
0.92.0 adds the email change / re-verification / recovery flow. To carry the pending email until confirmation, BaseUserTokenModel gained a new column:

from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column


payload: Mapped[str | None] = mapped_column(String(320), nullable=True, default=None)

Since your user_tokens table inherits from BaseUserTokenModel, the column shows up on the model automatically — but the database needs a migration. It is additive and safe (nullable column, no required default):

# generate and apply
tempest db revision -m "add payload to user_tokens"
tempest db upgrade

Or by hand:

ALTER TABLE user_tokens ADD COLUMN payload VARCHAR(320) NULL;

That's it

No renames, no default backfill. Existing flows (activation, password reset) keep writing payload = NULL. The new email flow is fully opt-in — recovery (POST /auth/email-recovery/request) is only mounted with AUTH_EMAIL_RECOVERY_ENABLED=True.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
• Run the migration before deploying 0.92.0 (the column must exist).
  • If you hand-write src/db/models/user_token.py instead of using make_user_token_model, the column comes from the abstract base — no need to redeclare, just migrate.

docs.title: 0.63.0 — authenticated user loaded on the request session
docs.text:
Before 0.63.0, UserAuthService.current_user_dependency() loaded the authenticated user through load_user, which opened its own session (via db.get_session_context()) and closed it on exit. The UserModel handed to the route was therefore detached: mutating it and calling commit/refresh on the request session (the one your repositories use) raised InvalidRequestError: Instance is not persistent within this Session.

From 0.63.0 the dependency loads the user on the request session (db.session_dependency by default) via get_user(subject, session). The user is attached to the same session repositories use, so lazy-relationship reads and writes work without re-attaching anything.

Compatibility

The auth dependency and your repositories must share the same session callable for FastAPI's sub-dependency cache to deduplicate them. The recommended pattern is already covered:

# resources.py
get_session = db.session_dependency          # one object, reused

If you wrap the session in your own provider (async def get_session(): ...), pass it explicitly, otherwise the dependency opens a second session and the user is detached again:

get_current_user = auth.current_user_dependency(session_dependency=get_session)

Extra safety net

BaseRepository.resolve() now re-attaches detached instances via session.merge(). Even if some flow still hands in a detached user, resolve brings it back into the active session instead of breaking — so services that worked around this (re-fetch by id before mutating) can drop the workaround.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
• Drop any "re-fetch by id before mutating the authenticated user" workaround — it's no longer needed.
  • A single-argument user_loader passed to make_jwt_user_dependency keeps working. To share the request session, pass session_dependency= and use a two-argument loader (subject, session).

docs.title: 0.8.0 — ServerSettings rename
docs.text: 0.8.0 renames every field on ServerSettings, extracts log fields to a new LogSettings mixin, and adds eleven other primitives. The renames are the only breaking changes — every new primitive is opt-in.

docs.title: 1. Rename env vars
docs.text:
Old New Mixin HOST SERVER_HOST ServerSettings PORT SERVER_PORT ServerSettings DEBUG SERVER_DEBUG ServerSettings (new) SERVER_RELOAD ServerSettings LOG_LEVEL LOG_LEVEL moved to LogSettings LOG_JSON LOG_JSON moved to LogSettings

Mechanical sed on every .env / docker-compose.yml / deployment manifest:

sed -i \
  -e 's/^HOST=/SERVER_HOST=/' \
  -e 's/^PORT=/SERVER_PORT=/' \
  -e 's/^DEBUG=/SERVER_DEBUG=/' \
  .env .env.example .env.test

LOG_LEVEL and LOG_JSON keep their names — only the mixin moves.

docs.title: 2. Rename code references
docs.text:
# `settings.HOST` → `settings.SERVER_HOST`, same for PORT/DEBUG
grep -rn "settings\.\(HOST\|PORT\|DEBUG\)\b" src/ tests/

Replace each match with the SERVER_* form. If a service was using the old settings.DEBUG flag for application-level debug behavior, switch to settings.SERVER_DEBUG; if it was only being read for uvicorn auto-reload, switch to settings.SERVER_RELOAD.

docs.title: 3. Mix LogSettings into the project Settings
docs.text:
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
     BaseAppSettings,
     CORSSettings,
     DatabaseSettings,
     JWTSettings,
+    LogSettings,
     RabbitMQSettings,
     RedisSettings,
     ServerSettings,
 )


 class Settings(
     ServerSettings,
+    LogSettings,
     DatabaseSettings,
     RedisSettings,
     RabbitMQSettings,
     JWTSettings,
     CORSSettings,
     BaseAppSettings,
 ):
     ...

Skip this step if the service never read settings.LOG_LEVEL / settings.LOG_JSON — configure_logging accepts the values as keyword arguments directly.

docs.title: 4. (Optional) Adopt the new primitives
docs.text:
Pick what fits. None of these are required.

  • Replace the hand-written src/server.py uvicorn.run(...) with run_server(...).
  • Replace the hand-written get_current_user with make_jwt_user_dependency(tokens, load_user).
  • Move SMTP_* / UPLOAD_* / TOKEN_SECRET / VAPID_* / TASKIQ_* fields out of the project's Settings and onto the matching SDK mixin (Settings mixins composition).
  • Adopt the Outbox if you already write side-effects from the same transaction as your domain rows.

docs.title: 5. Verify
docs.text:
uv sync                      # picks up new pyproject deps
uv run pytest -q             # full suite
uv run ruff check src tests  # confirm no `HOST`/`PORT`/`DEBUG` references slipped

If pytest fails with a Pydantic ValidationError referencing HOST / PORT / DEBUG, an env var was not renamed (look at the process environment or .env).

docs.title: Recommended architecture
docs.text:
The Architecture page says which layers exist. This one says how each file inside them is shaped, in a way that works the same for someone joining the project and for an AI writing code in it: a file's name says what it holds, the dependency graph is predictable, and the suite explains what each test proves.

Every rule here has a code that tempest check enforces. That is the point: in a real service (transport-backend, recorded in #616), the rules that lived only in CLAUDE.md were broken in hundreds of places when the first guard was written. Prose is not a gate.

tempest new already ships this way

The project tempest new writes passes every rule on this page, errors and warnings, and turns layers_strict = true on. Why each directory it generates exists, and the gate of each item, is in the Service standard. If you are starting out, this page explains what is already on your disk. If you have an older service, jump to Migrating an existing service.

docs.title: How the gate enforces it
docs.text:
tempest lint-layers reads the source with ast and never imports the project. Each violation is one file:line: CODE message line, and the message says what to change. The rules on this page enter as warnings: they print with (warning) and do not fail tempest check until you turn on strict mode:

[tool.tempest]
layers_strict = true

To migrate one rule at a time, filter:

tempest lint-layers --rule IMP002

The full code table, with each one's real output, is in CLI › Layer rules.

docs.title: 1. One class per file, in a context package
docs.text:
Why: the file name becomes an index. services/billing/invoice.py holds InvoiceService and nothing else — whoever looks for the invoice service finds it without opening anything, and a diff touching the file touches only it. A models/route.py with five models forces you to open it to learn what is inside.

The four layers holding classes — controllers/, services/, db/repositories/ and db/models/ — keep each module in a context package (a plural noun of the domain: products, orders, billing), with one class per module.

❌ Before:

# src/db/models/route.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseModel


class RouteModel(BaseModel):
    """A delivery route."""

    __tablename__ = "routes"

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column()


class StopModel(BaseModel):
    """A stop on a route."""

    __tablename__ = "stops"

    address: Mapped[str] = mapped_column()

✅ After — one file per model, and the package re-exporting:

# src/db/models/routing/route.py
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseModel


class RouteModel(BaseModel):
    """A delivery route."""

    __tablename__ = "routes"

    name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column()

# src/db/models/routing/__init__.py
from .route import RouteModel as RouteModel
from .stop import StopModel as StopModel

__all__: list[str] = ["RouteModel", "StopModel"]
Code Reports LAY001 a second class or a module-level function in controllers/, repositories/ or models/ LAY002 a module directly at the root of one of the four layers SVC002 (error) the same in services/

The context name is free: the list the project's CLAUDE.md suggests is a guide, not a limit.

docs.title: 2. Import through the layer package; relative __init__
docs.text:
Why: a package's internal path is its own business. Code importing from src.services.billing.invoice import InvoiceService breaks the day the file moves; code importing from src.services import InvoiceService does not. And an __init__.py importing its neighbours by absolute path repeats the package's own name on every line.

✅ The package imports its neighbours relatively; the rest of the code imports through the package:

# src/services/__init__.py
from .billing import InvoiceService as InvoiceService
from .products import ProductService as ProductService

__all__: list[str] = ["InvoiceService", "ProductService"]

# src/controllers/billing/invoice.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseController

from src.schemas import InvoiceResponseSchema
from src.services import InvoiceService


class InvoiceController(BaseController[InvoiceService, InvoiceResponseSchema]):
    """Invoice coordination."""
Code Reports IMP001 an __init__.py importing a module of its own package by absolute path IMP002 importing a name from its submodule when a package above already re-exports it (followed transitively, through import * too)

When the package would close a cycle

IMP002 suggests the top-most package that re-exports the name without containing the importing module. Even so, importing through the package sometimes closes a cycle — in the transport service, tasks and scripts imported api.dependencies.resources directly, because importing the api.dependencies package would close a cycle with src.tasks. That case is a declared exception, not an import rewrite.

docs.title: 3. What services and controllers receive
docs.text:
Why: a service taking the AsyncSession builds its own repositories, so nobody outside can swap them in a test. A service taking another service hides an orchestration that is the controller's job. And a class with a from_session knows how to build its own graph: the knowledge of "what needs what" spreads over every class, and every call site repeats the assembly.

❌ Before:

# src/services/wallet/settlement.py
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from src.db.repositories import SettlementRepository


class SettlementService:
    """Settles the held balance."""

    def __init__(self, session: AsyncSession) -> None:
        """Keep the session."""
        self.repository = SettlementRepository(session)

    @classmethod
    def from_session(cls, session: AsyncSession) -> "SettlementService":
        """Build the service over a session."""
        return cls(session)

✅ After — the service receives the repository, and the graph is assembled in one place, the composition root:

# src/scripts/composition.py
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from src.controllers import SettlementController
from src.db.repositories import SettlementRepository
from src.services import SettlementService


def build_settlement_controller(session: AsyncSession) -> SettlementController:
    """Assemble the settlement controller over one session.

    Args:
        session (AsyncSession): The session the repository reads through.

    Returns:
        SettlementController: The controller, fully wired.
    """
    return SettlementController(SettlementService(SettlementRepository(session)))

The request provider in api/dependencies/controllers.py calls build_settlement_controller(session) with the session Depends resolved; a task, a queue consumer, a seed and the suite call the same function. The graph is written once.

Code Reports DI001 an AsyncSession parameter in a service or controller __init__ DI002 a service taking a *Service, a controller taking a *Controller DI003 a function or method named from_session, anywhere

The real case where two services must go together exists — in the transport service, the settlement and the wallet credit land in the same transaction. It becomes a declared exception, aimed at that one parameter. For the SDK's wallet, since v0.330.0 not even that: the balance write is the WalletLedger, a data layer the service receives the way it receives a repository.

docs.title: 4. A repository does not import a repository
docs.text:
Why: a query over two tables is a select() with a join, in the repository that owns the query. A repository importing another to "reuse" a query creates a dependency between data classes no service sees, and combining two repositories is exactly the service's job.

Code Reports REPO002 importing a *Repository inside repositories/ (a name used only as a class base — the project's base repository — passes)

docs.title: 5. One router per file; /api once
docs.text:
Why: with /api repeated in every include_router (22 times, in the transport service), changing the API prefix or mounting a domain outside it turns into a prefix hunt. And two routers in one file hide one of them from whoever looks by name.

✅ Each domain declares only its own prefix; /api appears in one place:

# src/api/routers/api.py
from fastapi import APIRouter

from .orders import router as orders_router
from .service_info import router as service_info_router

API_PREFIX: str = "/api"
"""Prefix every business route lives under."""


def build_api_router() -> APIRouter:
    """Assemble the router ``create_app`` includes.

    Returns:
        APIRouter: ``/api`` with every domain router included.
    """
    api: APIRouter = APIRouter(prefix=API_PREFIX)
    api.include_router(service_info_router)
    api.include_router(orders_router)
    return api
Code Reports RTR003 more than one APIRouter(...) in a routers/ module RTR004 a /api prefix (or below it) outside a build_api_router function

docs.title: 6. No nested function, no private module helper
docs.text:
Why: a function defined inside another has no importable name, no test of its own, and carries state through a closure, invisible in its signature. A module-level _x function is a helper with no home: nobody reuses it, and it drops out of the package's index.

❌ Before:

# src/utils/notify.py
from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable


def make_sender(channel: str) -> Callable[[str], Awaitable[None]]:
    """Build a sender for the channel."""

    async def send(message: str) -> None:
        """Send the message."""
        print(channel, message)

    return send

✅ After — state becomes a callable object; a fixed argument becomes functools.partial over a module-level function:

# src/utils/notify.py
from collections.abc import Coroutine
from functools import partial
from typing import Any


async def send(message: str, *, channel: str) -> None:
    """Send the message through the channel.

    Args:
        message (str): The text.
        channel (str): Where it goes.
    """
    print(channel, message)


class ChannelSender:
    """A sender bound to a channel, with visible state."""

    def __init__(self, channel: str) -> None:
        """Keep the channel.

        Args:
            channel (str): Where the messages go.
        """
        self.channel: str = channel

    async def __call__(self, message: str) -> None:
        """Send a message through the stored channel.

        Args:
            message (str): The text.
        """
        await send(message, channel=self.channel)


send_by_email: partial[Coroutine[Any, Any, None]] = partial(send, channel="email")
"""The same sender, with the channel already fixed."""
Code Reports STR001 a function defined inside another (in the source and the suite) STR002 a module-level function whose name starts with a single _ (in the source and the suite)

In the suite, the private helper becomes a fixture or a public helper module — in the transport service there were 174 nested functions and 76 _x helpers in the tests alone.

docs.title: 7. A task is registration only
docs.text:
Why: the API process should not import the tasks' code — and with it the whole graph they use. A 400-line tasks.py mixes registration, rules and scheduling.

The task layer tempest new --extras tasks writes splits it like this:

File Role tasks/names.py *_TASK_NAME and *_SCHEDULE (with every_n_minutes / daily); imports nothing from the project tasks/example.py registration only: @tq.cron(EXAMPLE_SCHEDULE, name=EXAMPLE_TASK_NAME), calling the script scripts/example.py the work, callable with or without a worker tasks/dispatch.py TaskDispatcher: the API enqueues by name, without importing the task tasks/worker.py imports the task modules and exposes broker / scheduler

Sending by name uses TaskQueue.enqueue_by_name, and the task's retry policy still applies — the worker restores the labels it was registered with.

A task name is for life

A queued message keeps the name. Renaming EXAMPLE_TASK_NAME strands the old messages: the worker logs task "<name>" is not found and drops them. When reorganizing tasks, move the code and keep the name.

docs.title: 8. Documented schema
docs.text:
Why: the client reads the openapi.json. A field without title, description and examples arrives there with a name and a type only — 370 fields, in the transport service.

A leaf field carries all three; a field holding another schema, only title and description. This is the only rule that has to import the project, so it runs in the suite (assert_schema_metadata) and in the tempest lint-schemas command — details in CLI › Schema metadata.

docs.title: 9. The suite explains what it proves
docs.text:
Why: a test is executable documentation. The docstring says the situation it builds and what it proves; a test that checks nothing always passes; pytest.raises(Exception) passes with any bug; and a drawn value in a parametrize id makes each pytest -n worker collect different tests — the transport suite did not run in parallel because of it (4 min serially, 47 s in parallel after the fix).

✅ The shape:

# tests/test_orders.py
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

from src.api.app import create_app


def test_a_duplicate_order_is_refused() -> None:
    """Cenário: the same order sent twice.

    Esperado: the second answers ``409`` with ``ORDER_DUPLICATED``.
    """
    with TestClient(create_app()) as client:
        payload = {"code": "A-1"}
        assert client.post("/api/orders", json=payload).status_code == 201
        duplicate = client.post("/api/orders", json=payload)
    assert duplicate.status_code == 409
    assert duplicate.json()["code"] == "ORDER_DUPLICATED"
Code Reports TST001 a test docstring without Cenário: and Esperado: TST002 a test with no assert, no pytest.raises/warns and no assert* call TST003 pytest.raises(Exception) or BaseException TST004 a parametrize id holding a value drawn at import

TST004 follows the measurement, not the assumption: a bare uuid4() or datetime.now() is ided by position and passes; it becomes a problem once it turns into text (str(uuid4()), uuid4().hex) or sits in ids=.

docs.title: Declared exception
docs.text:
Every rule admits the case you keep on purpose — with its reason written, in one place, reviewed in the diff like code:

# tests/architecture_exceptions.py
ARCHITECTURE_EXCEPTIONS: dict[str, str] = {
    "DI002 src/services/wallet/settlement.py::SettlementService.wallet_service": (
        "the settlement and the credit land in the same transaction"
    ),
}

The key is "<CODE> <path>" (every finding of that code in the file) or "<CODE> <path>::<subject>" (only the one about that name). An entry that no longer matches anything prints as EXC002: an exception does not outlive the code it excused.

docs.title: Migrating an existing service
docs.text:
Start by measuring. The count per code tells how much work there is and where to start:

tempest lint-layers | awk '{print $2}' | grep -E '^[A-Z]+[0-9]+$' | sort | uniq -c

The 0.328.0 scaffold itself, with no extras, gave this count (measured):

     11 IMP001
      8 IMP002
      1 LAY002
      1 RTR004
      3 TST001

Then take on one family per PR, each with --rule until it reaches zero:

  1. IMP001/IMP002 first: it is mechanical, changes no behaviour and makes the next changes cheaper — moving a file no longer breaks an import.
  2. LAY001/LAY002: move each class into its context package, re-exporting relatively. With step 1 done, the call sites do not change.
  3. DI001–DI003: create scripts/composition.py and make the providers call the build_* functions; delete the from_sessions.
  4. RTR003/RTR004: create routers/api.py and take /api out of the domains.
  5. STR001/STR002: stateful callbacks become classes; a fixed argument becomes partial.
  6. TST001–TST004: the suite — by far the biggest bill in the transport service (1380 of 1394 tests without the docstring shape).
  7. Tasks and schemas, when the service has them: split registration from work, and document the fields.

Three traps the transport service hit on the way:

Import cycle through the resources

Importing api.dependencies (the package) from the tasks and scripts would close a cycle with src.tasks. There, tasks and scripts kept importing api.dependencies.resources directly — with an IMP002 declared exception.

Task names preserved

When splitting the big tasks.py into domain modules, a task changes file but not name — or the messages already queued are stranded. Pin the old name in the *_TASK_NAME constant.

pytest-xdist ids

A parametrize with uuid4() turned into text in the id blocked pytest -n auto. Swap it for fixed literals before turning parallel on.

Once a family reaches zero, turn on layers_strict = true — from then on, a warning that comes back fails tempest check.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• One class per file, in <layer>/<context>/; the package re-exports relatively and the rest imports through the package.
  • A service receives repositories; a controller receives services. The graph is assembled in scripts/composition.py, and nobody has a from_session.
  • A repository does not import a repository.
  • One router per file, and /api only in build_api_router.
  • No nested function and no module _helper, in the source and the suite.
  • A task is registration only, with a fixed name; the API enqueues by name.
  • Documented schema, checked by assert_schema_metadata.
  • Tests with Cenário:/Esperado: that check something, with a specific exception and a deterministic parametrize.
  • All of it is a warning until you turn on layers_strict; what you keep on purpose goes in tests/architecture_exceptions.py, with its reason.

docs.title: API Reference
docs.text:
The full API reference is auto-generated from the SDK's English docstrings via mkdocstrings, so it reads the same in every UI language. To avoid duplicate symbol anchors, the rendered reference is published a single time on the default-language page:

Open the API Reference »

Searching

Every public symbol exported by tempest_fastapi_sdk is documented there with its full signature, parameters, return type, raised exceptions and source location. Use the search bar (or press /) to jump to a symbol by name — the full-text index includes the docstrings.

docs.title: Roadmap
docs.text:
The backlog that guided the SDK and what of it has landed — today every Tier S item below is marked ✅ with the version that shipped it. Sorted by impact, not implementation order — a release is pulled by business pressure, not list position.

What the SDK already covers

Full auth (JWT/bearer/role/permission/X-Token + bundled signup/activate/login/reset via UserAuthService + make_auth_router), OAuth2/OIDC (Google/GitHub + generic), Firebase ID token verification (FirebaseAuth + FirebaseIdentity + FirebaseUserResolver, [firebase] extra), CSRF middleware, DB (AsyncDatabaseManager + BaseRepository + bulk ops + AlembicHelper + BaseModel + BaseUserModel + BaseUserTokenModel + audit/soft-delete mixins + Alembic hook reordering base columns), standardized exceptions, structured logging + per-level files + /logs endpoint, metrics (CPU/RAM/GPU/Disk + Prometheus /metrics + PrometheusMiddleware), rate limiting, idempotency (IdempotencyMiddleware + memory/Redis stores), body-size limit, pagination (offset + cursor), settings mixins with title/description/examples, SSE, throttle, local upload/download + pluggable storage (LocalUploadStorage + MinIOUploadStorage), MinIO/S3 (AsyncMinIOClient), WebPush + unified web/mobile push (DeviceService + WebPushTransport + FCMTransport), webhook signature, bundled payment integrations (OpenPix generated from the spec + Stripe with form-encoded writes, idempotency and verified webhooks), BR validators (CPF/CNPJ/CEP/phone), admin panel (Jinja + HTMX, Django-admin parity — list view with search/filters/sortable columns, full CRUD, bulk actions, CSV/JSON export, FK-select widgets, dashboard with counts + metrics, TOTP MFA at login, created_by/updated_by audit trail), email (SMTP + Jinja2 templates), Redis cache, FastStream queue, TaskIQ tasks, hardened static files, server runner, health, tool-spec router, request-id middleware, CORS, typed HTTP client (HTTPClient httpx wrapper with retry/backoff/circuit-breaker), self-hosted generative AI (tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai — hardware check, local LLM TextGenerator + quantization, Embedder, web+PDF+vector-store RAG, STT/TTS audio in pt-BR/en-US), full CLI (tempest new, tempest generate --docker docs.title: Admin panel — evolution
docs.text:
The admin panel already exists (AdminSite / AdminModel / make_admin_router, Jinja + HTMX, CSRF token). The items below take it from "functional CRUD" to "production admin", reusing primitives the SDK already ships (AuditMixin, MetricsUtils, TOTPHelper, UploadUtils).

Feature Why it matters Reuses Per-column filter / search / sort on the list view ✅ v0.36.0 AdminModel(list_filter=…, search_fields=…, ordering=…) plus clickable sorting via ?sort=<column>&dir=asc|desc, validated against the displayed columns. BaseRepository + relationships CSV / JSON export ✅ v0.36.0 GET {prefix}/m/{slug}/export.csv / .json honours the active search, filters and sort; make_admin_router(export_max_rows=…) caps the size (default 5000). list view + filters Audit log visible in the admin ✅ v0.114.0 Who changed what and when, straight in the UI — a per-row timeline in the detail view. docs.title: Everything shipped so far
docs.text: The full release history — every version with its Added / Changed / Fixed entries — lives in the changelog, in Keep a Changelog format. It's the source of truth; this page only summarizes the backlog.

docs.title: What's next
docs.text:
The Tier S/A/B backlog and the admin-panel evolution (Tiers 1–3 + refinement) are done; so is the self-hosted genai roadmap (v0.139–0.154 — tool calling, structured output, VLM, reranker, hybrid search, ONNX embeddings, generation cache, token/context, vision router, metrics, moderation + pipeline integration). The candidates below came out of the 2026-07-24 overview analysis and are all shipped too — the last two, advanced rate limiting and WebAuthn, landed in v0.216.0 and v0.217.0.

The queue is empty. The next theme comes from business pressure, not from this page. Keeping an aspirational item here just because the section would look short is exactly what the footer note forbids.

docs.title: ✅ GenAI hardening — transformers 5.x debt (shipped v0.155.0)
docs.text: Constrained structured output now works on transformers 5.x (build_prefix_allowed_tokens_fn reimplemented from the lm-format-enforcer core, without the broken integrations.transformers module), and VisionTextGenerator loads on tf5 (AutoModelForImageTextToText + torchvision in the [genai-vlm] extra). Both validated on GPU (Qwen2.5-3B / Qwen2-VL-2B). Remaining caveat: multimodal accuracy depends on per-family processor wiring (non-blocker) — see planning/genai/manual-validation.md.

docs.title: Queue observability + genai tracing
docs.text:
Delivered in slices, one release per slice:

  • ✅ OTel spans on genai calls (generate/chat/embed/rag) — shipped in v0.156.0. The ambient genai_span reuses the TracerProvider from setup_tracing (GenAI semantic conventions); no-op without the [otel] extra. See the genai recipe (Distributed tracing).
  • ✅ TaskQueue: retry + dead-letter + per-task metrics — shipped in v0.157.0. RetryPolicy + enable_retries, DeadLetterSink + dead_letter (target is yours, no backend assumed), TaskMetrics into the shared /metrics. Opt-in middleware, imports without the [tasks] extra. See the queue recipe (Task reliability and observability).
  • ✅ Task panel in the admin — shipped in v0.158.0 as dead-letter + inventory (not a Flower clone). BaseDeadLetterModel + make_dead_letter_model, DbDeadLetterSink (persists terminal failures), make_dead_letter_admin_model (read-mostly AdminModel + requeue action), task_inventory (registered tasks). No live queue introspection — TaskIQ exposes none (Flower is Celery-specific); it shows what is real and persisted. See the queue recipe (Dead-letter panel in the admin).

docs.title: HTTP performance layer
docs.text:
• ✅ ResponseCacheMiddleware — shipped in v0.159.0. ETag / conditional GET (304) always on + opt-in server-side cache (ResponseCacheStore/Memory/Redis), respects no-store/private/ Set-Cookie, keyed by vary=. See the HTTP recipe (HTTP response cache).
  • ✅ Advanced rate limiting — shipped in v0.216.0. RateLimitRule (sliding window, or a token bucket when burst is set), StaticRateLimitPolicy / PlanRateLimitPolicy (+ plan_by_jwt_claim / plan_by_header / key_by_plan_principal) and MemoryQuotaStore / RedisQuotaStore, which decide the whole list before writing any rule — a rejected request never spends the others' budget. RateLimit-* response headers. See the HTTP recipe (Tolerating bursts: the token bucket).

docs.title: ✅ Modern auth — WebAuthn / passkeys (shipped v0.217.0)
docs.text:
WebAuthnService runs both ceremonies (registration and login) over fido2, BaseWebAuthnCredentialModel + make_web_authn_credential_model hold the public keys, and make_auth_router(webauthn=...) mounts the six routes when AUTH_WEBAUTHN_ENABLED is on. Beyond what the library verifies, the SDK refuses a signature counter that did not advance (the cloned-authenticator signal), spends the challenge on use, and never reveals whether an account exists in begin. Memory or Redis (GETDEL) challenge store. Extra [webauthn]. Recipe »

Out of scope by decision: OpenAI-compatible client (self-hosted focus), GraphQL/gRPC (REST by decision).

This roadmap is honest, not aspirational

Items past the next cuts only land on the changelog when business pressure pulls them. This page is refreshed on every release — if something belongs here and isn't, open an issue.

docs.title: Shipped in v0.173.0
docs.text:
Modelops — export, measure and quantize the models a service serves:

Feature Status Where CPU/RAM/GPU/energy benchmarking ✅ v0.173 benchmark times any callable; benchmark_onnx/benchmark_torch/benchmark_models build on it. Discarded warm-up plus N repetitions, median and IQR first (latency is heavy-tailed), p95/p99, throughput, RSS peak and delta, GPU memory. Modelops » Energy measurement with provenance ✅ v0.173 NvmlPowerSampler (prefers the driver's total-energy counter, falls back to integrating power), NvidiaSmiPowerSampler, RaplEnergySampler (CPU package energy via powercap, wraparound handled) and NullPowerSampler. Every number carries an EnergySourceEnum — none of them is wall-plug. A CPU run resolves no GPU sampler. Ranking: composite score + Pareto ✅ v0.173 composite_scores with weights renormalized over the dimensions actually measured, pareto_points skipping unmeasured axes instead of assuming the best, rank → BenchmarkReport with the effective weights and the host description. .onnx → .ort and graph optimization ✅ v0.173 export_onnx_to_ort (file or directory, FIXED/RUNTIME style, target_platform, type reduction, .required_operators.config for the minimal build), export_torch_to_onnx and optimize_onnx_graph. ONNX and HuggingFace quantization ✅ v0.173 quantize_onnx_dynamic, quantize_onnx_static (calibration reader from any iterable of feeds), and the transformers-export path on ONNX Runtime's own tooling: optimize_hf_onnx (O1–O4), quantize_hf_onnx (arm64/avx2/avx512/avx512_vnni) — plus quantize_hf_bnb (int4/int8 in PyTorch). No optimum dependency, so nothing here caps your transformers version. tempest model CLI ✅ v0.173 analyze / bench / optimize / quantize / export-ort / hardware, with --json on the reporting commands. A missing extra exits 2 with the install line. CLI »

docs.title: Shipped in v0.168.0
docs.text:
Permission guards with metadata:

Feature Status Where Second parameter meta: dict[str, Any] ✅ v0.168 A guard may declare a second parameter and receive metadata, which turns a generic guard into a route-specific check: write has_role once and let each call site declare meta={"role": "manager"}. One-parameter guards are untouched — the second argument only goes to guards that declare it. Reference » include_args=True ✅ v0.168 Merges the call's arguments (path params, body, other dependencies) into the same dict, so an ownership guard reads meta["order_id"] without the route handing anything over. User excluded, omitted parameters contribute their default, Depends(...) markers dropped, meta= literals winning over same-named arguments. Misuse still caught at import ✅ v0.168 TempestPermissionError when meta= is not a mapping, when meta=/include_args= have no guard to receive them, and when a guard asks for 3+ parameters. guard_metadata(fn) exposes the declared literals. New static checks ✅ v0.168 tempest permissions gained meta-unused (error), guard-meta-missing, guard-meta-annotation and meta-key-collision (warnings); guard-arity now accepts 1 or 2 parameters. The meta-unused verdict is held back when a guard in the decoration could not be resolved.

docs.title: Shipped in v0.167.0
docs.text:
Permission guards — decorator plus a two-layer linter:

Feature Status Where @requires(*guards, user_param=None) ✅ v0.167 Runs guards that take the user and return the user (or None) before the body, on a route, a controller or a service, sync or async. A guard denies by raising an AppException; a non-None return replaces the user the next guard and the body see — that is how require_active narrows Optional[UserT] to UserT. The user parameter resolves from the annotation (BaseModel/BaseUserModel), user_param= breaks a tie. The signature is preserved, so dependency injection and the OpenAPI schema stay untouched. Reference » Misuse caught at import time ✅ v0.167 TempestPermissionError for @requires() with no guard, a non-callable guard, wrong arity, an async guard on a sync function, and a missing or ambiguous user parameter. The application refuses to start with a check that never fires. Contract warning at call time ✅ v0.167 GuardContractWarning when a guard raises outside the AppException hierarchy (the API would answer 500 with no code) or returns a non-user value such as False (a denial that would be ignored). The original exception still propagates. tempest permissions --check / --strict / --path ✅ v0.167 Static check (ast, without importing the app) for what runtime cannot see: a guard whose raise no test exercises, a guard never wired. Errors no-guards/user-param-missing/user-param-ambiguous/guard-arity/guard-async-in-sync/guard-returns-bool/guard-foreign-exception; warnings guard-never-denies/guard-missing-annotation/guard-return-type/guard-unresolved. An ambiguous or out-of-scope guard is reported, never guessed. OpenAPI error-docs integration ✅ v0.167 tempest openapi-errors follows the @requires guards, so a guard's exception shows up as undocumented until the route declares it — and --fix writes it. declared_guards / guarded_user_param expose a route's guards for auditing.

docs.title: Shipped in v0.166.0
docs.text:
Errors in OpenAPI — automatic fix:

Feature Status Where tempest openapi-errors --fix ✅ v0.166 Writes the declarations --check was pointing at: injects responses=error_responses(...) into the route, extends an existing declaration (error_responses or @raises) preserving its order, and adds the missing imports. Edits anchored on AST positions, output passed through ruff check --select I --fix + ruff format. Reference » Only ever adds, on a clean tree ✅ v0.166 unreachable findings are never removed — reachability cannot see a dynamic raise, so deleting on its word would remove a correct declaration. Requires a clean git tree, so git diff is the review and git checkout the undo; --dry-run prints the formatted diff and runs on a dirty tree. Formatting with the project's config ✅ v0.166.1 The scratch file handed to ruff is created next to the file being rewritten, so the project's line-length and isort sections apply — and what gets written passes its own CI's ruff format --check. When no working ruff is found (PATH, python -m ruff, uv run ruff, each probed with --version), the command writes anyway and says so.

docs.title: Shipped in v0.161.0
docs.text:
Code generation from an OpenAPI specification:

Feature Status Where tempest openapi-client <spec> ✅ v0.161 Point it at the spec (URL or file, JSON or YAML) and get <src|app>/integrations/<name>/ with schemas.py + client.py. The end of transcribing a third party's documentation by hand. --name/--out/--header/--schemas-only/--force/--no-format. Reference » Schemas with metadata ✅ v0.161 One BaseSchema class per component, with the spec's title/description/examples on every Field — the generated module is the integration's documentation. Python names + the wire name as alias + populate_by_name; reserved words resolved (class → class_); optional collections as empty lists; enums as BaseStrEnum/BaseIntEnum; allOf flattened; recursion via model_rebuild(). Nothing is invented where the spec documents nothing. Reference » Typed HTTP client ✅ v0.161 One async method per operation, over an injected HTTPClient — retry/backoff/circuit-breaker/credentials stay with the caller, and httpx.MockTransport tests the whole integration offline. Typed path/query params, validated body and response, full Google docstrings. Reference » Output that passes your gates ✅ v0.161 The emitted code passes ruff check + ruff format --check before the formatting pass (tested against the raw output), so --no-format or a machine without ruff still yields a usable package. Regenerating an unchanged spec produces a byte-for-byte identical file, so the git diff of a --force is the integration's changelog. It never guesses ✅ v0.161 An unrepresentable construct (not, external $ref, Swagger 2.0, non-JSON body, header param) becomes Any + a # openapi: unsupported comment + a line in the command's summary. A wrong schema that looks right is worse than a documented gap.

docs.title: Shipped in v0.160.0
docs.text:
Errors documented in OpenAPI:

Feature Status Where ErrorResponseSchema ✅ v0.160 The {detail, code, details} envelope the handlers already emitted now exists as an exported schema — before there was nothing to point a hand-written responses={409: ...} at. Reference » error_responses(*exceptions) ✅ v0.160 Builds FastAPI's responses= from the exception classes. Groups by status (OpenAPI allows one response object per status) and distinguishes the codes through an examples map — Swagger/ReDoc render it as a selector, so two 404s with different codes stay visible. summary from __doc__, detail from message or a MessageCatalog. Reference » @raises(...) + TempestAPIRouter ✅ v0.160 The same declaration next to the handler; the router expands the tag into responses= before the route is constructed (so the model reaches components.schemas as a $ref). An explicit responses= wins per status. Reference » InheritedErrorCodeWarning ✅ v0.160 A subclass that declares no code of its own and inherits a generic SDK one warns at class creation — the silent defect that had a subclass emitting code: "CONFLICT" for months in production. Does not fire for a domain code, nor when message_key is declared. Reference » tempest openapi-errors --check ✅ v0.160 Compares, per route, the declaration against what is reachable through router -> controller -> service -> repository. Static (ast, no application import), reads raise statements and Raises: sections. Reports undocumented + unreachable, exits non-zero as a CI gate. Reference »

docs.title: How to request a feature
docs.text:
Open an issue at https://github.com/mauriciobenjamin700/tempest-fastapi-sdk/issues describing:

  1. The real use case (not the solution).
  2. The workaround you use today.
  3. Why the workaround hurts (perf, security, ergonomics, maintenance).

Issues with concrete use cases move up the queue — abstractions without demand don't land, even when they "would make sense".

docs.title: Service standard
docs.text:
This page is the citable reference for how a Tempest service is laid out: each item of the standard, why it exists, and what enforces it today — a tempest lint-layers code, a tempest check step, or a test tempest new already writes into your project. When an item has no gate, the page says so too.

The standard is the transport-backend's, the service these rules were measured on. #718 records why it became the reference: a new service was written by an AI without starting from tempest new, and only a review against the transport brought it back to a clean lint-layers --strict, lint-schemas and openapi-errors.

Start from tempest new

Everything this page describes already comes out of tempest new. Writing the service by hand, or copying another one, is exactly the mistake of #718. For a new domain inside an existing project, follow the recipe in the CLAUDE.md the scaffold writes; for the file-shape rules, see the Recommended architecture.

docs.title: What tempest new generates
docs.text:
tempest new demo --extras sqlite

The project's directory tree (tree -d, measured on this page's branch):

.
├── alembic
│   └── versions
├── src
│   ├── api
│   │   ├── dependencies
│   │   ├── docs
│   │   └── routers
│   ├── controllers
│   │   └── system
│   ├── core
│   │   ├── constants
│   │   │   └── messages
│   │   ├── enums
│   │   ├── exceptions
│   │   └── types
│   ├── db
│   │   ├── configs
│   │   ├── models
│   │   └── repositories
│   ├── schemas
│   ├── scripts
│   ├── services
│   └── utils
└── tests
    ├── integration
    │   └── system
    └── unit
        ├── architecture
        └── core

And tempest check on it, untouched (ENV=test, which the generated conftest.py pins as well):

$ ruff check --extend-select ANN001,ANN201,ANN202,ANN205,ANN206 .
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check .
61 files already formatted
$ mypy --disallow-untyped-defs --disallow-incomplete-defs .
Success: no issues found in 59 source files
$ lint-layers
Layer rules: no findings.
$ openapi-errors
Every route's declared errors match its flow (src).
$ lint-schemas
Schema metadata: src.schemas is fully documented.
$ pytest -n auto -p no:cacheprovider
...
9 passed

The nine tests are the ones the scaffold writes: three integration tests of the root route and health, three architecture guards and three for the exception contract.

docs.title: The standard, item by item
docs.text:
Rule What it looks like What enforces it today One layer class per file, per context src/<layer>/<context>/<file>.py, only the class + logger + __all__ LAY001, LAY002 No nested def and no module-level _x, in src and tests a stateful callback becomes a callable object STR001, STR002 __init__ imports relatively; elsewhere, import the package from .x import Y / from src.services import X IMP001, IMP002 A resource is a process singleton in one place api/dependencies/resources.py (db, get_session, get_*) — (scaffold convention) Providers per layer; a router never sees AsyncSession api/dependencies/controllers.py calls the build_* RTR001, DI001–DI003 /api set in one place routers/api.py → build_api_router() RTR003, RTR004 OpenAPI text out of the router api/docs/<router>.py, one EndpointDoc per handler — (scaffold convention) Exceptions: one module per status, contract in the class body core/exceptions/{bad_request,unauthorized,forbidden,not_found,conflict}.py tests/unit/core/test_exceptions_contract.py Frozen exception contract status, code, message and field of each class tests/unit/core/test_exceptions_contract.py Prose and constants out of the module that uses them core/constants/ + core/constants/messages/{errors,successes}.py — (scaffold convention) Protocol, alias, NamedTuple, enum core/types/<domain>.py, core/enums/<domain>.py LAY001 (outside the layer); ENUM001 (suffix) Database db/configs/{connection,migrations,names}.py — (scaffold convention) Mapping in the repository map_to_response REPO001 (partial) Graph assembled outside the request scripts/composition.py (build_*) DI003 (from_session) Every schema field documented Field(title=..., description=..., examples=...) lint-schemas + tests/unit/architecture/test_schemas.py Every route declares what it raises responses=error_responses(...) openapi-errors + tests/unit/architecture/test_openapi_errors.py Tests Cenário:/Esperado:, checking something; tests/{unit,integration}/<area>/ TST001–TST004 Guards in the suite itself tests/unit/architecture/ test_layers.py, test_openapi_errors.py, test_schemas.py Warnings fail from the first commit layers_strict = true under [tool.tempest] tempest check

The LAY, STR, IMP, DI, RTR003/RTR004 and TST codes are warnings: they only fail tempest check with layers_strict = true, which the generated pyproject.toml already turns on. The table of every code, with each one's real output, is in CLI › Layer rules.

What has no gate

The resource singleton, api/docs, core/constants and db/configs are convention: the scaffold starts that way and the CLAUDE.md recipe teaches it, but no rule fails when you deviate. They were left out because the check would have to judge intent (what is "prose", what is a "process resource"), and a rule that broad flags correct code.

docs.title: Exceptions: one module per status, contract in the body
docs.text:
Why: the status + code pair is what the client reads to decide what to show, and the message is what the user sees. When the class declares all three in its body, whoever reads the class without instantiating it — error_responses documenting OpenAPI, the BaseRepository raising the 404, tempest openapi-errors — sees the same contract the client receives. An __init__ that builds the message hides it, and makes every raise remember the arguments.

The module says the status, so whoever looks for "what returns 409" opens conflict.py:

# src/core/exceptions/not_found.py
from typing import Any, ClassVar

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import NotFoundException

from src.core.constants.messages import errors


class ItemNotFoundException(NotFoundException):
    """Raised when an item id matches no stored record."""

    code = "ITEM_NOT_FOUND"
    message = errors.ITEM_NOT_FOUND
    field = "item_id"
    details_example: ClassVar[dict[str, Any]] = {"item_id": "3f2b8c1e"}
  • code is the stable identifier. Without it the class inherits the SDK's generic one ("NOT_FOUND"), and the SDK warns with InheritedErrorCodeWarning.
  • message comes from a constant, never from an f-string.
  • field names the culprit input. Leave it unset on invalid credentials: saying which half of the pair was wrong helps whoever is guessing.
  • Data that changes per raise goes in details=:
from src.core.exceptions import ItemNotFoundException


def require_item(item_id: str, found: bool) -> None:
    """Refuse a lookup that missed.

    Args:
        item_id (str): The id that was looked up.
        found (bool): Whether the lookup matched a row.

    Raises:
        ItemNotFoundException: When ``found`` is false.
    """
    if not found:
        raise ItemNotFoundException(details={"item_id": item_id})

docs.title: The frozen contract
docs.text:
The generated tests/unit/core/test_exceptions_contract.py keeps, as literals, the status, code, message and field of every class src.core.exceptions re-exports — and fails when a new class lands without an entry. Measured: with an OrderAlreadyPaidException re-exported and no line in the contract, the test fails like this:

E       AssertionError: assert {'ItemNotFoun...aidException'} == {'ItemNotFoundException'}
E         Extra items in the left set:
E         'OrderAlreadyPaidException'
1 failed, 2 passed

Renaming, moving or rewording an exception becomes a visible change in that file's diff — which is an API change.

docs.title: Messages and constants out of the module that uses them
docs.text:
