  • Logging — structured logging, per-level files, and the /logs endpoint.

docs.title: MFA / 2FA with TOTP (Authenticator)
docs.text: Since v0.35.0 the bundled auth flow supports two-factor authentication with Authenticator apps (Google Authenticator, 1Password, Authy, etc.) following the TOTP (RFC 6238) standard. You get four ready-to-mount endpoints, single-use recovery codes, and a two-step login — all behind a global kill-switch.

docs.title: What's in this recipe
docs.text:
1. How it works in 30 seconds — the mental model of the two-step flow.
  2. Setup — the [mfa] extra, new UserModel columns, recovery-code table.
  3. Wiring — passing recovery_code_model to make_auth_router.
  4. The four endpoints — enroll / confirm / verify / disable.
  5. Two-step login — how POST /auth/login changes when MFA is active.
  6. Routes that require MFA — the amr claim and make_mfa_required_dependency.
  7. Settings (AuthSettings) — flag by flag.
  8. Attempt limit — 429 after five failures, and single-use TOTP codes.
  9. Using just UserAuthService (no router) — for hand-rolled endpoints.
  10. Accounts that do not use emailed links — refuses_email_link for operators and staff.
  11. Security.
  12. Next steps.

docs.title: How it works
docs.text:
TOTP is the 6-digit code that rolls over every 30 seconds in your Authenticator app. The server and the app share a secret (generated at enrollment); both derive the same code from the current clock. No SMS, no network — pure local math.

The flow has two moments:

  • Enrollment (once) — the logged-in user requests a secret, scans the QR code, and confirms by typing the first code. From there MFA is active.
  • Login (every time) — the password validates step 1, but instead of the JWT pair the backend returns a short-lived mfa_token. The user types the Authenticator code; step 2 swaps mfa_token + code for the real JWT pair.

Why two steps and not all at once?

Splitting keeps the password and the second factor decoupled. The mfa_token (5-min TTL by default) carries only the user's sub — intercepting it alone is not enough to log in, because the Authenticator code is still missing.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Requires the [mfa] extra (installs pyotp and segno, which draws the QR code), on top of [auth]:

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[auth,mfa]>=0.151.1"

docs.title: Columns via MFAMixin
docs.text:
The MFA columns (totp_secret, totp_enabled_at, totp_last_step) do not live on BaseUserModel — they come from an opt-in mixin, MFAMixin. Mix it into your UserModel only when you adopt MFA, so projects that never enable the feature carry no dead columns:

# src/db/models/user.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseUserModel, MFAMixin


class UserModel(MFAMixin, BaseUserModel):
    """Concrete user table — MFAMixin adds the totp_* columns."""

    __tablename__ = "users"

MRO order

The mixin comes before BaseUserModel in the base list — same pattern as AuditMixin / SoftDeleteMixin. The mixin also exposes an is_mfa_active property (totp_enabled_at is not None).

Migration required

totp_secret, totp_enabled_at and totp_last_step are new columns. Run uv run tempest db revision -m "mfa columns" + uv run tempest db upgrade before flipping the flag.

docs.title: Recovery-code table
docs.text:
Recovery codes save the user who lost their phone. They are single-use, shown once at enrollment, and the database stores only the SHA-256 hash of each. BaseUserRecoveryCodeModel is abstract — use the make_user_recovery_code_model helper to build the concrete table bound to your users table:

# src/db/models/__init__.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import make_user_recovery_code_model

from src.db.models.user import UserModel
from src.db.models.user_token import UserTokenModel

UserRecoveryCodeModel = make_user_recovery_code_model(
    user_table="users",
    tablename="user_recovery_codes",
    class_name="UserRecoveryCodeModel",
)

__all__: list[str] = [
    "UserModel",
    "UserTokenModel",
    "UserRecoveryCodeModel",
]
Prefer subclassing by hand?

The helper is just sugar. The explicit equivalent:

from uuid import UUID

from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseUserRecoveryCodeModel


class UserRecoveryCodeModel(BaseUserRecoveryCodeModel):
    __tablename__ = "user_recovery_codes"

    user_id: Mapped[UUID] = mapped_column(
        ForeignKey("users.id", ondelete="CASCADE"),
        nullable=False,
        index=True,
    )

docs.title: Wiring
docs.text:
Turn on the AUTH_MFA_ENABLED flag and pass the recovery_code_model to the router. Without the model, the router raises RuntimeError at build time — a deliberate guard:

# src/api/app.py

from fastapi import FastAPI

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AsyncDatabaseManager, UserAuthService, make_auth_router

from src.core.settings import settings
from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel, UserTokenModel

app = FastAPI()


db = AsyncDatabaseManager(settings.DATABASE_URL)

auth_service = UserAuthService(
    user_model=UserModel,
    token_model=UserTokenModel,
    auth_settings=settings,   # mixes in AuthSettings (AUTH_MFA_* below)
    jwt_settings=settings,
    email=None,
)

app.include_router(
    make_auth_router(
        auth_service,
        session_factory=db.session_dependency,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,   # required when MFA is on
    ),
)

Global kill-switch

With AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=False (default), the /auth/mfa/* endpoints respond 404 and login ignores any persisted totp_secret — handy to disable MFA during an Authenticator outage without touching the database.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text:
The four are only mounted when AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=True:

Method Path Auth Body / Output Behavior POST /auth/mfa/enroll Bearer JWT — → MFAEnrollResponseSchema Generates secret + QR URI + the drawn QR (provisioning_qr) + N recovery codes. Shown only once. Does NOT activate MFA yet. With MFA already active, answers 409 (MFA_ALREADY_ENROLLED) and changes nothing. POST /auth/mfa/confirm Bearer JWT MFAConfirmSchema → LoginResponseSchema Confirms enrollment with the first code. From here MFA is active. Revokes the user's refresh tokens and returns a new pair carrying the MFA amr (details). POST /auth/mfa/verify — MFAVerifySchema → LoginResponseSchema Login step 2: swaps mfa_token + code for the JWT pair. Five wrong codes per account in 15 min give 429 (attempt limit). POST /auth/mfa/disable Bearer JWT MFADisableSchema Disables MFA. Requires password and an active code (TOTP or recovery).

docs.title: Enrollment flow
docs.text:
import httpx

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"
access = "<logged-in user's JWT>"
headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {access}"}

# 1. Enroll — returns secret, QR URI and the recovery codes (once!)
r = httpx.post(f"{BASE}/auth/mfa/enroll", headers=headers)
data = r.json()
print(data["provisioning_qr"])    # SVG data URI: use it in <img src="...">
print(data["recovery_codes"])     # show the user — save OFFLINE

# 2. User scans the QR in the Authenticator and types the generated code:
code = input("Authenticator code: ")
httpx.post(f"{BASE}/auth/mfa/confirm", headers=headers, json={"code": code})
# 200 → MFA active; the body carries a new pair, and the old refresh token is dead

Recovery codes appear ONCE

The enroll response is the only time secret and recovery_codes leave in plaintext. Show them prominently and tell the user to store them offline.

docs.title: QR code: in the terminal and in the response
docs.text:
Every authenticator app reads QR codes, and it is the path people know. Typing 32 base32 characters by hand is slow and error-prone. That is why the enroll response already carries the provisioning_uri drawn, and the SDK has two functions to draw it wherever you need:

Function Returns For provisioning_qr_data_uri(uri, *, kind="svg") data:image/svg+xml;base64,... (or data:image/png;base64,... with kind="png") an <img> in a page or in the app provisioning_qr_terminal(uri, *, background="dark") text made of half blocks (▀, ▄, █ and space) print / typer.echo in a CLI

Both run on segno, which ships with the [mfa] extra and is imported at the first call only.

docs.title: In the API response
docs.text:
POST /auth/mfa/enroll returns the provisioning_qr field, an SVG data URI. The frontend drops it straight into an <img src="...">, with no QR library on its side:

{
  "secret": "GGZPWWOVQ6QIXMCMDOARELP3SR7JF424",
  "provisioning_uri": "otpauth://totp/Tempest:ana%40example.com?secret=GGZPWWOVQ6QIXMCMDOARELP3SR7JF424&issuer=Tempest",
  "provisioning_qr": "data:image/svg+xml;base64,PHN2ZyB4bWxucz0iaHR0cDovL3d3dy53My5vcmcvMjAwMC9zdmciIH...",
  "recovery_codes": ["..."]
}

The field is on by default, with no setting: it is optional and purely additive, so whoever already consumes the response keeps reading the same fields. If the server does not have segno installed (say, it installed pyotp without the [mfa] extra), provisioning_qr comes back null and the rest of the response is unchanged — the route does not break for lack of a drawing.

Mounting your own endpoint, call the function directly. This endpoint returns a page with the QR:

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService, provisioning_qr_data_uri

from src.api.dependencies import get_auth_service, get_current_user, get_session
from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel

router = APIRouter()


@router.post("/mfa/enroll-page", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def enroll_page(
    service: UserAuthService = Depends(get_auth_service),
    session: AsyncSession = Depends(get_session),
    user: UserModel = Depends(get_current_user),
) -> HTMLResponse:
    """Enroll TOTP and show the QR code once."""
    secret, uri, codes = await service.mfa_enroll(
        session,
        user=user,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
    )
    await session.commit()
    qr = provisioning_qr_data_uri(uri)
    items = "".join(f"<li><code>{code}</code></li>" for code in codes)
    return HTMLResponse(
        f'<img src="{qr}" alt="Authenticator app QR code">'
        f"<p>Or type the secret: <code>{secret}</code></p>"
        f"<ul>{items}</ul>",
        headers={"Cache-Control": "no-store"},
    )

Cache-Control: no-store asks the browser and any proxy not to keep the page: it carries the secret.

docs.title: In the terminal
docs.text:
provisioning_qr_terminal draws each character one module wide and two modules tall, so the QR stays square in a terminal, whose cells are taller than they are wide. A 95-character URI (issuer Tempest, ana@example.com, 32-character secret) prints 49 columns by 25 lines, and a 159-character one (22-character issuer, 41-character e-mail) 61 columns — both fit in 80 (measured with segno 1.6.6). This function enrolls and shows the QR:

import typer
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService, provisioning_qr_terminal

from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel


async def enroll_in_terminal(
    service: UserAuthService,
    session: AsyncSession,
    user: UserModel,
) -> list[str]:
    """Enroll TOTP and draw the QR in the terminal.

    Returns:
        The recovery codes, to show once.
    """
    secret, uri, codes = await service.mfa_enroll(
        session,
        user=user,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
    )
    typer.echo(provisioning_qr_terminal(uri))
    typer.echo(f"or type the secret: {secret}")
    return codes

Light terminal

The characters paint in the text colour. On a dark terminal (the default) the function draws the light modules and the border, so the camera reads dark on light, as on paper. On a light-background terminal pass background="light": then it draws the dark modules.

tempest user create --require-mfa already does this: it prints the QR before the URI (Bootstrapping the first privileged account).

The QR code IS the secret

The QR carries the provisioning_uri, and the URI carries the TOTP secret. Whoever photographs the screen generates every future code of the account. So:

  • show it once, in the enroll response, and offer no "see it again" — rotating the secret is disable + enroll;
  • never log the QR, the URI or the secret, not even at DEBUG;
  • do not store the image — not on disk, not in a cache, not in upload storage.

docs.title: Rotating the secret: disable, then enroll
docs.text:
Calling enroll again before confirm replaces the pending secret and codes: the enrollment is not active yet, so there is no factor to protect. After confirm, enroll refuses with 409 and touches nothing:

{"detail":"MFA is already active — disable it before enrolling again","code":"MFA_ALREADY_ENROLLED","details":{}}

That is the body with register_exception_handlers mounted. The refusal exists because enroll only asks for the bearer token and wipes the recovery codes: accepting a second enroll over active MFA let whoever held just the access token switch the second factor off, without the password and the code disable demands. To rotate the secret (new phone, leaked secret), the user goes through POST /auth/mfa/disable with password + code and then redoes enroll + confirm. In the service, the same refusal is the MFAAlreadyEnrolledException exception (a ConflictException subclass), raised by mfa_enroll even with the AUTH_MFA_ENABLED kill-switch off.

docs.title: Two-step login
docs.text:
When the user has MFA active, POST /auth/login no longer returns the JWT pair directly — it returns mfa_required=True + a short-lived mfa_token:

import httpx

BASE = "http://localhost:8000"

# Step 1 — password
r1 = httpx.post(
    f"{BASE}/auth/login",
    json={"email": "ana@example.com", "password": "strong-pass-12-chars"},
)
body = r1.json()
# {
#   "user_id": "...",
#   "access_token": null,
#   "refresh_token": null,
#   "mfa_required": true,
#   "mfa_token": "eyJhbGciOi..."
# }

# Step 2 — Authenticator code (or a recovery code)
code = input("Authenticator code: ")
r2 = httpx.post(
    f"{BASE}/auth/mfa/verify",
    json={"mfa_token": body["mfa_token"], "code": code},
)
tokens = r2.json()
# { "access_token": "...", "refresh_token": "...", "mfa_required": false }

For users without MFA (or with the kill-switch off), POST /auth/login keeps returning the JWT pair directly, with mfa_required=False — the frontend just checks that field and branches.

sequenceDiagram
    participant F as Frontend
    participant API as Backend (SDK)
    participant DB as Database

    F->>API: POST /auth/login (email + password)
    API->>DB: validate credentials
    alt user has MFA active
        API->>F: 200 {mfa_required: true, mfa_token: "..."}
        F->>API: POST /auth/mfa/verify (mfa_token + code)
        API->>DB: validate TOTP or recovery code
        API->>F: 200 {access_token, refresh_token}
    else MFA off / not enrolled
        API->>F: 200 {access_token, refresh_token, mfa_required: false}
    end

docs.title: Routes that require MFA
docs.text:
Turning MFA on protects the login. A sensitive route (creating another staff member, changing bank details) wants to know something else: did this session pass the second factor? For that, every access token the SDK issues carries the amr claim (RFC 8176):

How the session started amr POST /auth/login with the password alone (and signup with auto-activation) ["pwd"] POST /auth/activate/{token} and POST /auth/password-reset/confirm of an account without MFA (v0.314.0+) ["email"] (AMR_EMAIL_LINK) POST /auth/mfa/verify (TOTP code or recovery code) the first step + "otp": ["pwd", "otp"] after /auth/login, ["ext", "otp"] after a social login, ["email", "otp"] after an activation or a reset POST /auth/mfa/confirm (the new pair it returns) ["pwd", "otp"] POST /auth/webauthn/authenticate/complete ["hwk"] social login (/auth/oauth/...) of an account without MFA ["ext"]

On an account with MFA enrolled, /auth/password-reset/confirm and /auth/activate/{token} (for a reactivated account) do not issue a pair: they answer the mfa_required=true + mfa_token challenge, and the pair only comes out of /auth/mfa/verify, with amr == ["email", "otp"]. It is the same treatment as /auth/login — a compromised mailbox must not be a shortcut past the second factor. Since v0.314.0 social login follows the same rule: the callback and /auth/oauth/{provider}/token of an account with TOTP answer the challenge, and /auth/mfa/verify issues ["ext", "otp"] (see the social login recipe).

Why email, and neither pwd nor otp

Activation takes no password at all, and the reset proves the mailbox before it stores the new password — pwd would claim a check that never ran. email sits outside the RFC 8176 registry, like ext, because the RFC has no value for "single-use link sent by email". And it is not otp on purpose: the link is one factor, and calling it a one-time password would let it pass make_mfa_required_dependency. It stays out of MFA_AMR_METHODS, so the gate keeps refusing it.

refresh repeats the family's amr — it is stored on the refresh-token row (or inside the refresh JWT itself, in stateless mode) —, so a rotation never promotes a password session to MFA. make_mfa_required_dependency reads that claim:

# src/api/routers/staff.py
from typing import Any

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import JWTUtils, make_mfa_required_dependency

jwt = JWTUtils("replace-with-a-secret-of-32-bytes-or-more")
require_mfa = make_mfa_required_dependency(jwt)

router = APIRouter(prefix="/staff", tags=["staff"])


@router.post("/invite")
async def invite_staff(claims: dict[str, Any] = Depends(require_mfa)) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Only a session that passed the second factor invites another staff member."""
    return {"invited_by": str(claims["sub"])}

A password-only token gets 403 with code MFA_REQUIRED (MFARequiredException); no token at all, 401. A token without amr — issued before this version — also gets 403: the rollout window never counts an unknown session as MFA, and the user leaves it by redoing the two-step login.

Does a passkey count as MFA?

Not by default: methods= defaults to {"otp"}. If your AUTH_WEBAUTHN_USER_VERIFICATION is "required", the passkey already proves possession and a local factor, and you can accept it with make_mfa_required_dependency(jwt, methods={"otp", "hwk"}).

docs.title: Reading amr outside the gate: token_amr
docs.text:
make_mfa_required_dependency blocks. Sometimes you only want to know: show an "enable MFA" banner in the dashboard, record in the audit log whether the action came from a strong session, ask for extra confirmation instead of refusing. token_amr reads the claim from an already decoded payload and returns the tuple of methods, or None when the claim is missing or is not a list of strings.

The values have names, so you do not scatter "otp" across your code:

Constant Value AMR_CLAIM "amr" AMR_PASSWORD "pwd" AMR_OTP "otp" AMR_HARDWARE_KEY "hwk" AMR_EXTERNAL "ext" AMR_EMAIL_LINK "email" PASSWORD_AMR ("pwd",) MFA_AMR ("pwd", "otp") MFA_AMR_METHODS frozenset({"otp"}), the default for methods= 
from typing import Any

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    AMR_CLAIM,
    MFA_AMR,
    MFA_AMR_METHODS,
    PASSWORD_AMR,
    JWTUtils,
    token_amr,
)

jwt: JWTUtils = JWTUtils("replace-with-a-secret-of-32-bytes-or-more")


def second_factor_proven(claims: dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
    methods: tuple[str, ...] | None = token_amr(claims)
    return methods is not None and bool(MFA_AMR_METHODS.intersection(methods))


for label, extra in [
    ("password", {AMR_CLAIM: list(PASSWORD_AMR)}),
    ("password + otp", {AMR_CLAIM: list(MFA_AMR)}),
    ("no amr", {}),
    ("malformed amr", {AMR_CLAIM: "pwd"}),
]:
    claims: dict[str, Any] = jwt.decode(jwt.encode({"sub": "42", **extra}))
    print(f"{label:15} {token_amr(claims)!r:20} {second_factor_proven(claims)}")

password        ('pwd',)             False
password + otp  ('pwd', 'otp')       True
no amr          None                 False
malformed amr   None                 False

None counts as "second factor not proven", the same rule as the gate: a token minted before the claim existed, or by another issuer, never passes as an MFA session. The passkey case above becomes methods={AMR_OTP, AMR_HARDWARE_KEY}.

docs.title: Confirming MFA ends the other sessions
docs.text:
Whoever turns MFA on usually does it because they suspect someone has the password. So mfa_confirm revokes every refresh token of the user in the same transaction: a session opened with the password alone, before the factor existed, gets 401 at its next /auth/refresh. The device that confirmed loses nothing — the /auth/mfa/confirm route answers 200 with a new pair, already carrying the MFA amr (in the body for a bearer caller, as cookies for a caller authenticated by the access cookie).

Calling the service directly, the opt-out is explicit: mfa_confirm(session, user=user, code=code, revoke_sessions=False). The session it keeps stays ["pwd"], never "otp". An access token already issued lives until its short TTL ends, but it is ["pwd"] too, so the dependency above refuses it.

docs.title: Settings
docs.text:
Mix AuthSettings into your Settings class (as in the auth flow recipe) and configure via env:

# .env — MFA
AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=true                   # global kill-switch (default false)
AUTH_MFA_ISSUER=Acme Inc.               # name shown in the Authenticator
AUTH_MFA_RECOVERY_CODES_COUNT=10        # codes generated at enroll (2..50)
AUTH_MFA_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS=300          # mfa_token TTL between step 1 and 2 (30..900)
AUTH_MFA_VERIFY_WINDOW=1                # drift tolerance, in 30s steps (0..4)
Setting Default What it does AUTH_MFA_ENABLED False Mounts the /auth/mfa/* endpoints and the two-step login. AUTH_MFA_ISSUER "Tempest" Label next to the email in the Authenticator app. Use your product name. AUTH_MFA_RECOVERY_CODES_COUNT 10 Number of recovery codes generated at enrollment. AUTH_MFA_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS 300 Lifetime of the intermediate mfa_token (5 min). AUTH_MFA_VERIFY_WINDOW 1 Tolerance for the user's clock. 1 accepts previous + current + next step (90s). 0 is strict; above 2 weakens it.

docs.title: Attempt limit
docs.text: Since 0.306.0 step 2 of the login has two brakes you do not have to write.

docs.title: Five wrong codes, and the account waits
docs.text:
POST /auth/mfa/verify counts wrong codes per account, not per mfa_token. After five failures within fifteen minutes, the sixth attempt answers 429 without looking at the code, even when it is right:

{"detail":"too many invalid MFA codes, try again later","code":"MFA_THROTTLED","details":{"retry_after_seconds":900}}

The response carries a Retry-After header with the seconds left in the window. That is the body with register_exception_handlers mounted.

The key is the account because the mfa_token holds nothing back: whoever has the password asks POST /auth/login for another one at will. A fresh token keeps getting 429 until the window passes. A right code before the limit logs in normally and clears the count, so someone who mistypes a digit twice owes nothing.

More than one worker? Pass Redis

The default limit keeps the counter in an InMemoryThrottleBackend, which lives in the process. With uvicorn --workers 4, gunicorn or more than one pod, each process has its own counter, and the account reaches 5 * processes attempts per window. In that case, pass an AttemptThrottle over the Redis your processes share:

from fastapi import FastAPI
from redis.asyncio import Redis

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AttemptThrottle, UserAuthService, make_auth_router

from src.api.dependencies import get_session
from src.db.models import UserRecoveryCodeModel


def mount_auth(app: FastAPI, auth_service: UserAuthService, redis: Redis) -> None:
    """Mount the auth router with the MFA limit on Redis."""
    mfa_throttle = AttemptThrottle(redis, max_attempts=5, window_seconds=900)
    app.include_router(
        make_auth_router(
            auth_service,
            session_factory=get_session,
            recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
            mfa_throttle=mfa_throttle,
        ),
    )

The same parameter changes the budget (max_attempts, window_seconds).

docs.title: One code, one login
docs.text:
A TOTP code stays valid for the whole drift window (AUTH_MFA_VERIFY_WINDOW=1 gives 90 seconds). With nothing else, anyone who saw the code go by (over a shoulder, in a log, at a proxy) could log in with it again inside those 90 seconds.

The SDK now stores the 30-second step of the last accepted code in the totp_last_step column and refuses any code from the same step or an earlier one as if it were a wrong code (at verify, the same 401). It holds for confirm, verify, disable and email recovery (request_email_recovery): the code used to activate MFA no longer works for the first login, and the user waits for the next one to show in the app. The admin panel's challenge (POST /admin/mfa) follows the same rule and has the same attempt limit: see Admin.

The write is a conditional UPDATE: the stored row decides, not the loaded object, so a second session that read the user before the first acceptance is refused too (measured with SQLite, two sessions open over the same row).

New column: totp_last_step

Projects already on MFAMixin need the migration before running 0.306.0 — see the migration guide.

docs.title: Service direct
docs.text:
If you mount your own endpoints (no make_auth_router), the UserAuthService methods cover the whole cycle:

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService

from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel


async def enroll_user(service: UserAuthService, session: AsyncSession, user: UserModel) -> None:
    """Generate secret + recovery codes and show them to the user (once)."""
    secret, provisioning_uri, recovery_codes = await service.mfa_enroll(
        session,
        user=user,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
    )
    await session.commit()
    # render provisioning_uri as a QR; show recovery_codes


async def confirm_user(
    service: UserAuthService, session: AsyncSession, user: UserModel, code: str
) -> None:
    """Activate MFA after the user proves they scanned the QR."""
    await service.mfa_confirm(session, user=user, code=code)
    await session.commit()

Full surface:

Method Signature (abridged) Returns is_mfa_enrolled (user) -> bool True if MFA active (and kill-switch on). issue_mfa_token (user) -> str Short JWT bridging step 1 and step 2. mfa_enroll (session, *, user, recovery_code_model) -> tuple[str, str, list[str]] (secret, provisioning_uri, recovery_codes). Raises MFAAlreadyEnrolledException while MFA is active. mfa_confirm (session, *, user, code) -> None Activates MFA. mfa_verify (session, *, mfa_token, code, recovery_code_model, throttle=None) -> UserModel Authenticated user (mint the JWT next). mfa_disable (session, *, user, password, code, recovery_code_model) -> None Clears secret + codes. mfa_reset (session, *, user, recovery_code_model, revoke_sessions=True, revoke_passkeys=True) -> int Clears secret + codes without proof, revokes the sessions and deletes the passkeys; returns how many sessions fell. An operator path — see An account that lost its second factor. change_password_with_mfa (session, *, user, code, new_password, recovery_code_model=None, revoke_sessions=True, throttle=None) -> UserModel Replaces the password on proof of the factor. Raises MFANotEnrolledException on an account without MFA.

docs.title: Changing the password with the factor as proof
docs.text:
A staff account forgot its password, and the e-mailed reset link will not do — the inbox is shared, or the e-mail is exactly what is not trusted. If the person still has the Authenticator app (or a recovery code), the factor is the proof: change_password_with_mfa replaces the password without the current one and without a link.

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService

from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel


async def reset_staff_password(
    service: UserAuthService,
    session: AsyncSession,
    user: UserModel,
    code: str,
    new_password: str,
) -> None:
    """Replace the password of an account with MFA active, proving the factor."""
    await service.change_password_with_mfa(
        session,
        user=user,
        code=code,
        new_password=new_password,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
    )
    await session.commit()

What the method guarantees, in this order:

  1. An account without active MFA is refused with MFANotEnrolledException (422, code="MFA_NOT_ENROLLED") — including with the AUTH_MFA_ENABLED kill-switch off, which makes every account read as "no MFA", exactly as at login.
  2. A password outside the policy is refused before the code is checked (ValidationException), so a weak password does not burn a recovery code.
  3. The code is checked by the same routine as mfa_verify: a TOTP code is single-use and a recovery code gets used_at. A wrong code raises UnauthorizedException ("invalid MFA code").
  4. Sessions are revoked by default, in the same transaction, as in confirm_password_reset. revoke_sessions=False is the explicit opt-out.

It is not a login: no token pair is minted and last_login_at does not change. Without recovery_code_model, only TOTP codes are accepted. Pass throttle= to limit attempts: the key is mfa:{user_id}, the same as mfa_verify, so wrong codes here and at the login's second step spend one budget.

From the terminal

tempest user set-password uses this method when the account has MFA active — see CLI ».

docs.title: Bootstrapping the first privileged account
docs.text:
The route that creates staff can require MFA (make_mfa_required_dependency), but the first privileged account has nobody to invite it: it is born from the terminal. tempest user create --require-mfa makes sure it never exists without a second factor:

    --audit-model src.db.models:AuditLogModel --event staff.bootstrapped

Piece by piece:

  1. The user is inserted, mfa_enroll issues the secret and recovery codes, and mfa_confirm checks the code — all in one transaction, committed only with a valid code. Three wrong codes: it exits with code 1 and nothing is written.
  2. --audit-model writes record_event (actor="cli", changes with email, is_admin and mfa_enrolled) in that same transaction. The model needs AuditRequestMixin — the event column holds the name.   3. The recovery-code table comes from --recovery-code-model (default src.db.models:UserRecoveryCodeModel), and the UserModel needs MFAMixin; with either missing, the command exits with code 2 before writing.

Afterwards, tempest user set-password --email staff@example.com on that account asks for the code (TOTP or recovery code) and changes the password through change_password_with_mfa. With AUTH_MFA_ENABLED off, neither login nor set-password asks for the factor.

docs.title: An account that lost its second factor
docs.text:
The account holder lost the phone and the recovery codes. disable asks for the password and a code; the CLI's set-password asks for the code. Neither helps — and that is how it should be, because asking for the factor is the point. The way back belongs to the operator, explicit and audited:

tempest user mfa-reset --email staff@example.com \
    --audit-model src.db.models:AuditLogModel

Remove the second factor of staff@example.com? It will log in with the password alone until it enrolls again. [y/N]: y
MFA reset for staff@example.com (id=2ced9167-4e7a-4dc5-8626-72b64ff7e4a7)
Revoked 2 active refresh token(s).
Deleted 1 passkey(s).

Piece by piece:

  1. Confirmation is required. In a terminal, the command asks; outside one (CI, a pipe), it needs --yes and exits with code 1 without it. Declining the prompt changes nothing.
  2. The reset is UserAuthService.mfa_reset: it clears totp_secret, totp_enabled_at and totp_last_step and deletes every recovery code of the user — the same cleanup as mfa_disable, without the proof.
  3. Sessions are revoked by default, in the same transaction: whoever kept the lost phone may hold a live session too. --keep-sessions is the explicit opt-out; the table comes from --refresh-token-model (default src.db.models:UserRefreshTokenModel).
  4. Passkeys are deleted by default too, in the same transaction: a passkey signs in without the second factor, and one registered by whoever kept the phone would survive the reset. --keep-passkeys is the explicit opt-out; the table comes from --webauthn-credential-model (default src.db.models:UserWebAuthnCredentialModel). See Password and MFA resets delete the passkeys.
  5. --audit-model writes record_event in the same transaction (actor="cli", changes with mfa_enabled, sessions_revoked and passkeys_revoked), named by --event (default user.mfa_reset). If the audit write fails, the reset rolls back with it. Without --audit-model, the command goes on and says on stderr that no event was recorded.
  6. An account without MFA active exits with code 2 and has no MFA active, nothing to reset. — nothing is written, not even the event.

After the reset the account logs in with the password alone until it enrolls again — and set-password stops asking for a code. If the password is lost too, run both, in that order.

From code, without the CLI — in a support panel, say, behind your own permission check:

from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService

from src.db.models import UserModel, UserRecoveryCodeModel


async def support_mfa_reset(
    service: UserAuthService,
    session: AsyncSession,
    user: UserModel,
) -> int:
    """Remove the second factor of an account that lost it. Returns revoked sessions."""
    revoked = await service.mfa_reset(
        session,
        user=user,
        recovery_code_model=UserRecoveryCodeModel,
    )
    await session.commit()
    return revoked

mfa_reset proves nothing

It checks neither password nor code: it is an operator path. Never expose it on a route the account holder reaches — there it becomes the shortcut disable exists to prevent. Record the audit event in the same transaction.

docs.title: Accounts that do not use emailed links (v0.316.0+)
docs.text:
An operator, a staff account, a service account: whoever reads the inbox should not be able, on their own, to change the password or activate the account. With MFA enrolled the link no longer logs in (it answers the challenge), but it still changes the password — and whoever controls the inbox locks the owner out. The SDK accepts a per-account predicate that closes both link flows:

# src/api/app.py

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import UserAuthService

from src.core.settings import settings
from src.db.models import UserModel, UserTokenModel


def refuses_email_link(user: UserModel) -> bool:
    """Operators never use emailed links."""
    return user.is_admin


auth_service = UserAuthService(
    user_model=UserModel,
    token_model=UserTokenModel,
    auth_settings=settings,
    jwt_settings=settings,
    refuses_email_link=refuses_email_link,
)

The predicate receives an instance of your UserModel (so it can be typed against it) and returns a bool — True refuses. The refuses_email_link=None default keeps the previous behavior.

When the predicate matches:

  • POST /auth/password-reset/request and POST /auth/activation/request answer the same 202 with the same body as an unknown address, and persist no token and send no email. The refusal cannot be enumerated.
  • POST /auth/password-reset/confirm and POST /auth/activate/{token} answer 403 with the code EMAIL_LINK_FORBIDDEN. The token is consumed and the spend is committed before the error (the link never works again), and the password and is_active stay intact.

  • The HTML pages of AUTH_BACKEND_LINKS=true — GET /auth/activate/{token}, GET and POST /auth/password-reset/{token} — render the flow's error page with status 403. The reset form GET does not even show the form (and, since it only peeks the token, does not consume it).

  • POST /auth/signup with AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=false creates the account inactive and persists no activation token and sends no email. The response is the same 201 as an ordinary pending signup (activation_required=true, activation_url=null, no JWT pair): only the user_id differs. Activate that account out of band — tempest user activate, or create it already active with tempest user create.

The predicate sees the freshly inserted row, with the signup_schema columns already set and before on_signup runs: what it reads has to come in the signup body, not be written by the hook.

With AUTH_AUTO_ACTIVATE=true signup does not consult the predicate

The account is born active and depends on no link, so signup returns the JWT pair as always. The reset flows stay closed for it.

In dev mode, the body tells them apart

With AUTH_RETURN_TOKEN_IN_RESPONSE=true (or no EmailUtils) an ordinary signup returns the activation_url in the body and a refused one returns null — the same thing POST /auth/activation/request already does in that mode. The identical response holds when the link goes out by email.

Callers of UserAuthService.signup get, in the second tuple item, None (the account was born active), an ActivationToken (link issued) or an ActivationWithheld (link withheld). Only None authorizes minting JWTs.

Swap the code

Like account_inactive, email_link_forbidden is a field of AuthExceptions: pass a subclass with your own code so the consumer keeps reacting to what it already knows. The body translation (EMAIL_LINK_FORBIDDEN, PT-BR and EN in the default catalog) still applies.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• TOTP secret persisted on the UserModel. Consider encrypting the totp_secret column at rest (Postgres pgcrypto or an application-level Fernet wrapper).
  • The QR code is the secret. provisioning_qr and the URI leave only in the enroll response, and the SDK does not log them; show them once and do not store the image (QR code).
  • Recovery codes stored as SHA-256 hashes. The plaintext leaves only once at enrollment; a table leak yields no usable codes.
  • Recovery codes are single-use. used_at is stamped on consume; replay is rejected.
  • disable requires password + code, and enroll is not a shortcut around it. A hijacked session cannot disable MFA on its own — it needs the password and an active factor. enroll over active MFA answers 409 instead of wiping the recovery codes, so the access token alone cannot reset the factor.
  • mfa_token is short and user-bound. 5-min TTL by default; carries purpose: "mfa_pending" + the sub. Tokens of any other purpose are rejected in mfa_verify.
  • Constant-time verification. TOTPHelper.matching_step (and verify, which calls it) compares the code of each step in the window with hmac.compare_digest.
  • Single-use TOTP codes and a per-account limit. See Attempt limit.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• TOTP is the 6-digit code in an Authenticator app: the server and the app share a secret, and the code is derived from it plus the clock.
  • The extra is [mfa] (it brings pyotp and segno) on top of [auth], and nothing is mounted unless AUTH_MFA_ENABLED=True.
  • enroll returns the QR ready (provisioning_qr, an SVG data URI; null without segno), and provisioning_qr_terminal draws the same QR in a CLI. The QR is the secret: show it once, never log it, do not store it.
  • The router requires recovery_code_model: without it, it raises RuntimeError at wiring time rather than in production — losing the phone with no recovery code means losing the account.
  • With MFA on, POST /auth/login stops returning the JWT pair: it returns mfa_required=True plus an intermediate token, and the second step trades a code for the JWTs.
  • If you mount your own endpoints, the UserAuthService methods cover the whole cycle without the router. change_password_with_mfa replaces the password on proof of the factor, with no e-mail link and no token minted.
  • Whoever lost the phone and the recovery codes comes back through the operator: tempest user mfa-reset (or mfa_reset in code) removes the factor without proof, with confirmation, an audit event in the same transaction, the sessions revoked and the passkeys deleted.
  • The TOTP secret lives on UserModel — consider encrypting that column at rest.
  • /auth/mfa/verify answers 429 after five wrong codes per account in 15 minutes, and each TOTP code is worth one login. With more than one worker, pass mfa_throttle= over Redis.
  • The access token says how the session started (amr), and make_mfa_required_dependency refuses with 403 MFA_REQUIRED the one that never passed the second factor. Confirming MFA ends the other sessions.
  • refuses_email_link= closes the emailed-link flow for accounts such as operators: the request answers like an unknown address, confirmation returns 403 EMAIL_LINK_FORBIDDEN without changing the password, and signup creates the account inactive without sending a link.

  • Server-side sessions » — JWT alternative, combinable with MFA at step 1.
  • Security » — CSRF, rate-limit and body-size limit for the auth endpoints.

docs.title: Migrations
docs.text:
Every database recipe assumes the schema already exists. This one is about the step before that: how the schema comes into being, and why the hand-written version of that step is wrong in a way that stays invisible for weeks.

The SDK ships the whole path as one method — AlembicHelper.sync_schema() — and the rest of this page explains what it decides, so you can recognise which state your database is in.

docs.title: The complete bootstrap
docs.text:
# src/db/schema.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper, SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum

from src.core.settings import settings


async def sync_schema() -> SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum:
    """Bring the database schema in line with the migration tree."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    return await helper.sync_schema_async()

Call it from the lifespan and the service boots with the right schema from any starting state:

# src/api/app.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

from src.db.schema import sync_schema


@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI) -> AsyncIterator[None]:
    """Sync the schema before the first request is served."""
    outcome = await sync_schema()
    print(f"schema: {outcome.value}")
    yield


app: FastAPI = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)

docs.title: From async code, use the _async method
docs.text:
The lifespan runs inside uvicorn's event loop. Every AlembicHelper method that executes alembic/env.py has an _async twin — upgrade_async, safe_upgrade_async, downgrade_async, stamp_async, revision_async, check_async, current_async, has_existing_schema_async, adopt_async, sync_schema_async, squash_async, pending_destructive_ops_async — with the same signature, and that is the one you call from async code.

The reason is the env.py the SDK generates: it starts the async engine with asyncio.run(...), and asyncio.run cannot be called while a loop is already running. Calling the sync method from the lifespan now fails immediately, with the right instruction:

RuntimeError: AlembicHelper.upgrade() was called from a running event loop. It runs alembic/env.py, which drives migrations with asyncio.run() and cannot nest inside the loop; use `await helper.upgrade_async(...)` instead.

Before, the same error came from deep inside Alembic as asyncio.run() cannot be called from a running event loop, together with a RuntimeWarning: coroutine 'run_async_migrations' was never awaited — and check() did not even raise: it swallowed the error and answered False, as if the schema had drifted.

The _async method runs the sync one in a worker thread, which has no loop of its own, so the asyncio.run in env.py works there and the service's loop keeps serving while the migration runs. Since the thread needs nothing new in env.py, the env.py already in your repository keeps working — no need to regenerate it.

Sync current() still works on the loop

Reading the revision does not go through env.py: with a sync driver installed (the stdlib sqlite3, or psycopg2 on PostgreSQL), helper.current() works from async code as before. Only an async-only install (asyncpg with no sync driver) takes the asyncio.run path — and then it raises too, asking for current_async().

Technical details: sharing the connection instead of a thread

Alembic has an official recipe for running the migration on the loop itself: open an AsyncConnection and hand the sync connection that run_sync provides over as config.attributes["connection"]. The env.py the SDK generates from this release on accepts it — given the connection, it migrates on it, without creating an engine or calling asyncio.run:

# src/db/shared_connection.py
from alembic import command
from sqlalchemy.engine import Connection
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncEngine, create_async_engine
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper

from src.core.settings import settings


async def upgrade_on_shared_connection() -> None:
    """Run every pending migration on a connection this code owns."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    config = helper.config

    def _upgrade(connection: Connection) -> None:
        """Hand the sync connection to env.py and upgrade on it."""
        config.attributes["connection"] = connection
        command.upgrade(config, "head")

    engine: AsyncEngine = create_async_engine(settings.DATABASE_URL)
    async with engine.begin() as conn:
        await conn.run_sync(_upgrade)
    await engine.dispose()

The _async methods do not take that path, and the reason is compatibility: an env.py generated before this release ignores config.attributes and calls asyncio.run regardless — inside run_sync the loop is running, and it fails with the same error as before. The thread works with every env.py already generated. Use the path above when the migration must run on your connection or transaction, and regenerate env.py for it: run tempest db init in an empty directory and copy the generated alembic/env.py over yours, checking the metadata import (the default is from src.db.models import BaseModel).

The new env.py also refuses, with its own message, to be executed from inside a loop without a connection handed over — the case of calling command.upgrade straight from async code.

docs.title: The three states it tells apart
docs.text:
sync_schema() asks the question almost every hand-written bootstrap forgets: does the database hold tables Alembic did not create?

Starting state What runs Return Empty database upgrade() — the base revision creates the tables, without the destructive guard SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum.SYNCED Database that predates Alembic stamps the base, then safe_upgrade() SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum.ADOPTED Database already under Alembic safe_upgrade() SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum.SYNCED Project with no revisions yet nothing SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum.NO_MIGRATIONS

The empty database is the easy case, and it is what makes the rest work: the schema the base revision builds is, by construction, the same one later revisions assume they are altering — because it came from them.

An empty database goes through the history's drop_column

On a database with no stamp and no application table, every revision is pending. The safe_upgrade guard reads their source, not the database: a project that ever dropped a column would be refused on its first boot, before a single table exists. That is why this path runs upgrade() directly — there is no row to delete. In the other two states the database holds data, and the guard applies as always.

docs.title: Why create_tables() is not the answer
docs.text:
The Database recipe says db.create_tables() is for tests and local development only. It is worth also saying what happens if you use it, because the prohibition without the consequence does not make anyone see the defect in their own code:

create_all is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS

Against a table that already exists, create_tables() adds no column at all. It does not fail, does not warn, and does not return anything different. It is a silent no-op.

The real defect, which took a service down for a day:

# scripts/broken_bootstrap.py — the defect, reproduced; not a recipe.
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper, AsyncDatabaseManager

from src.core.settings import settings

db: AsyncDatabaseManager = AsyncDatabaseManager(settings.DATABASE_URL)


async def broken_bootstrap() -> None:
    """Reach the worst possible state: old schema, Alembic reporting head."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    if await helper.current_async() is None:
        await db.create_tables()
        await helper.stamp_async("head")
        return
    await helper.safe_upgrade_async()

Every line is plausible. Together they produce the worst possible state: an old schema, and Alembic declaring itself up to date.

$ alembic current
a3f9c21e88b4 (head)

$ alembic upgrade head
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Context impl SQLiteImpl.
INFO  [alembic.runtime.migration] Will assume non-transactional DDL.

Nothing to do. alembic history flags nothing. Weeks later, the first query touching a new column blows up far from the cause:

sqlalchemy.exc.OperationalError: (sqlite3.OperationalError) no such column: messages.edited_at

On the user's side that reads as "sending messages stopped working": the history GET returns 500, and nothing at boot said a word.

docs.title: Adopting a database that predates Alembic
docs.text:
This is the case the code above was trying to handle. The right answer is not to stamp head — it is to stamp the base revision:

# src/db/schema.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper

from src.core.settings import settings


def adopt_existing_database() -> bool:
    """Bring a pre-Alembic schema under Alembic, without upgrading it."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    return helper.adopt()

Stamping the base says "the baseline is already applied" — which is true, because the tables exist — and leaves every revision after it pending, which is also true. The safe_upgrade() that follows runs exactly those.

Stamping head says "everything is already applied", which is false for all but the first.

adopt() does nothing when that is not the case: a database already stamped has nothing to adopt, and an empty one needs the baseline to run, not to be skipped. That is why sync_schema() can call it unconditionally.

The question is answered by has_existing_schema()

It lists the tables and discounts alembic_version, which Alembic writes itself — its presence says nothing about the application schema.

docs.title: Repairing a database stamped wrong
docs.text:
If you are already in the bad state, the fix has two steps. The first clears the pointer; the second re-adopts properly:

# scripts/repair_schema.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper, SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum

from src.core.settings import settings


def repair() -> SchemaSyncOutcomeEnum:
    """Clear a wrong stamp and re-adopt the schema from the base."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    helper.stamp("base")
    return helper.sync_schema()

stamp("base") is not the same as stamp(helper.base_revision()): "base" is Alembic's word for no revision applied, and it deletes the alembic_version row. After that the database looks like what it is — an existing schema with no pointer — and sync_schema() takes the adoption path.

Check what is pending before you upgrade

After stamp("base"), the revisions between base and head will run against a schema that may already carry part of them. Run helper.pending_destructive_ops() and read helper.history() first — and have a backup. safe_upgrade refuses destructive migrations without force=True, which helps, but does not replace looking.

docs.title: SQLite: migrations run with foreign keys off
docs.text:
On SQLite, Alembic alters a table in batch mode (the generated env.py sets render_as_batch=True): it creates a copy with the new shape, copies the rows, drops the original and renames the copy. With PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON, that DROP TABLE runs the foreign-key actions of the dropped table — and a child with ON DELETE CASCADE goes with it.

Measured with Alembic 1.19.1 and SQLite 3.47.1, adding one nullable column to the parent table with batch_alter_table("org", recreate="always"):

PRAGMA foreign_keys Rows in member before → after Error 0 3 → 3 none 1 3 → 0 none

So the engines the SDK builds to migrate — the generated env.py's and the AlembicHelper read engines (current(), has_existing_schema()) — keep FK off, while AsyncDatabaseManager turns it on by default. If you use the connection-sharing recipe (config.attributes["connection"], described above), the generated env.py checks the pragma of the connection it receives and refuses before migrating:

RuntimeError: refusing to run migrations on a SQLite connection with PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON: Alembic batch mode recreates tables, and dropping the old copy of a parent table runs ON DELETE CASCADE on its children, deleting their rows without an error. ...

The way out is migrating on a connection from an engine without FK — a manager just for that:

# src/db/shared_connection.py
from alembic import command
from sqlalchemy.engine import Connection
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AlembicHelper, AsyncDatabaseManager

from src.core.settings import settings


async def upgrade_on_shared_connection() -> None:
    """Migrate on a connection that does not enforce foreign keys."""
    helper: AlembicHelper = AlembicHelper(
        "alembic.ini",
        db_url=settings.DATABASE_URL,
    )
    config = helper.config

    def _upgrade(connection: Connection) -> None:
        """Hand the connection to env.py and migrate on it."""
        config.attributes["connection"] = connection
        command.upgrade(config, "head")

    migrations_db: AsyncDatabaseManager = AsyncDatabaseManager(
        settings.DATABASE_URL,
        sqlite_foreign_keys=False,
    )
    await migrations_db.connect()
    try:
        async with migrations_db.engine.begin() as conn:
            await conn.run_sync(_upgrade)
    finally:
        await migrations_db.disconnect()

PRAGMA foreign_keys=OFF cannot fix an open connection

SQLite ignores the pragma inside a transaction, and the connection that reaches env.py is already in one. Turning it off has to happen when the engine is built (sqlite_foreign_keys=False, or a plain create_async_engine(url)), not on the connection.

An env.py generated before this version does not refuse

The check lives in env.py, and yours was copied into the repository when you ran tempest db init. If it receives a connection from an AsyncDatabaseManager — which now turns FK on by default —, switch to a connection without FK as above and regenerate env.py (run tempest db init in an empty directory and copy alembic/env.py over yours, checking the metadata import). Migrating through AlembicHelper or the CLI is not affected: those paths open their own engine, without FK.

docs.title: The generated env.py
docs.text:
tempest db init (or AlembicHelper.init) writes an alembic/env.py of three statements — the docstring is the only prose, with no inline comment:

"""Alembic environment script generated by tempest-fastapi-sdk."""

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.db import run_alembic_env

from src.db.models import BaseModel

target_metadata = BaseModel.metadata

run_alembic_env(target_metadata)

Everything the file used to do now lives in run_alembic_env: resolving DATABASE_URL, the revision hooks, render_enum_types, batch mode, the offline and online paths, and the connection handed over in config.attributes["connection"]. Two reasons, both seen on a real service:

  • A copy drifts. A service rewrote env.py by hand to pass lint, ended up with its own copy of the SDK's logic — later fixes never reached it — and lost the sys.path handling along the way, so uv run alembic downgrade -1 stopped importing src. With a call into the SDK, the fix arrives when the package is upgraded.
  • A full script cannot be lint-clean under every configuration. The alembic/ directory next to pyproject.toml makes ruff's default (src = [".", "src"]) treat alembic as first-party, and the tempest new scaffold (src = ["src", "tests"]) as third-party. from alembic import context lands in a different import block under each, so one of the two always reports I001. The generated file imports no alembic, and sorts the same under both.

The guard tests/test_alembic_env_lint_guard.py generates the file in a temporary project and runs ruff check --select E,W,F,I under both configurations (plus the scaffold's whole configuration): zero errors and zero inline comments.

docs.title: The bare Alembic CLI works too
docs.text: The generated alembic.ini carries script_location = %(here)s/alembic and prepend_sys_path = %(here)s, both anchored on the ini's own directory. So uv run alembic upgrade head and uv run alembic downgrade -1 import your package without the tempest CLI, and a lifespan that passes the ini's absolute path (AlembicHelper("/app/alembic.ini")) finds the scripts whatever directory the process started in. Up to 0.312.x the ini carried alembic and ., relative to the working directory, and only worked from the project root. path_separator = os comes with it: without it, Alembic 1.19.1 emits a DeprecationWarning about the legacy splitting of prepend_sys_path, and anyone running with -W error (or filterwarnings = ["error"]) sees the migration fail.

docs.title: One more hook
docs.text:
The hooks every revision goes through are in DEFAULT_REVISION_HOOKS. To add your own, compose and pass it as process_revision_directives= — the value replaces the default, so include the SDK's:

"""Alembic environment script with one extra revision hook."""

from typing import Any

from alembic.operations.ops import MigrationScript
from alembic.runtime.migration import MigrationContext
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.db import (
    DEFAULT_REVISION_HOOKS,
    compose_hooks,
    run_alembic_env,
)

from src.db.models import BaseModel


def skip_empty_revisions(
    context: MigrationContext,
    revision: Any,
    directives: list[Any],
) -> None:
    """Write no file when autogenerate finds no change."""
    script = directives[0]
    if (
        isinstance(script, MigrationScript)
        and script.upgrade_ops is not None
        and script.upgrade_ops.is_empty()
    ):
        directives[:] = []


run_alembic_env(
    BaseModel.metadata,
    process_revision_directives=compose_hooks(
        *DEFAULT_REVISION_HOOKS,
        skip_empty_revisions,
    ),
)

Measured against PostgreSQL 16: after upgrade head, an alembic revision --autogenerate with no model change writes no file.

Already have an env.py generated earlier?

It keeps working. To start receiving the SDK's fixes, replace its content with the three statements above (keeping your metadata import) and add prepend_sys_path = %(here)s and path_separator = os to the [alembic] section of alembic.ini. Migrations already written do not change: op.replace_enum and op.drop_enum_type are registered when env.py imports tempest_fastapi_sdk.db.

docs.title: Each revision file
docs.text:
tempest db revision -m "Cria tabela de anotações" (and AlembicHelper.revision) writes:

alembic/versions/2026_10_11_2317-c16a7545f8f9_cria_tabela_de_anotacoes.py
  • An ASCII name. The message is folded to ASCII only to build the file name, so alembic/versions/ holds no accented module name; the migration's docstring starts with the message as you wrote it, accents included.
  • No comment line. tempest db init writes the SDK's own script.py.mako, without the # revision identifiers line of Alembic's template, and the revision drops the # ### commands auto generated by Alembic ### markers autogenerate puts around the operations.

With bare alembic revision

The new template applies (no # revision identifiers), but the name keeps its accents and the markers stay: measured with alembic revision --autogenerate -m "Cria anotações", the file came out as ..._cria_anotações.py with all four markers. Use tempest db revision.

Project initialized before this?

The ASCII name and the marker removal already apply, because they live in tempest db revision. For the comment-free template, replace alembic/script.py.mako with the SDK's:

uv run python -c "from importlib import resources; print(resources.files('tempest_fastapi_sdk.db._alembic_templates').joinpath('script.py.mako').read_text())" > alembic/script.py.mako

docs.title: Where create_tables() is legitimate
docs.text:
In tests and throwaway local development — where the database is born and dies in the same process, and there is no migration to drift from:

# tests/conftest.py
from collections.abc import AsyncIterator

import pytest
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import AsyncDatabaseManager


@pytest.fixture
async def session() -> AsyncIterator[AsyncSession]:
    """Yield a session over a fresh in-memory schema."""
    db: AsyncDatabaseManager = AsyncDatabaseManager(
        "sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory:"
    )
    await db.create_tables()
    async with db.get_session_context() as opened:
        yield opened
    await db.drop_tables()

The technical reason it works here and not in production is the same in both cases: create_all only knows how to create what is missing. In a database that was just born, "what is missing" is everything — so it gets it right. In one that has already run, "what is missing" is no table at all, but possibly several columns — and columns it does not look at.

Recap

  • sync_schema() is the whole bootstrap: it tells an empty database, a pre-Alembic one and an already-migrated one apart, and reports which path it took.
  • On an empty database the whole tree runs without the destructive guard (there is no data to lose); with an application table, a pending drop_* still raises DestructiveMigrationError without force=True.
  • From async code (lifespan, endpoint), call the _async twin (await helper.sync_schema_async()); the sync method raises with a loop running, naming the _async one to use.
  • create_tables() is CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS — a silent no-op on an existing table. It is never the step that evolves a schema.
  • When adopting an existing schema, stamp the base revision (helper.base_revision(), or just helper.adopt()), never head.
  • To repair a wrong stamp("head"): stamp("base"), then sync_schema().
  • create_tables() stays legitimate where there is no migration to drift from: tests and in-memory SQLite.
  • On SQLite, migrations run on a connection without foreign keys: batch mode rebuilds the table and the cascade would delete the children. The generated env.py refuses a handed-over connection with FK on.
  • The generated env.py is one call to run_alembic_env: SDK fixes arrive with the package upgrade, and the file passes ruff with no inline comment. prepend_sys_path = %(here)s lets the bare Alembic CLI import your package.

  • CLI » — tempest db upgrade, revision, stamp, check.
  • Safe deploys » — safe_upgrade and the CI drift gate.

docs.title: Model weights (Hub lifecycle)
docs.text:
Loading a model by id is the easy half. The other half is everything the first from_pretrained call hides: which commit you actually got, how many gigabytes it wrote to which directory, whether the disk had room, and how to make the next boot reproduce the same weights without a network.

The tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.hub module owns that half.

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai-hub]"   # the weight lifecycle alone
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[genai]"       # includes the above + torch/transformers

The module imports with no extra at all

huggingface_hub is resolved inside the function that needs it. The schemas (ModelRef, CachedModel) stay usable and testable on a host that will never download anything; a missing dependency raises an ImportError naming the extra to install.

docs.title: Where the weights live (and why the second run is instant)
docs.text:
Before any configuration, the fact that answers the most common question: the download happens once. The first call writes the weights to an on-disk cache; every run after that reads them from there, with no network.

$ python test.py          # first time
model.safetensors: 988MB [00:14, 66.7MB/s]
Loading weights: 100%|██████████| 290/290 [00:00<00:00, 1084 it/s]

$ python test.py          # every time after
Loading weights: 100%|██████████| 290/290 [00:00<00:00, 2335 it/s]

The default cache is huggingface_hub's own:

Where When $HF_HOME/hub HF_HOME is set in the environment ~/.cache/huggingface/hub the default, when it is not cache_dir="..." you passed the argument to the loader — wins over both

Container restarts, cache gone

The cache lives on the process's filesystem. In a container with no volume, every restart downloads everything again — gigabytes of network and minutes of boot on each deploy. Mount a volume and point the cache at it:

# docker-compose.yaml
services:
  api:
    environment:
      HF_HOME: /models
    volumes:
      - hf-cache:/models

volumes:
  hf-cache:

Or, if you prefer it in code, TextGenerator(..., cache_dir="/models").

That rate-limit warning on stderr

Warning: You are sending unauthenticated requests to the HF Hub.
Please set a HF_TOKEN to enable higher rate limits and faster downloads.

Anonymous downloads work, but they are throttled. Set HF_TOKEN in the environment (or pass hf_token= to the loader) and the warning goes away with the limit — and it is mandatory for a gated model such as Llama.

And it shows up even when the weights are already cached. It is not the download: with local_files_only=False (the default) the load still reaches the Hub to resolve the revision, and that anonymous request is what prints the warning. With local_files_only=True there is no request at all — and no warning:

$ python app.py                          # default
Warning: You are sending unauthenticated requests to the HF Hub...

$ python app.py                          # local_files_only=True
(nothing)

Changing model_id or revision is a different cache entry. That is not a bug: they are different weights. If a second run downloaded again, one of those two changed — or the process's HF_HOME did.

docs.title: Configure it once, in the environment
docs.text:
Passing cache_dir= and local_files_only= to every loader works, but it scatters an infrastructure decision through domain code. All three values have an environment variable — and the argument always wins, so the service sets the default and a call that needs something else still can:

Variable Equivalent argument Effect GENAI_CACHE_DIR cache_dir= Where weights are written and read GENAI_OFFLINE local_files_only= Load from cache, never touch the network GENAI_HF_TOKEN hf_token= Authenticate to the Hub (gated + no rate limit) 
# .env
GENAI_CACHE_DIR=/models
GENAI_OFFLINE=true
GENAI_HF_TOKEN=hf_xxx
settings.py
from tempest_fastapi_sdk import BaseAppSettings, GenAISettings


class Settings(GenAISettings, BaseAppSettings):
    """The three variables, typed and visible to `tempest check-config`."""

Declaring the class is optional

The loaders read the environment directly — a service that never declares GenAISettings behaves the same. The class is what makes the values typed, documented and visible in the config check.

GENAI_OFFLINE accepts 1, true, yes and on, in any case; anything else is false. And, repeating it because it is the point: passing the argument beats the variable in both directions — with GENAI_OFFLINE=true in the environment, an explicit local_files_only=False goes back to using the network.

docs.title: The problem: main moves
docs.text:
This is what nearly every self-hosted service writes on day one:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextGenerator

generator = TextGenerator("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct")

It works. And it has three holes:

Hole What actually happens Unpinned revision The author pushes to main. The pod restarts. You are serving different weights without having changed a line. Download inside the request The first POST /generate pays for a multi-gigabyte download while a client waits on the other end. No offline mode An air-gapped host has no way to guarantee the load will not reach the network — it only finds out when it fails.

All three close with the same three keywords, and they are identical across every loader in the SDK.

docs.title: Pin the revision
docs.text:
First, find the commit behind the branch:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import resolve_revision

sha: str | None = resolve_revision("Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct", revision="main")
print(sha)

a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2

From the terminal, the same thing — alongside the download:

tempest model pull Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct --pin

Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
  revision   : default
  pin to     : a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2
  path       : /home/u/.cache/huggingface/hub/models--Qwen--Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct/snapshots/a8b602d
  size       : 999.59 MB
  files      : 9

Store the sha in the service configuration and pass it down:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import TextGenerator

generator = TextGenerator(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    revision="a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2",
)

resolve_revision returns None when it cannot pin

Hub down, private repository without a token, revision that does not exist — the function returns None instead of raising. The caller decides whether to proceed unpinned or abort the deploy; that call is yours, not the library's.

docs.title: Download before serving
docs.text:
The place to pay for a download is the image build or the deploy step — never the request path.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import ModelSnapshot, download_model

snapshot: ModelSnapshot = download_model(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    revision="a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2",
    cache_dir="/var/lib/models",
    allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"],
)
print(snapshot.size_bytes, snapshot.file_count, snapshot.path)

In the Dockerfile, one line:

RUN tempest model pull Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct \
    --revision a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2 \
    --cache-dir /var/lib/models \
    --allow "*.json" --allow "*.safetensors"

--allow is not a detail

Many repositories publish the weights twice — .bin and .safetensors. Restricting to the formats you actually load usually cuts half the download and half the disk.

docs.title: It refuses to start what will not fit
docs.text:
download_model sizes what it is about to download on the Hub before writing anything and compares it against the free space. Only the files allow_patterns / ignore_patterns select count — filtered by the same huggingface_hub function snapshot_download uses — and only those not already cached for that revision:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import download_model

try:
    download_model("meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B", cache_dir="/var/lib/models")
except OSError as exc:
    print(exc)

meta-llama/Llama-3.1-70B needs ~154.0 GB (estimate x1.1) but only 41.3 GB are free on /var/lib/models

Failing in two seconds with a number beats failing forty minutes later with a half-written cache. A 28 GB repository that ships its weights as both .bin and .safetensors, downloaded with allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"], asks for ~15.4 GB (14 GB x 1.1), not 30.8 GB. A file the cache already holds for that revision does not count; a blob cached under another revision still does, so the possible error is over-estimating, never the reverse.

To size it without downloading (the same patterns apply here):

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import model_disk_bytes

needed: int | None = model_disk_bytes(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    allow_patterns=["*.json", "*.safetensors"],
)
print(needed)

Disk and memory are different questions

model_disk_bytes answers "does it fit the volume?". What answers "does it fit RAM/VRAM?" is can_run — the two checks are independent, and a healthy deploy runs both.

docs.title: Run offline
docs.text:
With the weights already cached, local_files_only=True turns any load into a purely local operation:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import Embedder, TextGenerator

generator = TextGenerator(
    "Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    revision="a8b602d5f1c9e0d3b7c1f4a2e9d8c7b6a5f4e3d2",
    cache_dir="/var/lib/models",
    local_files_only=True,
)
embedder = Embedder(
    "sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2",
    cache_dir="/var/lib/models",
    local_files_only=True,
)

If the weights are not there the load fails immediately, instead of quietly reaching the network from a host that was supposed to be isolated.

docs.title: The same three keywords everywhere
docs.text:
There is no per-class "way to pin":

Class Module TextGenerator tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai Embedder tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai VisionTextGenerator tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai ClassifierModerator tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai Reranker tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai.rag

All of them take revision=, local_files_only= and trust_remote_code=, on top of the cache_dir=/hf_token= that already existed. Two exceptions, both forced by the library underneath:

  • SpeechToText takes revision=, local_files_only= and hf_token=, but not trust_remote_code — CTranslate2 loads weights, never repository Python.
  • OnnxEmbedder already has the graph on disk; only the tokenizer comes from the Hub, so the parameters are tokenizer_revision= and hf_token=. Point tokenizer at a local tokenizer.json when the host must not reach the network.

docs.title: trust_remote_code is opt-in on purpose
docs.text:
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import VisionTextGenerator

generator = VisionTextGenerator(
    "Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)

This executes Python from the repository

Some architectures only load with trust_remote_code=True, and transformers says so in the error message. Flipping the switch runs code you did not review, from the same repository the weights came from — which is why it is per-model rather than an SDK default. If you do flip it, pin the revision alongside: the code you audited today and the code tomorrow are the same main.

docs.title: See and reclaim the cache
docs.text:
Weights are the biggest thing a self-hosted service writes to disk, and nothing prunes them: every model ever loaded stays until someone removes it.

tempest model cache-list --revisions

   4.43 GB  Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct
   4.43 GB    a1b2c3d4e5f6  [main]
 999.59 MB  Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct
 999.59 MB    a8b602d5f1c9  [main]
 181.97 MB  sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2
 181.97 MB    1110a243fdf4  [main]
   5.61 GB  total

In Python, to expose it on an operations endpoint:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import CachedModel, cache_size_bytes, list_cached_models

models: list[CachedModel] = list_cached_models()
for model in models:
    print(model.model_id, model.size_bytes, len(model.revisions))
print(cache_size_bytes())

To reclaim space:

tempest model cache-rm Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct --dry-run

would free 4.43 GB by removing Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import remove_cached_model

freed: int = remove_cached_model(
    "Qwen/Qwen2-VL-2B-Instruct",
    revision="a1b2c3d4e5f6",
)
print(freed)

Removing weights has no undo

The only way back is downloading them again. That is why the command asks for confirmation (skip it with --yes) and --dry-run reports the size without touching anything. A model that is not cached returns 0 — not an error, a successful no-op.

docs.title: The object underneath: ModelRef
docs.text:
Every loader builds a ModelRef and forwards it. You rarely need to construct one by hand, but it is what explains the behaviour:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.genai import ModelRef

ref = ModelRef(
    model_id="Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct",
    revision="a8b602d",
    local_files_only=True,
)
print(ref.loader_kwargs())
print(ref.download_kwargs())

{'revision': 'a8b602d', 'local_files_only': True}
{'revision': 'a8b602d', 'local_files_only': True}

Only what differs from the default is emitted. That keeps the call identical to what the SDK sent before when nothing is pinned, and keeps the same dictionary usable with narrower loaders — tokenizers.Tokenizer.from_pretrained accepts revision but not trust_remote_code. download_kwargs() drops trust_remote_code, which is a load-time decision and means nothing while fetching files.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• resolve_revision turns main into the immutable sha. Pin it and the boot stops depending on the day.
  • download_model / tempest model pull pays for the download in the build or the deploy, and refuses to start what the disk cannot hold.
  • local_files_only=True makes the load purely local — the mode an air-gapped host wants.
  • trust_remote_code=True is opt-in per model, because it executes repository code.
  • list_cached_models / remove_cached_model (and cache-list / cache-rm) show and reclaim what the weights occupy.

Where to go next: Self-hosted generative AI for what to do with the weights once loaded, and Modelops to measure, quantize and export them.

docs.title: Modelops (export, bench, quantization)
docs.text:
Three jobs that always travel together: you quantize to make a model cheaper, you benchmark to find out whether it actually got cheaper, and you export to the format the target device runs.

tempest_fastapi_sdk.modelops covers all three, measuring CPU, RAM, GPU and energy over the same window — "how fast" and "how much power" come out of one measurement instead of two unrelated runs.

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[modelops]"        # benchmarking, monitoring, compact reader
uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[modelops-onnx]"   # + ONNX, .ort, quantization

Nothing here caps your transformers version

Two extras, and neither pulls optimum — which today declares transformers<4.58. The HuggingFace path (optimizing and quantizing an export) runs on the onnxruntime from [modelops-onnx], so your service stays free to use the 5.x series. The one step that does need optimum is producing the export, and that becomes a throwaway uvx command — see "HuggingFace: optimize and quantize an export".

Submodule, not top-level

Like genai/vision, this is heavy tooling and lives in a submodule: from tempest_fastapi_sdk.modelops import benchmark_onnx. The module imports with no extra installed — every dependency is resolved inside the function that needs it, and its absence raises an ImportError naming the extra to install.

docs.title: Start here
docs.text:
If you have never used this module, start with this block. It runs as is — no data of yours needed, the dataset ships inside scikit-learn.

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[modelops-onnx,modelops-sklearn]"

from sklearn.datasets import load_iris
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.modelops import edge_pipeline, load_edge_package

# 1. Any model, trained on the dataset that ships with scikit-learn.
data = load_iris()
X_train, X_test, y_train, y_test = train_test_split(
