State lives in an in-process dict. Every uvicorn restart/redeploy logs everyone out, and with more than one replica each worker sees only its own sessions (a cookie issued by one replica hits 401 on the other). It is strictly for tests and local dev — in production always use RedisSessionStore.

docs.title: RedisSessionStore — production
docs.text:
from redis.asyncio import Redis

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import RedisSessionStore

from src.core.settings import settings


session_store = RedisSessionStore(
    Redis.from_url(settings.REDIS_URL, decode_responses=True),
    prefix="myapp:",
)

Internal schema:

  • myapp:sess:<sha256-hex> — JSON of the Session, TTL = expires_at - now
  • myapp:user:<user-uuid> — Redis SET of session hashes (index for list_by_user / delete_by_user)

Redis handles TTL automatically — no janitor process needed.

RedisSessionStore requires the [cache] extra

RedisSessionStore depends on the async redis client, which only ships with the [cache] extra. Since it feeds a middleware, hand it a Redis.from_url(...) (lazy) or AsyncRedisManager.client_proxy — never cache.client, which raises before the lifespan. Install with uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[cache]" (add auth etc. as your service needs). MemorySessionStore needs no extra at all.

docs.title: Custom
docs.text:
Any class that implements the SessionStore protocol (6 async methods: get, set, touch, delete, delete_by_user and list_by_user) plugs in out of the box — DynamoDB, a Postgres table, Memcached, etc.

touch(session) -> bool is what makes revocation hold against a request already in flight. SessionAuth.resolve reads the session and writes last_seen_at (and the new expires_at, under SESSION_SLIDING) back through it, not through set. The contract: update only if the key still exists, in one atomic operation, without re-adding the session to the user index, and return False when it is gone — resolve then returns None. In RedisSessionStore that is a single SET ... XX. Without it, a logout or revoke_all that lands between the read and the write is undone: the write re-creates the session with a fresh TTL.

Custom store without touch

A store written before touch keeps working: resolve falls back to set and emits a DeprecationWarning, because that path cannot stop a revoked session from coming back. Implement touch to close the window.

docs.title: Middleware
docs.text:
SessionMiddleware runs before the routers, reads the cookie, resolves through the store, and populates request.state.session:

from fastapi import APIRouter, Depends

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import Session, make_session_dependency

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/profile")
async def profile(session: Session = Depends(make_session_dependency(required=True))):
    return {"user_id": str(session.user_id), "data": session.data}

required=True (default): no cookie → UnauthorizedException → 401 in the SDK envelope.

required=False: the handler accepts both — session is Session | None. Use on public endpoints that adapt content for logged-in users.

Direct access (no dependency):

from fastapi import APIRouter, Request

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import Session

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/anything")
async def handler(request: Request) -> dict:
    s: Session | None = request.state.session
    return {"authenticated": s is not None}

docs.title: Login without a user table
docs.text:
SessionAuth(user_model=...) looks the e-mail up in a table and verifies the hash. An admin panel guarded by one root credential from the environment has no table to point at. For that case, SessionAuth.from_credentials(username, password, ...) builds the service on a StaticCredentialAuthenticator, and make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login")) guards the HTML route with no middleware at all.

The whole example — login form, protected page and logout:

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Form, Request, status
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse, RedirectResponse, Response
from pydantic import SecretStr

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseAppSettings,
    MemorySessionStore,
    Session,
    SessionAuth,
    SessionSettings,
    UnauthorizedException,
    make_session_dependency,
    redirect_to,
    register_exception_handlers,
)


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ADMIN_USERNAME: str
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: SecretStr


settings = Settings()
session_auth = SessionAuth.from_credentials(
    settings.ADMIN_USERNAME,
    settings.ADMIN_PASSWORD,
    store=MemorySessionStore(),
    settings=settings,
)
require_admin = make_session_dependency(
    session_auth=session_auth,
    on_missing=redirect_to("/login"),
)

app = FastAPI()
register_exception_handlers(app)


@app.get("/login", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def login_page() -> str:
    return (
        '<form method="post" action="/login">'
        '<input name="username"> <input name="password" type="password">'
        "<button>Entrar</button></form>"
    )


@app.post("/login")
async def login(
    request: Request,
    username: str = Form(),
    password: str = Form(),
) -> Response:
    try:
        _session, plaintext = await session_auth.login_with_credentials(
            username,
            password,
            previous_session_id=request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME),
        )
    except UnauthorizedException:
        return HTMLResponse("Credenciais inválidas", status_code=401)
    response = RedirectResponse("/admin", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)
    response.set_cookie(value=plaintext, **settings.session_cookie_kwargs())
    return response


@app.get("/admin", response_class=HTMLResponse)
async def admin(session: Session = Depends(require_admin)) -> str:
    return f"<h1>Painel</h1><p>Sessão expira em {session.expires_at:%H:%M}</p>"


@app.post("/logout")
async def logout(request: Request) -> Response:
    cookie = request.cookies.get(settings.SESSION_COOKIE_NAME)
    if cookie:
        await session_auth.revoke(cookie)
    response = RedirectResponse("/login", status_code=status.HTTP_303_SEE_OTHER)
    response.delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs())
    return response

With ADMIN_USERNAME=root, ADMIN_PASSWORD=s3cret and SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=false in the environment, driven by httpx.AsyncClient:

GET /admin sem cookie: 303 /login
POST /login errado: 401 Credenciais inválidas
POST /login certo: 303 /admin
  Set-Cookie: tempest_session=63XC...; HttpOnly; Max-Age=86400; Path=/; SameSite=lax
GET /admin com cookie: 200 <h1>Painel</h1><p>Sessão expira em 16:55</p>
POST /logout: 303 /login
  Set-Cookie: tempest_session=""; expires=...; HttpOnly; Max-Age=0; Path=/; SameSite=lax
GET /admin com cookie revogado: 303 /login

(The labels are the Portuguese ones the run printed: no cookie, wrong login, right login, with cookie, logout, revoked cookie.)

docs.title: Piece by piece
docs.text:
1. SessionAuth.from_credentials(...) — accepts exactly one pair. Both halves are always compared, each with hmac.compare_digest over the value's SHA-256, and the results are combined with &, not and: a wrong username costs the same as a wrong password, and the message (invalid username or password) is the same for both. It takes a SecretStr, so the Settings field goes straight in. An empty credential raises ValueError at construction — an empty env var does not turn into "accept an empty form". It does not need the [auth] extra: the comparison is stdlib only, and the PasswordUtils (bcrypt) the user_model= mode uses is never built here.
  2. The session owner is uuid5(STATIC_CREDENTIAL_NAMESPACE, username) by default: stable across restarts and replicas, so session_auth.revoke_all(...) reaches every root session. Pass user_id= to pick another.
  3. login_with_credentials(...) — verifies and opens the session in one call. Wrong credentials raise UnauthorizedException without creating a session and without revoking the previous one; the route decides what to render.
  4. make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login")) — reads the cookie and resolves the session itself (with the sliding TTL, like the middleware). With no session it raises HTTPException(303, Location=/login); FastAPI's handler and the SDK's register_exception_handlers both keep the header, and the browser follows. Without on_missing, the answer stays 401.
  5. Logout — revoke(cookie) deletes the session from the store (the same cookie then redirects to the login) and delete_cookie(**settings.session_cookie_delete_kwargs()) drops the cookie in the browser.

Another credential backend

from_credentials is a shortcut. Any object with async def authenticate(self, username: str, password: str, /) -> UUID that raises UnauthorizedException on refusal satisfies the SessionAuthenticator protocol — LDAP, an upstream API — and goes into SessionAuth(authenticator=..., store=..., settings=...). Pass user_model= or authenticator=, never both. make_session_router (JSON login by e-mail) needs user_model= and refuses, at build time, a service built with authenticator=.

SessionMiddleware is a BaseHTTPMiddleware and sits in the path of every response

The middleware wraps the whole app, and Starlette's BaseHTTPMiddleware relays every chunk of the response body through an in-memory stream. Measured here (Starlette 1.6.0, direct ASGI call with an empty send, median of 7 runs): a 256 MiB StreamingResponse in 64 KiB chunks took ~4 ms with no middleware and ~64 ms with SessionMiddleware — about 15 µs per chunk, paid by every route, including the upload/download that never reads the session. In a service that streams files and uses a session on three routes, prefer the dependency with session_auth=: only the routes that declare it pay for the lookup. If the middleware is mounted anyway, the dependency reuses the session it resolved instead of resolving again.

docs.title: SessionAuth built after import
docs.text:
In the example above the SessionAuth exists at import, because Settings() runs at module level. In a service whose settings sit behind an @lru_cache — which the tests clear and rebuild per test — there is no SessionAuth to pass when the dependency is declared. Pass a factory that takes the request:

from functools import lru_cache
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse
from pydantic import SecretStr

from tempest_fastapi_sdk import (
    BaseAppSettings,
    MemorySessionStore,
    Session,
    SessionAuth,
    SessionSettings,
    make_session_dependency,
    redirect_to,
    register_exception_handlers,
)


class Settings(SessionSettings, BaseAppSettings):
    ADMIN_USERNAME: str
    ADMIN_PASSWORD: SecretStr


def get_session_auth(request: Request) -> SessionAuth:
    auth: SessionAuth = request.app.state.session_auth
    return auth


AdminSession = Annotated[
    Session,
    Depends(
        make_session_dependency(
            session_auth=get_session_auth,
            on_missing=redirect_to("/login"),
        )
    ),
]


@lru_cache
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


def create_app() -> FastAPI:
    settings = get_settings()
    app = FastAPI()
    register_exception_handlers(app)
    app.state.session_auth = SessionAuth.from_credentials(
        settings.ADMIN_USERNAME,
        settings.ADMIN_PASSWORD,
        store=MemorySessionStore(),
        settings=settings,
    )

    @app.get("/admin", response_class=HTMLResponse)
    async def admin(session: AdminSession) -> str:
        return f"<h1>Panel</h1><p>Session expires at {session.expires_at:%H:%M}</p>"

    return app
  1. get_session_auth(request) — returns the service of the app serving the request. make_session_dependency calls it per request, and only when the middleware did not resolve the session first; declaring the dependency never calls it. Two apps in one process — a test that runs get_settings.cache_clear() and builds another — each resolve against their own: one app's cookie does not open the other's panel.
  2. AdminSession — the alias lives at module level, before any SessionAuth exists, and routes use it as is.
  3. The type is Session, not Session | None. With required=True (the default) the dependency raises instead of returning None, and the signature says so: no if session is None just for the type checker. With required=False the type stays Session | None.

docs.title: Security
docs.text:
• Hash at rest: the cookie carries a 32-byte URL-safe plaintext; the store keeps only the SHA-256. A leak of the sessions table does not grant logins.
  • Session-fixation prevention: SESSION_ROTATE_ON_LOGIN=True (default) — a successful login always mints a fresh id, even if the browser already had one. Closes the "attacker plants a known cookie before login" vector.
  • Native CSRF via SameSite: SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE=lax (default) blocks cross-site POSTs. Pair with CSRFMiddleware for GET-state-changing endpoints and form submissions.
  • HttpOnly + Secure: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True + SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True by default. JavaScript cannot read (anti-XSS); the browser does not send over HTTP.
  • Sliding TTL with floor: SESSION_SLIDING=True (default) refreshes on every hit, but created_at stays put — you can force an absolute logout after N days via a job that prunes rows where created_at < now - 30d.
  • Anti-enumeration, in the body and in the timing: /auth/session/login rejects an unknown e-mail, a wrong password and an inactive account with the same UnauthorizedException and the same message (invalid email or password). And all three refusals pay one bcrypt verification: an unknown e-mail is checked against a throwaway hash (PasswordUtils.dummy_verify), and an inactive account's password is verified before is_active. Measured on this machine (bcrypt cost 12, SessionAuth.authenticate called directly, median of N=21): wrong password 153.9 ms, unknown e-mail 154.1 ms — before the fix, the unknown e-mail answered in 0.4 ms. What is not bcrypt still varies (the query, the network), and the process's first refusal for an unknown e-mail pays one extra hash to build the throwaway hash. Rate-limit attempts per IP/identifier anyway: that closes brute force, which equal timing does not.
  • Instant revocation: revoke_all(user_id) on password change / suspected compromise → logout on every device on the next request.

docs.title: Trade-offs
docs.text:
When NOT to use:

  • Public APIs for mobile — native apps care little about cookies; bearer JWT in the Authorization header is still better.
  • Stateless microservices — every replica decodes JWT without a DB hit. Sessions require a shared Redis.
  • Edge/CDN auth — Cloudflare Workers and friends validate JWT at the edge without reaching the origin. Sessions require a backend round-trip.

When to combine JWT + Session:

Possible. A web SPA uses the session cookie; mobile on the same backend uses UserAuthService.login → JWT. Both flows coexist without conflict — UserAuthService and SessionAuth speak to the same UserModel, differing only in the post-verify step (mint JWT vs mint Session).

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• A server-side session is the alternative to JWT when instant revocation is a requirement: the cookie carries only an opaque id, and the state lives in the store.
  • Four objects make the flow — SessionStore, SessionAuth, SessionMiddleware and make_session_router — mounted once in app.py.
  • Five bundled endpoints cover the whole cycle, and the middleware populates request.state.session before any router runs.
  • The cookie carries the plaintext; the store keeps only the SHA-256. Leaking the sessions table does not log anybody in.
  • Without a user table, SessionAuth.from_credentials(...) compares both halves of the credential in constant time, and make_session_dependency(session_auth=..., on_missing=redirect_to("/login")) guards an HTML route with a 303, no middleware. With the SessionAuth built after import, session_auth= takes a (request) -> SessionAuth factory, and the dependency alias comes out typed as Session.
  • settings.session_cookie_kwargs() / session_cookie_delete_kwargs() write and delete the cookie with the same attributes.
  • MemorySessionStore covers dev and tests; swap the store, not the rest of the wiring, to move to Redis or a database.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Auth flow » — bundled JWT flow (signup / activate / reset). Sessions only cover login/logout.
  • Security » — CSRFMiddleware to harden POSTs against cross-site attacks even with SameSite=lax.
  • Cache » — AsyncRedisManager and client_proxy, the right handle for a middleware store like RedisSessionStore.

docs.title: Slides, answer keys and Markdown to PDF
docs.text:
A service that teaches — or that asks a language model to put a lesson together — ends up holding text like this:

Lesson 1: Logic gates
What a gate is
A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.

And it has to deliver that as a presentation, as a PDF to print, as a presenter handout. The usual path is one parser per format, each with its own idea of what a bullet is, and the PowerPoint ends up saying one thing and the PDF another.

tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides reads the text once, into a typed object, and every format comes out of that same object: HTML, PDF, PPTX, DOCX and Markdown. The same holds for answer keys (numbered questions and answers) and for free-form Markdown turned into PDF, with the stylesheet you choose — ABNT included.

Required extra

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[slides]"
Brings in weasyprint, jinja2, python-pptx, python-docx and markdown. The PDF uses the same engine as PDF generation, so it needs the same system libraries — read Deployment. The parser and the schemas import without the extra: each engine loads on first use.

docs.title: Your first deck
docs.text:
# scripts/lesson.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideRenderer, parse_slides

SOURCE: str = """Lesson 1: Logic gates
What a gate is
A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.
Notes: ask the class for a real-world example first.
The gates you will meet
- NOT gate: inverts its only input, so 0 becomes 1.
- AND gate: outputs 1 only when every input is 1.
- OR gate: outputs 1 when at least one input is 1.
Conclusion
Every digital circuit is built from a handful of gates.
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Parse the lesson and write it as HTML and PowerPoint."""
    deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(SOURCE)
    renderer = SlideRenderer()
    Path("lesson.html").write_text(renderer.html(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.pptx").write_bytes(await renderer.pptx(deck))
    for slide in deck.slides:
        print(slide.slide_number, slide.kind, slide.title)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Run it and you get:

1 lesson_title Logic gates
2 content What a gate is
3 bullets The gates you will meet
4 conclusion Conclusion

Four slides, and every line of the text landed somewhere:

  • Lesson 1: Logic gates opens a lesson and becomes its cover (lesson_title). The deck title, when you pass no deck_title=, is the first lesson's.
  • A short line (4 to 90 characters), capitalized, with no closing punctuation (What a gate is) opens a section; a single word needs at least 8 characters, so a stray Yes does not open one. The section title is the slide title.
  • A paragraph under a section becomes a content slide (content).
  • Term: description becomes a bullet, and the bullets of a section share one slide (bullets). The leading dash is optional.
  • Notes: is a speaker note, attached to the paragraph or bullet right above it.
  • A section whose title contains conclusion becomes a conclusion slide.

parse_slides is synchronous: it is pure CPU over a string. The renderers that produce binaries (pdf, pptx, docx) are async and run in a worker thread, so a long deck does not block the event loop.

What does not become a bullet

A sentence with a colon in the middle would pass as a bullet if the rule were just "has a :". So the term must start with a capital, have at most 8 words and 80 characters, carry no .,!?; and no unbalanced parenthesis, and contain no sentence verb (is, are, means, …); the description needs at least 20 characters. The result is: 42 after the second pass. stays a paragraph — without the full stop, the same line on its own becomes a section title.

docs.title: Slides that do not overflow
docs.text:
A section with a lot of content becomes more than one slide, instead of one slide in a tiny font:

  • More than 6 bullets open another slide with the same title. Measured with 8 bullets in a section: one slide with 6 and another with 2.
  • Paragraphs group up to 700 characters per slide. A paragraph is never cut: one longer than the limit sits alone on its own slide.

docs.title: The vocabulary: text in your service's language
docs.text:
The markers the parser reads and the labels the renderers print are not fixed. They live in a SlideVocabulary, English by default. A service that writes Portuguese passes its own:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideVocabulary, parse_slides

PT_BR: SlideVocabulary = SlideVocabulary(
    lesson_pattern=r"^Aula\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$",
    notes_pattern=r"^(?:Notas|Nota)\s*:\s*(.+)$",
    conclusion_marker="conclus",
    sentence_verbs=(" é ", " são ", " foi ", " foram ", " será ", " tem ", " significa "),
    default_lesson_title="Conteúdo",
    lesson_label="Aula {index}",
    conclusion_label="Conclusão",
    handout_subtitle="Roteiro do apresentador",
    handout_cover_note="Slide de capa.",
    notes_heading="Notas do apresentador",
    language="pt-BR",
)

TEXT: str = """Aula 1: Portas lógicas
O que é uma porta
Uma porta lógica recebe entradas binárias e devolve uma única saída binária.
Notas: peça um exemplo do dia a dia antes de seguir.
As portas básicas
- Porta NOT: inverte a única entrada, então 0 vira 1.
- Porta AND: devolve 1 só quando todas as entradas valem 1.
Conclusão
Todo circuito digital é montado a partir de poucas portas.
"""

deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(TEXT, vocabulary=PT_BR)
for slide in deck.slides:
    print(slide.slide_number, slide.kind, slide.title, slide.subtitle)

1 lesson_title Portas lógicas Aula 1
2 content O que é uma porta None
3 bullets As portas básicas None
4 conclusion Conclusão None

Two parts, with different jobs:

  • Markers (lesson_pattern, notes_pattern, conclusion_marker, sentence_verbs, ignored_lines) decide how the text is read. Both patterns are regular expressions, matched case-insensitively; lesson_pattern needs two groups (number and title), notes_pattern one (the note text). conclusion_marker="conclus" matches Conclusão and Conclusões.
  • Labels (lesson_label, conclusion_label, handout_subtitle, notes_heading, slide_label, language, …) decide what is printed. {index} in lesson_label becomes the lesson number; language goes into <html lang>.

Without the vocabulary, the same Portuguese text comes out wrong — and with no error at all, because nothing in it is invalid, it just is not what you meant. Measured with the English default over the TEXT above:

[('lesson_title', 'Content'), ('content', 'O que é uma porta'),
 ('bullets', 'O que é uma porta'), ('bullets', 'As portas básicas'),
 ('content', 'Conclusão')]

Aula 1: opened no lesson (the cover is the implicit Content one), the Notas: line became a bullet and the conclusion became an ordinary slide.

Pass the same vocabulary to the renderer

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideRenderer, SlideVocabulary

PT_BR: SlideVocabulary = SlideVocabulary(
    lesson_pattern=r"^Aula\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$",
    lesson_label="Aula {index}",
    conclusion_label="Conclusão",
)
renderer: SlideRenderer = SlideRenderer(vocabulary=PT_BR)
The parser uses the markers; the renderer, the labels. A SlideRenderer() without a vocabulary prints Lesson 1 and Conclusion on a deck read in Portuguese. Build the vocabulary once, as a service constant, and hand it to both.

An invalid pattern fails at construction, far from the first user text, and the message names the field:

ValueError: lesson_pattern needs two groups: number and title
ValueError: lesson_pattern is not a valid regular expression: missing ), unterminated subpattern at position 0

docs.title: Every format
docs.text:
One SlideDeck, five outputs:

Format Call Speaker notes Theme HTML renderer.html(deck, theme=...) — sync, str no yes PDF await renderer.pdf(deck, theme=...) — bytes no yes PPTX await renderer.pptx(deck, theme=...) — bytes in the notes pane yes DOCX await renderer.docx(deck) — bytes a block per page no Markdown renderer.markdown(deck) — sync, str a Note: block no 
# scripts/formats.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import SlideDeck, SlideRenderer, SlideThemeEnum, parse_slides


async def main() -> None:
    """Write one deck in every format."""
    deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(Path("lesson.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    renderer = SlideRenderer(max_concurrent=2)
    Path("lesson.html").write_text(renderer.html(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.md").write_text(renderer.markdown(deck), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("lesson.pdf").write_bytes(await renderer.pdf(deck, theme=SlideThemeEnum.DARK))
    Path("lesson.pptx").write_bytes(await renderer.pptx(deck, theme=SlideThemeEnum.DARK))
    Path("handout.docx").write_bytes(await renderer.docx(deck))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

What each one delivers, measured on the four-slide deck from the start:

  • HTML is a single document, CSS inlined and nothing fetched — it opens offline and fits an <iframe srcdoc> preview. Every value is escaped.
  • PDF is that same HTML laid out: one page per slide, 960 × 540 pt (1280 × 720 px). The four slides gave four pages.
  • PPTX comes out 16:9 (13.33 × 7.5 inches), one slide per slide, with the speaker note in the notes pane — slide 2 carried ask the class for a real-world example first., the others none.
  • DOCX is the presenter handout: a cover with the title and Presenter handout (the handout_subtitle), then one page per slide with the lesson label, the title, the content and a Speaker notes block — holding the note, or blank lines to write on by hand. The footer reads Logic gates · Slide 1 / 4.
  • Markdown is reveal.js flavoured, slides separated by ---:
<!-- Deck: Logic gates -->
<!-- Total slides: 4 -->

<small>Lesson 1</small>

# Logic gates

---

<small>Lesson 1</small>

## What a gate is

A logic gate maps binary inputs to a single binary output.

Note:
ask the class for a real-world example first.

SlideThemeEnum.DEFAULT is dark text on white with blue accents; SlideThemeEnum.DARK, light text on a slate background. max_concurrent caps how many PDF, PPTX and DOCX renders run at once on that renderer — each is CPU in a worker thread, and without a ceiling a burst of requests takes every core.

docs.title: Answer keys
docs.text:
An answer key is another text format — title, parts, numbered questions and answers — with its own parser and renderer:

# scripts/answer_key.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import (
    AnswerKey,
    AnswerKeyRenderer,
    AnswerKeyVocabulary,
    parse_answer_key,
)

PT_BR: AnswerKeyVocabulary = AnswerKeyVocabulary(
    title_prefixes=("título:",),
    subtitle_prefixes=("subtítulo:",),
    answer_pattern=r"^(?:R|Resposta)\s*[:.]\s*(.*)$",
    default_title="Gabarito",
    answer_label="Resposta:",
    footer="Gabarito de uso do professor",
    language="pt-BR",
)

TEXT: str = """Título: Portas lógicas — gabarito
Subtítulo: Turma 3B, 2026

Parte 1: Conceitos
1. O que faz uma porta NOT?
R: Inverte a entrada: 0 vira 1 e 1 vira 0.
2. Quando a porta AND devolve 1?
Resposta:
Só quando <b>todas</b> as entradas valem 1.

Parte 2: Aplicação
1) Qual porta implementa "pelo menos um"?
R: A porta OR.
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Parse the answer key and write it as Markdown, PDF and DOCX."""
    answer_key: AnswerKey = parse_answer_key(TEXT, vocabulary=PT_BR)
    renderer = AnswerKeyRenderer(vocabulary=PT_BR)
    print(answer_key.title, "|", answer_key.subtitle, "|", answer_key.total_items)
    Path("answer_key.md").write_text(renderer.markdown(answer_key), encoding="utf-8")
    Path("answer_key.pdf").write_bytes(await renderer.pdf(answer_key))
    Path("answer_key.docx").write_bytes(await renderer.docx(answer_key))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Portas lógicas — gabarito | Turma 3B, 2026 | 3

And answer_key.md:

# Portas lógicas — gabarito

_Turma 3B, 2026_

## Parte 1: Conceitos

**1. O que faz uma porta NOT?**

> Resposta: Inverte a entrada: 0 vira 1 e 1 vira 0.

**2. Quando a porta AND devolve 1?**

> Resposta: Só quando todas as entradas valem 1.

## Parte 2: Aplicação

**1) Qual porta implementa "pelo menos um"?**

> Resposta: A porta OR.

The reading rules:

  • 1. or 1) opens a question, and the numbering stays in its text.
  • The answer marker (answer_pattern) opens the answer, which runs until the next question or part. The answer can start on the same line (R: A porta OR.) or on the next one (Resposta: alone) — several lines are joined with spaces.
  • A capitalized line that does not end like a sentence opens a part — but only outside a question or after a blank line, so the second line of a wrapped question stays in the question.
  • title= and subtitle= on the call override the lines in the text.

AnswerKeyRenderer has html, markdown (sync), pdf (A4) and docx (async). footer prints one line at the end of the HTML and the PDF; None, the default, prints none.

HTML tags in the text are stripped, in every format

Answer keys written by a model sometimes arrive with <b>. The schema keeps the text as it came ('Só quando <b>todas</b> as entradas valem 1.'), and every renderer strips the tag before writing — look at the Markdown above. The HTML then still escapes whatever is left. An answer <script>alert(1)</script>yes comes out alert(1)yes, as text, in all four formats.

docs.title: Markdown to PDF
docs.text:
The third job has no parser: free-form Markdown — a report, a thesis, a document a model wrote — laid out as PDF. The stylesheet is a parameter:

# scripts/thesis.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS, MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

TEXT: str = """# Introdução

Este trabalho descreve as portas lógicas.

| Porta | Saída |
| --- | --- |
| NOT | inverte |
"""


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a Markdown document with the ABNT stylesheet."""
    renderer = MarkdownPdfRenderer(stylesheet=ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS)
    document: MarkdownPdf = await renderer.render(TEXT, title="TCC")
    Path(f"{document.title}.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

render returns a MarkdownPdf with content (the bytes) and title — yours, or default_title ("Document") when you pass none. Three possible stylesheets:

  • DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_CSS (the default): A4, sans-serif, page numbers.
  • ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS: the ABNT NBR 14724 layout for Brazilian academic work — A4, 3 cm top and left margins and 2 cm bottom and right, Times New Roman 12 pt, 1.5 line spacing, justified text, 1.25 cm first-line indent, first-level headings in upper case. Measured: # Introdução comes out INTRODUÇÃO in the PDF text with this sheet, and Introdução with the default.
  • Yours: any CSS the service maintains, passed as stylesheet=.

The Markdown enables tables, fenced code blocks, footnotes, a table of contents (toc) and attr_list. Code is coloured when Pygments is installed and left plain when it is not.

Raw text fetches nothing

Markdown from a user is a URL from a user: ![x](file:///etc/passwd) would read the server's disk, and ![x](http://169.254.169.254/...) would make a request from inside your network. render goes through the same asset policy as PDF generation, with nothing allowed: both raise AssetRefused (422, PDF_ASSET_REFUSED) and no PDF comes out. data: still passes, because it carries its own bytes — measured with an SVG image as data:image/svg+xml;base64,....

docs.title: Markdown with images: the .zip archive
docs.text:
A document with an image has to bring the image along. render_archive takes a .zip holding the Markdown and the files it references:

# scripts/zipped_report.py

import asyncio
import io
import zipfile
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

SQUARE: str = (
    '<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="10" height="10">'
    '<rect width="10" height="10"/></svg>'
)


def build_archive() -> bytes:
    """Zip one Markdown file and the image it references."""
    buffer = io.BytesIO()
    with zipfile.ZipFile(buffer, "w", compression=zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as archive:
        archive.writestr("report/report.md", "# With an image\n\n![square](img/q.svg)\n")
        archive.writestr("report/img/q.svg", SQUARE)
    return buffer.getvalue()


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a zipped Markdown document with its image."""
    document: MarkdownPdf = await MarkdownPdfRenderer().render_archive(build_archive())
    print(document.title)
    Path(f"{document.title}.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

It prints report: without title=, the title is the Markdown file's name without its extension. How the file is chosen and what it may read:

  • The first .md in path order is the document. With a.md and b.md in the same zip, a.md wins.
  • Relative paths resolve from the Markdown's directory — img/q.svg above is report/img/q.svg.
  • Nothing outside the extracted zip can be read. ![x](../../../../etc/passwd) raises AssetRefused: that render's asset policy allows only the extraction directory.

And the archive is checked before a single byte reaches the disk, from the zip's central directory. Each refusal is a MarkdownArchiveError (422, MARKDOWN_ARCHIVE_INVALID) with details["reason"]:

reason When not_a_zip the bytes are not a zip unsafe_member an entry would land outside the extraction directory (../outside.md, /abs.md) too_many_members more entries than max_archive_members (default DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_MEMBERS, 500) too_large the declared uncompressed size exceeds max_archive_bytes (default DEFAULT_MAX_ARCHIVE_BYTES, 50 MiB) no_markdown no .md in the zip not_utf8 the Markdown is not UTF-8

too_large is what holds a zip bomb back: measured, a 221-byte zip declaring 100,000 uncompressed bytes is refused with max_archive_bytes=50_000, without extracting. The refused entry's name never goes into the error — it is text chosen by whoever sent the file.

docs.title: Mermaid diagrams
docs.text:
WeasyPrint runs no JavaScript, so a ```mermaid block would reach the PDF as code. With render_mermaid=True, each block is drawn in headless Chromium before layout:

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[slides,slides-mermaid]"
uv run playwright install chromium

# scripts/flow.py

import asyncio
from pathlib import Path

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import MarkdownPdf, MarkdownPdfRenderer

FENCE: str = "`" * 3
TEXT: str = f"# Flow\n\n{FENCE}mermaid\ngraph TD\n  Order-->Payment\n{FENCE}\n"


async def main() -> None:
    """Render a document whose Mermaid block becomes a drawing."""
    renderer = MarkdownPdfRenderer(
        mermaid_timeout=15.0,
        mermaid_error_message="This diagram could not be drawn.",
    )
    document: MarkdownPdf = await renderer.render(TEXT, render_mermaid=True)
    Path("flow.pdf").write_bytes(document.content)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())

Measured with Chromium installed: the valid diagram becomes inline SVG (its node labels show up in the PDF text), and an invalid block in the same document becomes a box with the message and the escaped source. One browser draws every block of the document.

A failing diagram never takes the document down. Without Playwright, without Chromium (measured with Playwright installed and the browser missing), with invalid syntax or past the deadline (measured with mermaid_timeout=0.001), the block becomes the .mermaid-error box and the PDF still comes out. Both stylesheets the SDK ships style that box and .mermaid-diagram; a sheet of your own that starts from either keeps diagrams inside the page.

The Mermaid script comes from the internet

The Chromium page loads mermaid@10.9.8 from jsDelivr on every render. That request is the browser's, outside the PDF's asset policy — the server needs egress to cdn.jsdelivr.net. Measured by pointing the script at an address that does not answer: the diagram becomes an error box. The version is pinned, so a new Mermaid release does not change your PDF without notice.

Why it is a separate extra, and out of [all]

Playwright asks for a browser download (playwright install chromium) that a service rendering plain decks should not carry. That is why [slides-mermaid] is neither in [slides] nor in [all].

docs.title: Errors
docs.text:
They are all AppExceptions: let them propagate from the route and the client gets the SDK envelope, with code. With register_exception_handlers(app, catalog=default_message_catalog()), the sentence follows Accept-Language — entries exist in pt-BR and en-US.

Exception Status code When SlideSourceEmptyError 422 SLIDES_SOURCE_EMPTY empty or whitespace text (parser, render, empty Markdown in a zip) SlideSourceTooLargeError 413 SLIDES_SOURCE_TOO_LARGE text longer than max_chars (default DEFAULT_MAX_SOURCE_CHARS, 200,000); details={"limit": n} MarkdownArchiveError 422 MARKDOWN_ARCHIVE_INVALID archive refused; details={"reason": ...}, table above AssetRefused 422 PDF_ASSET_REFUSED the Markdown referenced something not allowed; details={"refused_count": n}

max_chars=None on parse_slides, parse_answer_key or the MarkdownPdfRenderer disables the limit. None of these errors echoes the refused text. Elsewhere in the SDK, AssetRefused lists the refused URLs under details["refused"]; raised from Markdown, it carries only details={"refused_count": n} — the URL is the user's own text echoed back and, inside a zip, would disclose the server's temporary directory path. WeasyPrint stops at the first refusal, so n is 1 in practice: measured with two refused references in one document, {"refused_count": 1}.

Without the extra it is an ImportError, not an envelope

The parser and the schemas import with no dependency, but the first render without [slides] installed raises ImportError — not an AppException — and the route answers 500. The message names the extra, the same for HTML, PDF, PPTX, DOCX and Markdown to PDF: Rendering slides needs python-pptx. Install the extra: pip install "tempest-fastapi-sdk[slides]" (with jinja2, weasyprint, python-docx or markdown in place of the missing package). It is an installation defect, not an input one: install the extra rather than handling the error in the route.

docs.title: Serving over HTTP
docs.text:
# src/api/app.py

from fastapi import FastAPI, Response
from pydantic import Field

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.api import register_exception_handlers
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.exceptions import default_message_catalog
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.pdf import PDF_MEDIA_TYPE
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.schemas import BaseSchema
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.slides import (
    ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS,
    MarkdownPdf,
    MarkdownPdfRenderer,
    SlideDeck,
    SlideRenderer,
    SlideThemeEnum,
    SlideVocabulary,
    parse_slides,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import PPTX_MEDIA_TYPE, build_content_disposition

PT_BR: SlideVocabulary = SlideVocabulary(
    lesson_pattern=r"^Aula\s+(\d+)\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*$",
    notes_pattern=r"^(?:Notas|Nota)\s*:\s*(.+)$",
    conclusion_marker="conclus",
    lesson_label="Aula {index}",
    conclusion_label="Conclusão",
    language="pt-BR",
)

slides: SlideRenderer = SlideRenderer(vocabulary=PT_BR)
markdown_pdf: MarkdownPdfRenderer = MarkdownPdfRenderer(stylesheet=ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS)


class SlideSourceSchema(BaseSchema):
    """The structured text of a lesson."""

    text: str = Field(title="Text", description="Source in the lesson/section/bullet format.")
    theme: SlideThemeEnum = Field(default=SlideThemeEnum.DEFAULT, title="Theme")


class MarkdownSourceSchema(BaseSchema):
    """A Markdown document."""

    text: str = Field(title="Text", description="The document's Markdown.")
    title: str | None = Field(default=None, title="Title")


app = FastAPI()
register_exception_handlers(app, catalog=default_message_catalog())


@app.post("/api/slides/pptx")
async def slides_pptx(payload: SlideSourceSchema) -> Response:
    """Return the lesson as a PowerPoint presentation."""
    deck: SlideDeck = parse_slides(payload.text, vocabulary=PT_BR)
    content: bytes = await slides.pptx(deck, theme=SlideThemeEnum(payload.theme))
    return Response(
        content=content,
        media_type=PPTX_MEDIA_TYPE,
        headers={"Content-Disposition": build_content_disposition(f"{deck.title}.pptx")},
    )


@app.post("/api/markdown/pdf")
async def markdown_to_pdf(payload: MarkdownSourceSchema) -> Response:
    """Return the Markdown laid out as an ABNT PDF."""
    document: MarkdownPdf = await markdown_pdf.render(payload.text, title=payload.title)
    return Response(
        content=document.content,
        media_type=PDF_MEDIA_TYPE,
        headers={"Content-Disposition": build_content_disposition(f"{document.title}.pdf")},
    )

Measured with TestClient:

POST /api/slides/pptx {"text": "Aula 1: Portas lógicas\n..."}
200  application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation
     attachment; filename="Portas lgicas.pptx"; filename*=UTF-8''Portas%20l%C3%B3gicas.pptx

POST /api/slides/pptx {"text": "   "}   (Accept-Language: en-US)
422  {"detail": "The source text is empty", "code": "SLIDES_SOURCE_EMPTY", "details": {}}

POST /api/slides/pptx {"text": "   "}   (Accept-Language: pt-BR)
422  {"detail": "O texto de origem está vazio", "code": "SLIDES_SOURCE_EMPTY", "details": {}}

POST /api/markdown/pdf {"text": "# Introdução\n\nTexto.", "title": "TCC"}
200  application/pdf
     attachment; filename="TCC.pdf"; filename*=UTF-8''TCC.pdf

Piece by piece:

  • The renderers are built once, at module level: they hold the vocabulary, the stylesheet and the max_concurrent semaphore, which only limits anything when it is shared across requests.
  • PPTX_MEDIA_TYPE / DOCX_MEDIA_TYPE come from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils, and PDF_MEDIA_TYPE from tempest_fastapi_sdk.pdf. A python:slim image has no /etc/mime.types, and guessing through mimetypes serves the .pptx as application/octet-stream in production only.
  • build_content_disposition builds the header from the title, which is user text: it drops control characters, so a line break cannot split the response, and sends the UTF-8 name in filename*.
  • No try/except. The parser's error already is the right response.

The route adds no auth or limit on its own

Producing PPTX and PDF is CPU, and the client holds the connection until it finishes. Put your service's authentication and rate limit on these routes — a document route without them is the one that ends up public.

Coming from Leviathan's slide-generator

The module was ported from that service. What changed on the way:

  • Escaping in the HTML. The answer-key template marked question and answer | safe, and a <script> in the text ran inside whatever page embedded the preview. Here everything is escaped, and tags are stripped first.
  • Asset policy. Markdown to PDF used WeasyPrint's default fetcher, which read file:// from the host and requested any http://. Now raw text fetches nothing and an archive reads only what it carried.
  • Archive bounds. Entry count and uncompressed size are checked before extracting.
  • ABNT margins. The original had margin: 3cm 2cm — 3 cm at the top and bottom, 2 cm on the sides. NBR 14724 asks for 3 cm top and left, 2 cm bottom and right, which is what ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS applies.
  • Pinned Mermaid. The original loaded mermaid@10 (a floating version) and opened one browser per diagram; here it is mermaid@10.9.8 and one browser per document.
  • Vocabulary. The markers were pt-BR only and hard-coded; now they are SlideVocabulary / AnswerKeyVocabulary, with English defaults.

docs.title: Recap
docs.text:
• parse_slides reads the text into a SlideDeck; SlideRenderer writes HTML and Markdown (sync) and PDF, PPTX and DOCX (async, in a worker thread, with max_concurrent).
  • Markers and labels live in SlideVocabulary — English by default. Portuguese text asks for your own, passed to the parser and the renderer.
  • A large section becomes more than one slide: 6 bullets or 700 characters of paragraph per slide, never cutting a paragraph.
  • parse_answer_key + AnswerKeyRenderer do the same for answer keys; HTML tags in the text are stripped in every format.
  • MarkdownPdfRenderer lays Markdown out with the sheet you pass — DEFAULT_MARKDOWN_CSS, ABNT_MARKDOWN_CSS or your own.
  • Raw text fetches no URL; an archive reads only what it carried and is checked before extraction.
  • Mermaid needs [slides-mermaid] + playwright install chromium; a failing diagram becomes an error box, and the PDF still comes out.
  • Errors are AppExceptions with a code — let them propagate.

Next: PDF generation for typed documents (receipt, quote, report), or Spreadsheets (.xlsx) when the recipient needs to work with the numbers.

docs.title: Spreadsheets (.xlsx)
docs.text:
A PDF is what you send when the numbers are final. A spreadsheet is what you send when the recipient has to work with them: sort, filter, re-total, check line by line. A budget, a price table, a reconciliation, a report export — all of it arrives as .xlsx, and almost always gets assembled with openpyxl by hand.

Assembling by hand costs three things, always the same three:

  • Row arithmetic. Every write is a (row, column) pair you track. Insert a line near the top and every constant below it shifts.
  • Styling that drifts. Four assignments (font, fill, alignment, border) repeated on every cell, and the thousandth row stops matching the first.
  • The wrong number format. "#,##0.00" looks right and is a trap: Excel resolves that mask with the locale of whoever opens the file. The workbook you built in São Paulo shows 1.234,56 at home and 1,234.56 on a colleague's en-US laptop. The value is the same; the document is wrong, and nobody notices.

tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet fixes all three: a row cursor, columns declared once, and masks pinned to pt-BR.

And the other way round, to read a spreadsheet — the .xlsx a user uploads, or the sheet someone keeps in Google — see Reading an .xlsx file and Reading a Google Sheet.

Extra required

uv add "tempest-fastapi-sdk[spreadsheet]"
Brings openpyxl. The engine is imported at first use, so importing the module — and defining your project's columns and theme — works without it.

docs.title: Your first spreadsheet
docs.text:
# scripts/budget.py

from decimal import Decimal

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT,
    Column,
    SheetWriter,
    new_workbook,
    workbook_to_bytes,
)


def main() -> None:
    """Write a two-item price table to disk."""
    workbook = new_workbook("Orçamento")
    writer = SheetWriter(
        workbook["Orçamento"],
        columns=[
            Column("Item", width=48, wrap=True),
            Column("Qty.", width=12, horizontal="center"),
            Column("Unit price", width=20, number_format=BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT),
        ],
    )

    writer.title_block(["PREFEITURA MUNICIPAL DE EXEMPLO", "Pregão 1/2026"])
    writer.header_row()
    writer.write_row(["Installation service", 2, Decimal("2930.00")])
    writer.write_row(["Monthly maintenance", 12, Decimal("450.50")])
    writer.total_row(["Total", None, Decimal("11266.00")])
    writer.apply_widths()

    with open("budget.xlsx", "wb") as handle:
        handle.write(workbook_to_bytes(workbook))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

uv run python scripts/budget.py

Open the file: the title centred across all three columns, a navy header with white text, amounts right-aligned as R$ 2.930,00, and the total row picked out in amber.

What you did not write

No (row, column) pairs. No Font, PatternFill or Border. No mask repeated per cell. The cursor belongs to SheetWriter, the styling comes from the theme, the format comes from the column.

docs.title: new_workbook and the ghost sheet
docs.text:
openpyxl always creates a workbook with one sheet called Sheet. Forgetting to remove it ships a document with a stray empty tab — the kind of detail that gives away that a file was generated by a script.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import new_workbook

workbook = new_workbook("Analysis", "Budget", "Feasibility")
print(workbook.sheetnames)  # ['Analysis', 'Budget', 'Feasibility']

With no arguments the default sheet is kept — handy when you name it later.

docs.title: Columns: declare them once
docs.text:
Column specifies the column, not a cell. It applies to every body row, which is why the format cannot drift between the first row and the thousandth.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT,
    BR_PERCENT_FORMAT,
    Column,
    TEXT_FORMAT,
)

columns = [
    Column("Process", width=18, number_format=TEXT_FORMAT),
    Column("Description", width=52, wrap=True),
    Column("Discount", width=12, number_format=BR_PERCENT_FORMAT),
    Column("Amount", width=18, number_format=BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT),
]
Field What it does title Header text, used by header_row() width Width in characters; None keeps the default (which truncates) number_format Mask applied to every body cell horizontal "left", "center", "right"; None lets Excel decide wrap Text wrapping — on for the description, off elsewhere

wrap=True on a short column makes rows tall for nothing

Row height follows the tallest cell. A two-word column with wrapping on stretches the whole row and buys nothing.

docs.title: Numbers, not strings
docs.text:
The temptation is to format in Python and write the finished text. The cell then holds "R$ 2.930,00", which is text: the recipient cannot sum, sort or filter on it, and Excel's SUM returns zero for the whole column.

from decimal import Decimal

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT,
    Column,
    SheetWriter,
    new_workbook,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import format_currency_br

workbook = new_workbook("Budget")
writer = SheetWriter(
    workbook["Budget"],
    columns=[
        Column("Item", width=48),
        Column("Amount", width=18, number_format=BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT),
    ],
)

# ❌ becomes text: no sum, no sorting, no filtering
writer.write_row(["Service", format_currency_br(Decimal("2930.00"))])

# ✅ write the number and let the mask present it
writer.write_row(["Service", Decimal("2930.00")])

On screen both rows read the same R$ 2.930,00; in the file only the second one is a number.

Use format_currency_br for prose

tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils.format_currency_br exists for text headed to a PDF, an e-mail or a page. A spreadsheet cell takes a number.

docs.title: Brazilian formats
docs.text:
Constant Renders For BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT R$ 1.234,56 Money with the symbol BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT_NO_SYMBOL 1.234,56 Column whose header already says (R$) BR_QUANTITY_FORMAT 1.234,56 Non-monetary quantity BR_INTEGER_FORMAT 1.234 Counts, whole numbers BR_PERCENT_FORMAT 30,00% Percentages BR_DATE_FORMAT 14/08/2026 Dates BR_DATETIME_FORMAT 14/08/2026 19:30 Date and time TEXT_FORMAT exactly what you wrote An identifier that looks numeric

What makes these masks work is the pt-BR language code, [$-416], at the start of every one of them — currency, percent and dates included. It pins the dot as thousands separator, the comma as decimal and the slash as date separator inside the file, so the document does not depend on the machine of whoever opens it.

Measured by opening the same workbook in LibreOffice 7.4 headless under three locales:

Constant en-US de-DE pt-BR BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT R$ 1.234,56 R$ 1.234,56 R$ 1.234,56 BR_PERCENT_FORMAT 30,00% 30,00% 30,00% BR_DATE_FORMAT 14/08/2026 14/08/2026 14/08/2026 0.00% (no code) 30.00% 30,00 % 30,00% DD/MM/YYYY (no code) 14/08/2026 14.08.2026 14/08/2026 [$R$-416] #,##0.00 R$ 1,234.56 R$ 1.234,56 R$ 1.234,56

The date slash is not a literal

In a date mask, / is the locale's date separator, not the slash character. Without [$-416], a German reader sees 14.08.2026.

Why the currency mask does not use [$R$-416]

[$R$-416] is the "currency symbol with language" form and looks like the natural way to write reais. It does not pin the separators: the last row of the table shows LibreOffice reading 1,234.56 under en-US. So BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT is [$-416]"R$ "#,##0.00 — the language code first and the symbol as a quoted literal. Excel was not measured.

A percent cell holds the ratio, not the percentage

Excel multiplies by 100 itself. A cell with BR_PERCENT_FORMAT must receive Decimal("0.30"), not 30 — writing 30 displays 3000,00%. It reads like a typo but it is a unit error.

TEXT_FORMAT saves leading zeros

A CPF, a process number (0001/2026), a bank branch. Without it Excel normalizes them to numbers and the zeros are gone for good.

docs.title: The rows a document has
docs.text:
from decimal import Decimal

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT,
    Column,
    SheetWriter,
    new_workbook,
)

workbook = new_workbook("Budget")
writer = SheetWriter(
    workbook["Budget"],
    columns=[
        Column("Item", width=48),
        Column("Qty.", width=10, horizontal="center"),
        Column("Amount", width=18, number_format=BR_CURRENCY_FORMAT),
    ],
)

writer.title_block(["AGENCY", "Pregão 1/2026", "Annex I"])  # merged, centred
first_item_row = writer.header_row()                        # table header
writer.group_row(["GROUP 1 — HANDICRAFT"])                  # in-table subheading
writer.write_row(["Item", 2, Decimal("10.00")])             # body
writer.total_row(["Total", None, Decimal("20.00")])         # emphasis
writer.blank_rows(2)                                        # breathing room

All of them return the next free row — that is how first_item_row got the position of the first item without anyone counting lines.

A None cell in the middle of a row is still styled: that is how a total row skips the middle columns without losing its fill.

docs.title: Live formulas
docs.text:
Wrap the expression in Formula and it becomes a real formula:

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    Column,
    Formula,
    SheetWriter,
    new_workbook,
)

workbook = new_workbook("Budget")
writer = SheetWriter(workbook["Budget"], [Column("Item"), Column("Amount")])
writer.write_row(["Checked sum", Formula("=SUM(B5:B24)")])

Worth it for closing checks. An auditor who edits a value sees the number react, instead of reading a constant that was true only at generation time.

A plain str is always text, even when it starts with =. A cell's value usually comes from a user, a database row or an import, and openpyxl would turn =HYPERLINK("https://...") typed into a name field into a live link in every exported sheet. Through SheetWriter the cell is stored as inlineStr in the XML and shows exactly what was passed. Formula("SUM(B5:B24)"), without the =, raises ValueError.

Only = needs handling in .xlsx

In CSV, +, -, @, tab and CR also open a formula, and the admin's CSV export neutralizes them. In .xlsx, openpyxl treats only a str starting with = as a formula; the others are written as text, stored in the XML as a string with no formula element (measured on openpyxl 3.1.5). That is why SheetWriter leaves the value untouched — no leading apostrophe.

docs.title: Theme
docs.text:
SheetStyle is plain data — hex colours, integer sizes, no openpyxl objects. That is what makes your project's theme definable, testable and comparable without the extra installed.

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import SheetStyle, SheetWriter

CORPORATE = SheetStyle(
    header_background="0B3D2E",
    header_foreground="FFFFFF",
    group_background="D6E9DF",
    total_background="F3E5AB",
    border_color="C0C0C0",
    font_name="Calibri",
)

Pass it to the constructor: SheetWriter(sheet, columns, style=CORPORATE).

Colours follow the openpyxl convention

RRGGBB or AARRGGBB, without a leading #.

docs.title: Serving it as a download
docs.text:
None of this touches disk: workbook_to_bytes returns the bytes and the handler ships them.

from fastapi import APIRouter
from fastapi.responses import Response

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import (
    XLSX_MEDIA_TYPE,
    new_workbook,
    workbook_to_bytes,
)
from tempest_fastapi_sdk.utils import build_content_disposition

router = APIRouter()


@router.get("/budgets/{budget_id}/spreadsheet")
async def download_budget(budget_id: int) -> Response:
    """Stream the budget as an .xlsx download."""
    workbook = new_workbook("Orçamento")
    return Response(
        content=workbook_to_bytes(workbook),
        media_type=XLSX_MEDIA_TYPE,
        headers={
            "Content-Disposition": build_content_disposition(
                f"budget-{budget_id}.xlsx",
            ),
        },
    )

XLSX_MEDIA_TYPE comes ready from the SDK. Do not trust a guess from the extension: Python's built-in table has no .xlsx, and mimetypes only gets it right when the host has /etc/mime.types — python:3.13-slim does not (details in Downloads).

No temp file, no race

Two concurrent requests would write the same temporary path. In memory the problem does not exist — and there is nothing to clean up.

docs.title: Reading a Google Sheet
docs.text:
So far the road went from code to spreadsheet. The opposite shows up early in every project: someone keeps the price list or the stock in a Google Sheet, and the service has to read it.

The hand-written version usually goes like this: cut the link at /edit, fish the gid out of the fragment, build /export?format=csv&gid=... and hand it to pandas. It works — until the day it does not, for reasons that do not show when reading the code:

  • #gid= is a fragment. The browser never sends it to the server; pass the whole link along and the chosen tab is lost on the way.
  • The export answers with a redirect. docs.google.com replies 307 to a *.googleusercontent.com host. An httpx.AsyncClient built without follow_redirects hands you that 307 as if it were the response.
  • Errors do not look like errors. An ID that does not exist answers 404 with an HTML page; a gid that is no tab at all answers 400, also as HTML. Skip the Content-Type check and you end up parsing HTML as data.

read_google_sheet_as handles all three and validates each row into a Pydantic model on top.

No extra

Reading uses only httpx (a base dependency) and the standard library's csv module. It needs neither [spreadsheet] nor openpyxl.

docs.title: The code
docs.text:
The sample sheet is public and has three columns: item, valor (price) and tamanho (size).

# scripts/stock.py

import asyncio

from pydantic import BaseModel

from tempest_fastapi_sdk.spreadsheet import read_google_sheet_as

SHEET_URL: str = (
    "https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/"
    "1h0ATstw2f6ryXvbwV-DW6zwsBRIF-2k5zHcm2uTEge8/edit?usp=sharing"
)


class Product(BaseModel):
    """One row of the stock sheet."""

    item: str
    valor: int | None = None
    tamanho: str


async def main() -> None:
    """Read the sheet and print each product."""
    products: list[Product] = await read_google_sheet_as(SHEET_URL, Product)
    for product in products:
        print(product.item, product.valor, product.tamanho)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
